page_1.body_text: Use the Enterprise Wiki to create a single, go-to place for knowledge sharing and project management across the enterprise. Enterprise Wikis are simple to use, flexible, and lightweight in features. They are quick and easy to create, and you can easily add links to other information systems, corporate directories, or applications. By using an Enterprise Wiki, you can avoid email overload, provide structure to new and existing information, and encourage collaboration. This helps build consensus among team members. Working with content - text, graphics or video - is as easy as working in any word processing application, such as Microsoft Word. Use the Rich Text Editor to enhance the formatting of content, apply styles to text, reorganize or spell check your content, insert and format tables, and embed graphics or video. You can do all these things without leaving the wiki page. Other things you can do when working with Enterprise Wikis: Collaborate on wiki pages with other users Comment on a wiki page to enable discussion about the contents of the page Rate a wiki page to share your opinion about its content Categorize wiki pages to enable users to quickly find information and share it with others

Cornerstone Research expressly disclaims any implied warranty or representation about the information or accuracy, relevance, timeliness, completeness, or appropriateness for any particular purpose of any kind presented on CRIKIT. page_5.body_text: ​FAQ 1.  Copyright Restrictions 2.  How CRIKIT got it's name 3. Taxonomy 1.  Copyright Restrictions To comply with copyright restrictions, the following policies apply on CRIKIT: For Crikit Materials Any materials found on Crikit cannot be included verbatim into any work product. For Academic Literature In general all Academic papers should be added to the Academic Literature section of CRIKIT in the appropriate JEL category using the Academic Paper Template Please provide the link to the source - JSTOR, EBSCO (both available via Library Page on the Portal), SSRN, etc. Once the paper has been added under Academic Literature, you may link to that page from anywhere else in CRIKIT (for example, cite to it (see example)). In the rare instances where you feel the need to upload the paper directly to CRIKIT, please contact the IR  regarding the copyright policies for the paper in question. Please do not upload the paper unless you received an explicit permission from the IR. For Court Opinions If the Court opinion is obtained from the Court's website, you may upload it to CRIKIT directly.  Please provide the link the source (court's page) as appropriate. We cannot upload anything downloaded from Lexis or Westlaw. For Government Reports Please provide a link to the source directly (i.e. FCC page with the report in question) instead of uploading the report to CRIKIT. For additional information about Copyright, go here . 2.  How CRIKIT got it's name Background note: "wiki" in "Wikipedia" comes from "wiki wiki" which means "quick" in Hawaiian. An e-mail solicitation of possible names for Cornerstone Research (CR) knowledge management and sharing system among analysts and associates produced a list of suggestions.  A shortlist was offered to the members of Knowledge Sharing Task Force and by popular vote the name Crikit was chosen. "CRIKIT" comes from CR+WIKI+IT as in "Find it!" (and make it snappy - "wiki"). It is pronounced like "cricket." Thanks to Matt Lambert (formerly CRSF) for suggesting the winning entry. 3. page_10.body_text: Useful Websites Accounting and Taxation Antitrust Economic Data Energy, Oil, and Gas Financial Institutions Accounting and Taxation: Accounting Research Tutorial A step-by-step tutorial on how to thoroughly research accounting issues . AICPA library Service University of Mississippi Library- provides access to the AICPA library collection via its online library catalog and the Digital Accounting Collection. CPA Directory a director of CPAs for the USA. CPA net online community and complete resource for the accounting profession. Federal Accounting Standards Advisory Board FASAB promulgates federal accounting standards after considering the financial and budgetary information needs of citizens, congressional oversight groups, executive agencies, and the needs of other users of federal financial information. Federation of Tax Administrators State tax rates, including corporate, individual, sales, and excise tax data. FTA serves as a source of information and expertise for state administrators and others on the workings of state tax agencies and systems as well as issues generally affecting tax policy and administration. Financial Accounting Standards Board FASB a private, not-for-profit organization whose primary purpose is to develop generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) within the United States in the public's interest. Government of Accounting Standards Board GASB establishes and improves standards of state and local governmental accounting and financial reports. Information for Accountants from the Securities and Exchange Commission, includes Staff Accounting Bulletins. Internal Revenue Service Home page of the US IRS with tax forms, publications, statistics, and other tax information. International Accounting Standards Board develops a single set of high quality, understandable and international financial reporting standards (IFRSs) for general purpose financial statements. NBER TAXSIM project NBER TaxSim is a collection of programs and data sets that produce a micro simulation model of the U.S. federal and state income tax systems over many years. TaxSim includes a database of 80,000+ actual tax returns, a tax calculator that recreates each year's federal and state tax laws, and a table generator to report the statistics. TaxSim is widely used in academics to analyze tax issues. Public Company Accounting Oversight Board to oversee the auditors of public companies in order to protect the interests of investors and further the public interest in the preparation of informative, fair, and independent audit reports. Rutgers Accounting Research Center Collection of accounting resources, both articles and websites. Sarbanes-Oxley provides a complete cross-referenced index of SEC filers, audit firms, offices, CPAs, services, fees, compliance/enforcement actions and other critical disclosure information. Taxlinks All IRS revenue rulings since 1954. Taxsites an index of tax and accounting websites. Top of Page Antitrust: ABA Antitrust Law section This is the website of the Antitrust Section of the American Bar Association. Air Transport Association The site contains airline industry economics, statistics, and history Antitrust Legal Cases Browser Links to descriptions of antitrust legal cases and antitrust statutes. Antitrust professors Blog Auctions Auction history, types, and collusion . Business Valuation Update BVWire Archive BVWire™ brings you current, cutting-edge news on a weekly basis. From the buzz of the latest professional conferences to the best resources, guides, and data; from the impact of last week's tax case to this week's FASB, IRS, or other critical updates. European Commission Competition Cases The website of the European Commission Competition section.  Has access to all Competition Cases Federal Trade Commission The FTC's website has a section on Economic Issues and on Antitrust/Competition. FindLaw for Legal Professionals Antitrust trade and regulation section. Lots of links to information about antitrust law and cases. Database of antitrust experts. FTC Bureau of Competition Glossary of Antitrust Terms Provides definitions of many terms used in antitrust law and economics. Interstate Natural Gas Association of America Trade association that represents natural gas pipelines in the U.S., the inter-provincial pipelines in Canada, and PEMEX in Mexico. Includes searchable glossary, charts and graphs of pipeline network. Institute of Competition Law Loyola Institute for Consumer Antitrust Studies OECD Competition NERA Antitrust Insights Penn State Center for Study of Auctions, Procurement and Competition Profit Impact of Market Strategy (PIMS) database PIMS is a database of business profiles including financial data and information on competitive environments, customers, markets, and operating structures. UCB Competition Policy Center Top of Page Economic Data: Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) economic statistics . Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) This U.S. government site provides employment, unemployment, and other statistics relating to labor. Regional and local data by MSA also available. Historical data going back to "the beginning of time" available. Census Bureau U.S. government site provides historic time series data. Federal Deposit Insurance Corp. (FDIC) All of the data published in the FDIC publication Statistics on Banking: A Statistical History of the United States Banking Industry is available directly through the Internet via this site. The publication (as well as Web site) contains comprehensive information about U.S. savings and commercial banks, at a national and state level, from 1934-1996. Data includes bank failures, total assets of banks, and other aggregate statistics on banking. Federal Reserve Economic Database (FRED) Great source for interest rates going way back; includes daily, weekly, monthly and annual series for Monetary data, Interest rates (wide variety), GDP, CPI/PPI, Employment and population, and Exchange rates. Financial Data Finder A comprehensive source of links to a variety of types of financial data. Website is maintained by the Finance Department of the Fisher School of Business at Ohio State University. National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) Macroeconomics, Industry, Population data. Top of Page Energy, Oil, and Gas: California Board of Equalization This is California's Tax Division. The site includes various petroleum and sales data gathered from tax records. California Energy Commission Home page of the California State Energy Commission. Energy Central delivers enhanced news, data and information specific to the energy industry every business day. Energy Information Administration Official energy statistics including pricing and forecasts. Energy Intelligence EI offers newsletters, data and special reports and other publicaitons for the oil and gas industries . Environment & Energy Publishing (E&E) offers comprehensive daily coverage of environmental and energy policy and markets. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Government energy regulatory agency – lots of useful market data, industry snapshots, e-filings etc. Futures and Options Exchanges This page lists all futures and options exchanges. Interstate Natural Gas Association of America Trade association that represents natural gas pipelines in the U.S., the inter-provincial pipelines in Canada, and PEMEX in Mexico.  Includes searchable glossary, charts and graphs of pipeline network. ISDA (International Swaps and Derivatives Association, Inc.) the leading global trade association representing participants in the privately negotiated derivatives industry, a business which includes interest rate, currency, commodity and equity swaps as well as related products such as caps, collars, floors and swap options. Lundberg Survey Incorporated Has marketing data on retail gasoline sales. Natural Gas Supply Association Trade association of natural gas producers. Site includes white papers on energy issues, facts about natural gas supply and demand, links and other information on energy-related topics. NYMEX The New York Mercantile Exchange is a physical commodity futures exchange which includes pricing of such commodities as crude oil, gasoline, heating oil, natural gas, propane, gold, silver, platinum, palladium, and copper. Oxford Institute for Energy Studies The Oxford Institute for Energy Studies is a centre for advanced research into the social science areas of energy issues. The Institute conducts independent research on energy issues including financial markets, economics, and regulation. Studies are available through the Institute's books, papers, and journals. PennWell Publishing Company PennWell publishes more than 40 business-to-business publications, providing technical and business information, news and analysis to key executives and industry practitioners around the globe. Industries covered include oil, gas and electric power. Platt's (A McGraw-Hill Co.) "Platt's is the world's largest and most authoritative source of energy industry and information services". sci.geo.petroleum Very extensive but non-descriptive directory of petroleum related links. U.S. House Committee on Energy Subcommittee on Energy and Air Quality Provides links to Committee hearings and markups, news releases, and correspondence. US Department of Energy Energy Information Administration-Natural Gas Section Data on prices, production, demand, etc. Top of Page Financial Institutions: AAAdir Directory contains links to other Internet sites including a Directory of Banks, Credit Unions and Financial Information on the Internet. ADR.com This site created by JPMorgan is a great source for accessing news, earnings estimates, quotes, technical charts, and institutional ownership on American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) and international equities. You can search for ADRs by region, industry, and ticker or company name. Click on market overview to get data on the best and worst performing ADRs as well as top DRs by sector, ownership, and country. American Council of Life Insurers A life insurance association web site that includes a section for consumers. It provides detailed guides about the different types of life insurance. American Insurance Association Advocacy and educational material for learning about property and casualty insurance with links to policy reports and other key organizations. Assets and Liabilities of Commercial Banks in the United States [Federal Reserve Bank Release H.8] . Bank and Thrift Failure Reports Bank of New York Mellon Depository Receipts Directory Provides good background information on American Depository Receipts (ADR). You can view ADRs by industry, country, or region. Also, allows searching for DRs by institutional ownership and dividend paying issuers. Bank Rate Monitor Web's leading aggregator of financial rate information. Provides free rate information to consumers on more than 300 financial products, including mortgages, credit cards, new and used automobile loans, money market accounts, certificates of deposit, checking and ATM fees, home equity loans and online banking fees. BondsOnline Topics include: U.S. corporate bonds, US Municipal bonds, U.S. Treasury and Federal Agency securities, bond funds, convertible bonds. It also gives information about portfolio strategy, hedging, swap mechanics, and analytic software. Credit Union National Association (CUNA) The Credit Union National Association (CUNA) is the premier national trade association serving credit unions. 90% of America's credit unions are affiliated with CUNA. Dynamic Maps of Nonprime Mortgage Conditions in the United States Economic Census. Geographic Area Series: Finance and Insurance FDIC The site contains comprehensive information about US savings and commercial banks, both at the state and federal levels. FDIC Call Reports and TFRs HTML-formatted version of quarterly financial reports which federally-insured banks must submit to the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) or other federal regulatory agencies. Includes Consolidated Reports of Condition and Income for commercial banks, as well as Thrift Financial Reports for savings banks and related thrift institutions. FDIC Bank Data and Statistics Use searchable databases to find information on specific banks, their branches, and the industry. FDIC Failed Banks Learn how accounts and loans are affected when a bank fails, how to seek unclaimed funds, and how to obtain a lien release. FDIC Financial Institutions Directory FDIC Research & Analysis Access FDIC policy research and analysis of regional and national banking trends. FDIC Summary of Deposits FDIC Statistics On Banking: Historical . Federal Financial Institutions Examination Council (FFIEC) The Council is a formal interagency body empowered to prescribe uniform principles, standards, and report forms for the federal examination of financial institutions by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (FRB), the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA), the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), and the Office of Thrift Supervision (OTS) and to make recommendations to promote uniformity in the supervision of financial institutions. Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago- Commercial Bank and Holding Company Database Website provides access to various data files, merger information, and documentation for Commercial Banks and Bank Holding Companies including free bank Call Reports and bank holding company Y-9s. FRED (Federal Reserve Economic Data) at St. Louis Federal Reserve A database of over 3000 U.S economic time series. HealthDecisions.org Provides news, a learning center and events directory, and portals for many kinds of health insurance. Sponsored by America's Health Insurance Plans (AHIP), an association of 1,300 American companies providing health insurance to more than 200 million Americans. HUD (U.S. Dept of Housing and Urban Development.) The Office of Housing provides vital public services through its nationally administered programs.  It oversees the Federal Housing Administration (FHA), the largest mortgage insurer in the world. Independent Insurance Agents & Brokers of America Links to consumer information, state associations, and current issues in education and government affairs, and directory information Institutional Investor Publishes rankings of investment banking analysts. Provides an Analyst Database.  This database of sell-side equity research analysts includes all of II's ranked analysts since 1998, worldwide. Publishes the Reuters Institutional Investor Equities Investment Survey. These surveys include rankings of the sales and trading divisions of investment banks. Insurance Analyst PRO is the financial sector's premier online resource for insurance industry data retrieval and analysis. With NAIC Annual Statement data back to 1995 and Quarterly Statement data dating back to 2002 for the Property & Casualty ; Life, Accident & Health ; and Health filing types, Insurance Analyst PRO is one of the most comprehensive insurance data resources. Insurance Information Institute An excellent source of factual information and basic industry data about the industry. Covers auto, home, business, life, disabilities, disasters, statistics, industry financials, hot topics, media, and more. Insurance Institute for Highway Safety/Highway Loss Data Institute The IIHS and HLDI are responsible for studying highway safety in the hope of reducing auto related accidents, fatalities, and damage to property. Its research often has important industry and public policy implications. The IIHS web site provides studies, news, and other highway safety information. Library of Congress: Banking statistics Monthly Statement of the Pubic Debt of the United States Monthly data for treasury bills, notes, and other federal securities. Tables include a description of the security, issue date, amount, and date of final maturity. For more data related to federal bills, notes, and bonds visit the Bureau of the Public Debt. Mutual Fund Investor's Center Use the Snap Charts feature to draw charts for periods of 1 day to all available dates going back to 50 years. NAIC (Insurance) The Official web site of The National Association of Insurance Commissioners. Contains a description of the type of data available from the NAIC, the purpose of the NAIC, and other useful information. Also contains links to state insurance regulators. National Association of Federal Credit Unions NAFCU, one of the largest credit union trade associations, provides its members with representation, information, education, and assistance to meet the challenges that cooperative financial institutions face in today's economic environment. The association stands as a national forum for the federal credit union community where new ideas, issues, concerns and trends can be identified, discussed, resolved. National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) NAIC represents U.S. insurance regulators from the 50 states, the District of Columbia and the four U.S. territories. ​ Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) What resources do I have from my desktop? How do I submit a request to Information Resources? What books and magazines does CR own? How do I check out a book? And where do I return books once I’m finished with them? So Nelson’s. . . What do those stars mean? What sources are included in Factiva? What sources are included in Major Business Pubs (This is a Cornerstone-created group of publications on Factiva)? What sources are typically included in Promo searches on Factiva? Are all local newspapers covered in Factiva? Can Factiva search foreign languages? What’s up with those Factiva timestamps? What types of articles can I exclude from Factiva? Can I exclude republished news, daily market data, obituaries, and other recurring articles? Can I get a time stamp for analyst reports from Eikon? What analyst report contributors are not available through our resources? Do SEC filings have time stamps? How do I get a password for …? How do I get TAQ data after June 2007? What is included in the research IR performs to locate Daubert/adverse motions and orders? What are some Beta sources we use? Are all company SIC codes the same? How do Thomson SDC industry codes relate to the NAIC and SIC codes? What is the coverage of online newspapers in our databases? When was this news publically available? When do I need to purchase copyright permissions? Why does IR warn against purchasing ebooks? What does * (an asterisk) in the headline of an article retrieved from Factiva mean? How do I produce a link? What resources do I have from my desktop? The CR Information Resources staff purchases access to statistics and articles. They are linked from the Wiki page Cornerstone Access to Databases . There is no fee or charge back to use these resources except Capital IQ and Science Direct. See Information Resources Pricing . Once you identify the resource you want to use, the following search guides will help you to focus your search. EBSCO HeinOnline HeinOnline Advanced Capital IQ Science Direct How do I submit a request to Information Resources? You can submit a request to IR using #Information Resources in Outlook. Be sure to include: A detailed description of what you want The case name and matter A link to the LAN folder to place the results The deadline by which you need it (please state a date/time rather than ASAP) TOP OF PAGE What books and magazines does CR own? The IR has a collection of books.  Search the library catalog from the link on the portal. The book you need can be sent to you via interoffice mail from any office at no charge. The IR staff can usually borrow books from some academic libraries.  The process takes 2 to 7 days and costs about $30. TOP OF PAGE How do I check out a book? To check out a book please email #Information Resources with the Title and Author of the book. There is no limit on how long you may keep the book at your desk.  Be sure to return it to the shelf so someone else can also use it. Once you return the book please email #Information Resorces so we can update the catalog. If you are in a different office, contact Information Resources and someone will arrange for the book to be sent to you via interoffice mail. TOP OF PAGE And where do I return books once I’m finished with them? Once you return the book please email #Information Resorces so we can update the catalog. Each office of CR is color-coded.  On the spine of the textbook, you will find the Library label with a colored sticker: Green :        San Francisco Gray :            Menlo Park Blue :            Boston Yellow :        Washington, DC Red :            New York Purple :        Los Angeles Pink :            Chicago And when in doubt, please send the book to Information Resources in Los Angeles. TOP OF PAGE So Nelson’s. . . What do those stars mean? Nelson Information's Directory of Investment Research publishes an annual list of analysts who write investment reports on specific companies.  The Cornerstone collection begins in 1998 and is kept in the San Francisco office.  As of the 2006 edition, Nelson Information's Directory of Investment Research does not include stars for any analysts listed.  2008 is the latest year for which this directory was published. The cover page of the 2001 edition and earlier of Nelson Information's Directory of Investment Research said “The star after analyst’s name indicates membership on consensus all-star research teams of Institutional Investor and Nelson Research.” The cover page of the 2002–2005 editions of Nelson Information’s Directory of Investment Research states, “The star after analyst's name indicates membership on consensus all-star research teams of Institutional Investor and Extel.” There are two sources listed: Institutional Investor (from their website) – The Institutional Investor Research Group (“IIRG”) develops detailed analyses of Institutional Investor magazine's published research team rankings covering the U.S., Europe, Asia, and Latin America, in separate lists. Extel (a Thomson product) – The Extel Survey is regarded as the leading benchmark for the assessment of the investment community worldwide by the investment community worldwide.  It provides weighted rankings on sell-side analysts, fund managers, and corporate IR practitioners. Sources for annual analyst rankings : Institutional Investor – Published each October and available in full text here . Wall Street Journal – Published in May and available through Factiva, see sample (May 2013 is the last ranking). Starmine – Published in Financial Times and in this spreadsheet . NOTE:  As of 2009, Nelson Information's Directory of Investment Research will no longer be published.  This resource has been our prime source to identify which analysts follow a particular company. An alternative option to Nelson's is to use a list of analyst report citations from Eikon or CapIQ.  You can request this from the IR for a specific company and date range.  Sort the data on the spreadsheet by contributor, then date.  You will see the list of analysts associated with each investment bank for each year. TOP OF PAGE What sources are included in Factiva? Factiva has more than 20,000 publications available in full text in 28 languages. A search in Factiva All will search all publications in English. A search can include several foreign languages.  The list of all Factiva publications (any language) is for internal use only! TOP OF PAGE What sources are included in Major Business Pubs (This is a Cornerstone-created group of publications on Factiva)? TOP OF PAGE Are all company SIC codes the same? If you are trying to create a list of companies with the same SIC code, this could be tricky. When a company files reports with the SEC, the company is assigned a SIC code.  It is not common for a company to change the code, because the SEC has to agree to it and it is a long process, but it can happen.  If you look in the header of the filing you will see the SEC assigned SIC code. Most SEC filing forms do not require (or have a space for) primary SIC code.  However, certain registration statements do (such as S-1 and SB-1 and SB-2).  Companies self-designate on their registration statement what they believe their primary SIC code to be.  Based on the first digit of this code, the SEC sends the filing to a particular group to review.  That group will then look at the company's business description, etc. and decide what the SIC code should be based on the company's primary role .  It may be different than what the company says.  The SEC does not appear to require any changes to the form submitted in the event that the SEC feels the code should be something else. Thus, what you see on the registration statement is what the company classified itself to be.  However, the SEC does track SIC codes in its system, and records the code that the SEC believes is correct.  This SEC-designated SIC code is then supplied to Edgar, and is the source of the header information that accompanies every electronic filing stored on Edgar for a company.  If a company wishes to change it’s SIC code as listed in the SEC system and Edgar header file, it must go through a formal review process, fill out forms, etc. with the SEC.  Most information companies such as D&B, GIS, etc. pull their SIC code information from Edgar, but.... Refinitiv Eikon .  Eikon does “value added” services, and reviews things like SIC code themselves.  When they receive a filing for a company, they look at the company's business description and decide on the appropriate SIC code based on which role produces the most revenue for the company.  Sometimes this may differ from the SEC, because it may not be the company's primary role. Capital IQ ’s assigned primary industry for most public and some private companies comes from Standard & Poor's, specifically their GICS product. GICS has a very rigorous process through which they assign and update a GIC (Global Industry Classification) – they look at revenues derived from a business as well as a qualitative review of the companies business, so it's not just a quantitative assignment.  For example, PepsiCo derives most of its revenues from it's bottling business, but S&P has decided that based on the company's actual product line, it should be a soft drink company.  All assignments are passed through a committee that consists of S&P and MSCI staff.  They review/update GICs one or two times a year.  So. . . The S&P indexing team never looks to see what SIC code any company has assigned to itself.  (Usually done with SEC filings.)  They assign each company in the database a GICS code then map the GICS code to the SIC code they believe is most appropriate. follow, but flashes are intended to get important news out to newswires users
as quickly as possible

​ Book Recommendations Favorite
  Book of All Time Current/Recent Book to Recommend Recommended By Notes A Wrinkle in
  Time (L'Engle) Phlip K Dick Short Stories (any collection) Laura Londa 1. My favorite book of all time is A Wrinkle in
  Time by Madeleine L’Engle. I think I
  first read it in 4th or 5th grade and loved it ever since. Whenever if get
  down or burned out, I read it again (and listen to Quadrophenia by The Who),
  and I perk up again. 2. I’m currently reading a collection of short stories by Philip K. Dick
  (sci fi writer). If you didn’t already
  know, many movies have been based on his short stories. His stories are often
  thought-provoking. And since they are
  short, they are easy to read in between other things or whatever. To name a few of the movies that are based
  on his short stories: a. Blade Runner b. Paycheck c. The Adjustment Bureau d. Total Recall e. Minority Report f. Next g. A Scanner Darkly The
  Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay (Chabon) Heather Winningham The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier &
  Clay by Michael Chabon. It’s rich in history, adventure, and romance. I fell
  in love with the characters and enjoyed taking this exuberant rollercoaster
  ride with Sammy, Joe, and Rosa. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Amazing_Adventures_of_Kavalier_%26_Clay A Tree Grows in
  Brooklyn (Smith) Magazines that have piled up on coffee table Susan Davis Favorite book of all time: A Tree Grows in Brooklyn by Betty
  Smith Read recently that I would recommend: All the magazines that have piled up
  on my coffee table that I never had time to read until now. A
  House for Mr. Biswas (Naipaul) The Emperor of Maladies: A Biography of
  Cancer (Murkherjee) The Gene: An Intimate History (Murkherjee) Rahul Guha Favorite book of all time: A House for
  Mr. Biswas, by V.S. Naipaul Recent (not so recent, but still amazing): The Emperor of all Maladies: A
  Biography of Cancer, and The Gene: an Intimate History, both by Siddhartha
  Mukherjee. Probably best pieces of non-fiction I’ve ever read – highly
  recommended! A Prayer for Owen
  Meany (Irving) Hitchhikers' Guide to the Galaxy (Adams) Becoming (Obama) Heather Gamberg Favorite book of all time: I can’t name just one. “A Prayer for
  Owen Meany” by John Irving is one of my faves and so it “Hitchhikers’ Guide
  to the Galaxy” by Douglas Adams Reading now or recently: Just finished Michelle Obama’s “Becoming” (read
  the Kindle version and listened to the audio book) and highly recommend
  it. P.S. “The Emperor of All Maladies” is a great book. One
  Hundred Years if Solitude (Marquez) Infinite Jest (Wallace) 10Q84 (Murakami) The Overstory (Powers) Jonathan Patrick Not capable of picking one …. One Hundred Years of Solitude – Gabriel Garcia Marquez Infinite Jest – David Foster Wallace More recent: 10Q84 - Haruki Murakami The Overstory – Richard Powers The Seven Storey Mountain
  (Merton) Peace
  Like a River (Enger) Marilyn
  Skillings Favorite
  book of all time: The Seven Storey Mountain by Thomas Merton (his
  autobiography) Great book recently: Peace Like a River by Leif Enger (fiction) Between
  the World and Me (Coates) Katie Papp My favorite book that I’ve read recently
  is “Between the World and Me” by Ta-Nehisi Coates The Amazing Adventures of
  Kavalier & Clay (Chabon) Middlesex (Eugenides) Because
  of Mr. Terupt (Buyea) Moon Over Manifest (Vanderpool) Where the Mountain Meets the Moon (Lin) Celeste
  Saravia Favorites
  of all time: I don’t have one. A couple of my favorite books are (1) The
  Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay and (2) Middlesex. Reading Now or Recently: Most of my current/recent reads are with my kids
  (1) currently reading “Because of Mr. Terrupt” and recently finished (2)
  “Moon over Manifest,” both are very good. Also, in the kid genre and very good is “Where the Mountain Meet the
  Moon.” I haven’t read “The Emperor of All Maladies” but I’ll put in a plug for The
  Interpreter of the Maladies, which was great. Jonathan
  Strange and Mr. Norrell (Clarke) The City in the Middle of the Night
  (Anders) The Famished Road (Okri) Nora Sawyer 1. I have trouble naming a favorite book
  (I have so many favorites!), but right now my comfort read is Jonathan
  Strange and Mr. Norrell, by Susanna Clarke. I first read the book when it
  came out in 2004 --- an excerpt was published in (I think) the New York Times
  Review of Books, and I was so excited that I ran out and bought it the night
  before it was officially released (thanks to a Modern Times bookstore
  employee who was putting it out on display just as the store was about to
  close, allowing me to rush in and buy it before anyone stopped me). If you’re not familiar with it (or the miniseries put out on Netflix), it’s
  a novel set in Regency England, in a world where magic used to be real, but
  has fallen out of practice. Gentleman scholars still study theoretical magic,
  but real magic is considered gauche and mostly fake, something practiced by
  charlatans and street magicians. Of course, there wouldn’t be much of a novel if this didn’t change. So
  pretty much at the start of the book, we discover one “practical magician” in
  England (Mr. Norrell), who’s soon joined by another (Jonathan Strange). The
  story unfolds as one part a well-observed, Jane Austen-like comic novel set
  in 19th century British society, part historical treatise on magic and
  folklore, and one part haunting fairy-tale. I feel like I’m not describing it
  well, but you can try a taste of it at the link below. And if you do read it,
  don’t skip the footnotes. They’re amazing. https://www.bookbrowse.com/excerpts/index.cfm/book_number/1463/jonathan-strange-mr-norrell 2. The past few weekends, I’ve spent a lot of time bingeing on books I’d
  normally be read in small bites during my ferry rides to and from work. Here
  are two stand-outs: The City in the Middle of the Night by Charlie Jane Anders. This is science
  fiction, set on a far-off earth colony on a planet called January, long after
  the first generation of humans landed. The planet is tidally locked, like our
  moon, so all of the human colonists live in two cities set in the narrow band
  of twilight between the meltingly-bright day and the eternally-dark and
  freezing night. The story, which follows the intertwining stories of a few
  characters, begins as Sophie, a poor student, is exiled into the night, makes
  contact with the creatures that live there, and returns to her city in
  hiding, on the run from the law. It’s a really good story, and one that
  grapples with big ideas without ever seeming overly philosophical. (For a
  taste of Charlie Jane Anders’ writing, I also recommend her short story As
  Good as New). The Famished Road, by Ben Okri. This is sort of a animist/magical realist
  novel. It follows Azaro, a “spirit child,” who retains the ability to see the
  spirit world (something most of us forget when we are born). He lives with
  his mother and father in an un-named city, and throughout the book, the
  spirit and mortal worlds unfold around him, creating a sort of absurdist and
  beautiful picture of life and family and community (and like City in the
  Middle of the Night, this book follows a character who moves past the
  boundaries of Anthropocene-era built-cities into a more-than-just-human
  perspective of the world). It’s a really difficult book to describe, but one
  I really loved reading. Also, when I googled it just now for inspiration on
  how to describe it better, I found out that Radiohead’s Street Spirit (Fade
  Out) was inspired by the book. So there’s that. Hyperion (Simmons) Red Notice (Browder) Patient
  H.M. (Dittrich) Modern Romance (Ansari) Brian
  Dito Hmm,
  I am not much into science fiction but just finished the 4 book series by Dan
  Simmons called Hyperion which was really good! Would say it’s one of my most
  favorite series I have read. A non fiction book on finance crimes and consolidation of power in Russia
  pre and post USSR was Red Notice written by Bill Browder, pretty exciting and
  eye opening. Another non fiction I would recommend is Patient H.M by Luke Dittrich, goes
  through the history of neurology and mental illnesses. I will warn people
  that it can get pretty graphic with the brain surgery stuff. One book I thought was cool and quite different from what I usually read
  was written by the comedian Aziz Ansari called Modern Romance. Talks about
  the history of dating and where social media and brought it today. Was
  co-authored by a buddy of his. There’s like 30 or so others I have read recently but those are the more
  memorable ones. Lincoln
  in the Bardo (Saunders) The Girl Who Drank the Moon (Barnhill) Tina Green Favorites of all time: I have different favorite books for
  different periods of my life. My
  favorite book from the past ~5 years is Lincoln in the Bardo by George
  Saunders. Reading Now: The Girl Who Drank the
  Moon, by Kelly Barnhill (children’s book, that my 9-YO and I are reading
  together). Men Explain Things to Me
  (Solnit) Charlotte
  Witherspoon Men
  Explain Things to Me (original essay reprinted here) What? It’s Equal Pay Day! The
  Good Earth (Buck) Things Fall Apart (Achebe) The Water Dancer (Coates) Kory Kantenga Favorite book(s) of all time: The Good Earth by Pearl Buck Things Fall Apart by Chinua Achebe Reading now: The Water Dancer by Ta-Nehisi Coates Lord of the Light (Zelazny) The
  Name of the Wind (Rothfuss) The Wise Man's Fear (Rothfuss) Bob
  Majure Revealing
  my Sci-Fi side here... Favorite of all time: Roger Zelazny's "Lord of Light" is a roller
  coaster ride of metaphysics and embodies everything science fiction can be.
  Don't hate it for the inexcusably bad (i.e., perfect) pun. Recent: I returned to Patrick Rothfuss's masterpiece of incompletion: the
  two-book trilogy "The Name of the Wind" and "The Wise Man's
  Fear." Warning: Do NOT start this series if you need a perfectly told
  story to have an end... Ever. Think
  and Grow Rich (Hill) You Were Born Rich (Proctor) Killing Cancer Not People (Wright) Becoming (Obama) You're Not Sick, You're Thirsty. Don't Treat Thirst with Medication
  (Batmanghelidj) Ngoc Tai Two favorite books: 1. Think and Grow Rich – Napoleon Hill 2. You Were Born Rich – Bob Proctor Most recent books: 1. Killing Cancer Not People – Robert G. Wright 2. Becoming – Michelle Obama 3. You’re Not Sick, You’re Thirsty. Don’t Treat Thirst with Medication – F.
  Batmanghelidj. M.D. (current reading) War and Peace (Tolstoy) Midnight's Children (Rushdie) One Hundred Years of Solitude (Marquez The Sound and the Fury (Faulkner) Middlemarch (Eliot) My
  Name is Red (Pamuk) The Museum of Innocence (Pamuk) A Strangeness in My Mind (Pamuk) Maj Sjowall/Per Wahloo mysteries Marseilles Trilogy (Izzo) Yesim
  Richardson I
  can’t pick a favorite book but here are some classics that have stayed with
  me: War and Peace by Leo Tolstoy,
  Midnight’s Children by Salman Rushdie, One Hundred Years of Solitude by
  Gabriel Garcia Marquez, The Sound and the Fury by William Faulkner,
  Middlemarch by George Eliot. Also, my favorite Orhan Pamuk novels: My Name is Red, The Museum of Innocence, and A Strangeness in My
  Mind I love mystery and recently discovered the Maj Sjowall/Per Wahloo books
  from the 1960s and 70s. They’re
  great. Also the Marseilles Trilogy by
  Jean-Claude Izzo. Gratitude (Sacks) Katy Matusich I too can’t pick a favorite, but am
  currently reading Gratitude by Oliver Sacks. Lolita (Nabokov) Ada or Ardor (Nabokov) All the Pretty Horses (McCarthy) Middlemarch (Eliot) Anna Karenina (Tolstoy) All of Jane Austen All of Edith Wharton Transit
  of Venus (Hazzard) All of Aleksandar Hemon All of Julie Otsuka Elisa
  Oliveri Favorite:
  tie between Lolita and Ada, or Ardor by Nabokov Runners up: All the Pretty Horses (Cormac McCarthy), Middlemarch (Eliot),
  Anna Karenina (Tolstoy), and all of Jane Austen and Edith Wharton Best recent read: Transit of Venus by Shirley Hazzard (Holy cow, was it
  good!) And then a plug for my favorite writers writing now, Aleksandar Hemon and
  Julie Otsuka. Go read them!! The
  Snow Leopard (Matthiesesen) From Heaven Lake (Seth) Team of Rivals (Goodwin) Mike Topper So many great books already mentioned,
  many of which I have enjoyed immensely. And as others have said, impossible
  to pick a favorite. Two books that I read as a young man that set me on a path, that through
  various twists, turns, backtracks and meanders I am still following
  today: The Snow Leopard (Peter Matthiesesen) From Heaven Lake (Vikram Seth) More recently, I have been slowly making my way through U.S. Presidential
  biographies, of which a favorite is: Team of Rivals (Doris Kearns Goodwin) Cosmicomics (Calvino) Life
  and Death on the New York Dance Floor, 1980-1983 (Lawrence) Fiebre Tropical (Lopera) Tim
  Strong Just
  finished and quite enjoyed: Life and Death on the New York Dance Floor,
  1980–1983 by Tim Lawrence All-time favorite: Cosmicomics by Italo Calvino Just started: Fiebre Tropical by Juliana Delgado Lopera Le
  Petit Prince (Exupéry) Manual de Iinquisidores (Antunes) Body and Soul (Conroy) Jos é Alberro All-time favorite: Le Petit Prince, Saint
  Exupéry Currently devouring : Manual de Inquisidores, Antonio Lobo Antunes Had to reread even though it is corny (I am actually a frustrated pianist
  that did not do to the Vienna Conservatory) : Body and Soul Frank Conroy The Bothers Karamazov
  (Dostoevsky) Crime and Punishment (Dostoevsky) The Plague (Camus) Justice: What's the Right Thing to Do? (Sandel) Eric
  Tam I
  used to read a lot of fiction and was a fan of Fyodor Dostoevsky. I thought his best book was The Brothers
  Karamazov, but his Crime and Punishment had the best plot. I will also plug The Plague by Albert
  Camus, which seems relevant to our times. On the non-fiction side, I recommend Justice: What’s the Right Thing To Do? by Michael
  Sandel. It is a highly readable
  overview of different conceptions of justice as argued by different
  philosophers over time and how they may apply to contemporary issues. The book is thoughtful, engaging, and
  non-technical. The
  Trial (Kafka) Macunaima (Andrade) One Hundred Years of Solitude (Marquez) The Foundation (Asimov) Renato Giroldo Favorites: The trial (Kafka), Macunaima
  (Andrade), One hundred years of solitude (Marquez) Currently: The foundation (Asimov) The Xanth Series (Anthony) The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant (Donaldson) A People's History of the United States 1492-Present (Zimmerman) Start with No (Camp) Way of the Peaceful Warrior (Millman) Kushner
  Inc. (Ward) Alex
  Levin Most
  fun books The Xanth Series by Piers Anthony – The play on words and puns is very
  imaginative and creative. The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant by Stephen R. Donaldson – Another fun
  Science Fiction series Most Influential A People’s history of the United States 1492 – Present by Howard Zimmerman
  – For me, very much an eye opener to the history of the U.S. Start with No by Jim Camp – Great book into the psychology of negotiating Way of the Peaceful Warrior by Dan Millman – changed my perspective of
  living life forever. Reading now Kushner Inc. – By Vicky Ward – A good look at the Kushner Family origins
  from first generation to present day. A
  Fan's Notes (Exley) I Am Pilgrim (Hayes) The Lock Artist (Hamilton) Washington Black (Edugyan) Darwin Neher I agree with those who say that different
  books make impacts at different parts of life. A book that spoke to me as an “angry young man,” was A Fan’s Notes by
  Frederick Exley. Recent-ish great books in the thriller vein would be I Am Pilgrim by Terry
  Hayes, and The Lock Artist by Steve Hamilton. Best recent literary book would be Washington Black by Esi Edugyan. Angle of Repose (Stegner) Crossing to Safety (Stegner) LBJ:Passage to Power (Caro) Lab Girl (Jahren) This is Where I Leave You (Tropper) The Sellout (Beatty) Boomsday (Buckley) Joe
  Schertler So
  many great books in this thread, but without repeating prior ones some
  favorites of mine from the last few years: Fiction: Wallace Stegner – Angle of Repose or Crossing to Safety Elizabeth Strout – Olive Kitteridge or Olive Again Nonfiction/Biography: Robert Caro - LBJ: Passage to Power (4th book in Caro’s biography of LBJ;
  Caro’s presumably currently writing the 5th and final book) Hope Jahren – Lab Girl Satire / humor: Jonathon Tropper - This is Where I Leave You Paul Beatty – The Sellout Chris Buckley - Boomsday They
  Can't Kill Us Until They Kill Us (Abdurraqib) Trick Mirror (Tolentino) Juliana Tu The number one book/personal essay
  collection I’ve recommended to all of my friends and to some other CRCH
  analysts: They Can’t Kill Us Until They Kill Us by Hanif Abdurraqib 1. Everybody I know that has read this book to has loved it AND gone back
  to reread it. 2. To get an idea of Hanif’s writing style see his free to read online
  pieces a. here (Carly Rae Jepson and the Kingdom of Desire) b. here (Macklemore’s “White Privilege II” Didn’t Move Me, But That’s Not
  The Point) 3. Themes: race, music, identity Another great personal essay collection, that I read per CRCH analyst
  Francesca Jarrett’s rec and loved: Trick Mirror by Jia Tolentino 1. Free to read online writing by Jia a. here (Athleisure Time) b. here (The Important, Inappropriate Literary Man) 2. Themes: internet, identity, feminism All the Light We Cannot See
  (Doerr) The
  Jersey Brothers (Freeman) Mary
  Woodford Two
  to add to the pile: All the Light We Cannot See, by Anthony Doerr – fiction. Non-fiction: The Jersey Brothers, by Sally Mott Freeman. Both happen to be set in the World War II time frame, but not limited to
  that in terms of their themes and stories. A Little Life (Yanagihara) White on Black (Gal'ego) Zuleikha (Yakhina) All the Light We Cannot See (Doerr) The Goldfinch (Tart) Leonardo's Handwriting (Rubina) Ksenia Fiorin Best books read in the last couple of
  years: 1. A Little Life by Hanya Yanagihara 2. White on Black by Ruben David Gonsales Galʹego 3. Zuleikha by Guzel Yakhina 4. All the Light We Cannot See by Anthony Doerr 5. The Goldfinch by Donna Tart 6. Leonardo’s Handwriting by Dina Rubina A Gentleman in Moscow (Towles) Interpreter
  of Maladies (Lahiri) Laura
  Stiglin A
  Gentleman in Moscow by Amor Towles – historical fiction about an aristocrat
  trapped in a Moscow hotel in the 1930s … beautifully written, clever and fun
  with a little bit of everything - intrigue, romance, wonderful character development Interpreter of Maladies by Jhumpa Lahiri – an exquisite collection of short
  stories that won the Pulitzer Prize for fiction Norwegian
  Wood (Murakami) After the Quake (Murakami) Our Man in Havana (Greene) James Bond series (Fleming) Quantitative Techniques for Competition
  and Antitrust (Davis) Kivanc Kirgiz I second the Murakami recommendation.
  Norwegian Wood and After the Quake are good ones to get started. Graham Greene is another good one. I will probably go back and reread Our
  Man in Havana’s chapter where two spies play checkers with miniature bottles
  of whiskey and whoever loses a piece have to drink it. That was the trust
  serum back in the day… Ian Flemming’s James Bond series cannot be missed for light reading. I
  finished On Her Majesty’s Secret Service last month. I just started a new book: Quantitative Techniques for Competition and
  Antitrust Analysis by this bloke Peter Davis. Riveting stuff. All in Red (Chmielewska) Collection of poems by Brodsky The
  Undoing Project (Lewis) The Remains of the Day (Ishiguro) Zoya
  Marriott A
  book I liked recently was “The Undoing Project” by Michael Lewis, about
  Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky. And
  “The Remains of the Day” by Kazuo Ishiguro. My go-to “pick me up” book since college has been “All in Red” (“Wszystko
  czerwone”) by Joanna Chmielewska, though I am not sure whether it has been
  translated into English. And my favorite book is probably a collection of poems by Joseph Brodsky The
  Cemetary of Forgotten Books series (Zafon) All Creatures Great and Small (Herriot) Andrea Goodman Favorite: a series of books by Carlos
  Ruis Zafon, The Cemetary of Forgotton Books. There are 4 books, Shadow of the Wind, The Angel’s Game, The Prisoner
  of Heaven, and The Labyrinth of the Spirits. They take place in Madrid and other parts of Spain during and after
  the Franco era. Zafon’s writing is
  incredibly beautiful. Currently: I’m revisiting a series I read about 30 years ago starting with
  All Creatures Great and Small by James Herriot about a veterinarian in
  Yorkshire. I’ve never seen the PBS
  series, but devoured all the books. I’m finding this a relief to disappear into that far-off place with
  all that’s currently going on. I’ve
  heard they are remaking the series. The Powerbroker (Caro) Middlemarch (Eliot) God in Ruins (Atkinson) Homegoing (Gyasi) Station Eleven (Mandel) Saints for All Occasions (Sullivan) The Dublin Murder Squad mysteries (French) The Kingsbridge Series (Follett) The Baroque Cycle (Stephenson) Tess
  of d'Ubervilles (Hardy) When Time Stopped (Neumann) Normal People (Rooney) Kate
  Maxwell Koegel As
  someone who worked in an independent bookstore for 6 years, this thread has
  brought me much joy. Books I have really loved: • The Powerbroker by Robert Caro Long but a vital read for anyone who has, well, ever been in an American
  city • Middlemarch by George Eliot Delightful on audio—the humor in some of the absurdity is more
  apparent • God in Ruins by Kate Atkinson Companion to the wonderful Life after Life, which should be the first read.
  She also has enjoyable mysteries • Homegoing by Yaa Gyasi Nothing impressed upon me the intergenerational sin of slavery more than
  this book • Station Eleven by Emily St. John Mandel This is about pandemic, beware. However, it has stayed with me for years
  and I return to thinking about it often • Saints for All Occasions by J. Courtney Sullivan A must read for members of slightly dysfunctional Irish Catholic
  families Currently reading: • Tess of d’Urbervilles by Thomas Hardy Especially interesting in the light of #metoo • When Time Stopped by Ariana Neumann A memoir that reads like fiction at points • Normal People by Sally Rooney I am avoiding finishing it because then it would be over Series that will take lots of time and are worth it: • The Dublin Murder Squad mysteries by Tana French Smart mysteries which share characters but avoid sameness • The Kingsbridge Series by Ken Follett Chief merits are length, history, and rich heroes and villains, if a little
  lacking in nuance • The Baroque Cycle by Neal Stephenson Intermixing of history (especially economic history), technology, and some
  mysticism I,
  Claudius (Graves) The Odyssey (trans. Wilson) A Revolutionary Life (Xiaoping) Andrew Follett Favorite: I, Claudius by Robert Graves. Tiger King-sized personalities meets Game of Thrones-sized palace
  intrigue. Currently reading that I would recommend: • Emily Wilson’s new translation of The Odyssey. It really does live up to the hype. • Deng Xiaoping: A Revolutionary Life. I am only ~10% the way through this one,
  but so far it is informative and reasonably paced. Noisy Dinosaurs (Litton) Clever Creatures and Boundless Beasts: A Land of Dinosaurs
  (Carpenter) Wild About Books (Sierra) David
  Russo I’ve
  been enjoying lots of reading these days. There are a few books that I turn
  to every day, usually multiple (5+) times a day. Noisy Dinosaurs is a clear favorite. Unlike most of the books that others
  have recommended, it makes dinosaur noises at you. Dostoevsky and Eliot have
  nothing on that. Another classic of the genre is Clever Creatures and
  Boundless Beasts: A Land of Dinosaurs. And that’s just a start – if anyone
  wants to dig deeper, let me know. Wild About Books is another favorite. (It’s actually pretty clever.) And
  the character development in the Pout-Pout Fish series will warm your
  hearts. (I’m really just envious and would love to be reading actual grown-up
  books.) The
  Road (McCarthy) The Idiot (Bautman) Meditations (Aurelius) Joshua Byrne My favorite depends on the day, but I’ll
  go with The Road by Cormack McCarthy. It is quite the morbid affair, but it
  is also the most powerful story of human connection I’ve ever read. Currently, I’m reading: • The Idiot by Elif Bautman: A story of a Turkish immigrant who comes to
  school in the United States and slowly realizes that she is doomed to write
  fiction for the rest of her life. One of the funniest books I’ve ever
  read. • Meditations by Marcus Aurelius: Philosophical passages about the power of
  stoicism and purpose. I’ve found it nice to start the day to, especially
  considering what is going on in the world. Neapolitan Novels series
  (Ferrante) The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle (Murakami) The Power and the Glory (Greene) Patrick
  Melrose series (St. Aubyn) Laurien
  Gilbert My
  favorite: Neapolitan Novels series by Elena Ferrante. The books follow the lives of two childhood
  best friends growing up in a lower-income neighborhood in post-war
  Naples. I shared the books with my own
  best friend, which made it a particularly memorable reading experience. Since there are Murakami and Graham Greene fans in this thread, I have to
  give a shout-out to The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle and The Power and the Glory as
  well. Currently reading: • Patrick Melrose series by Edward St. Aubyn (also made into a recent
  miniseries): Very funny but fairly
  dark story about a man trying to break free from the influences of his family
  to create his own identity, with a unexpected section that’s all about
  bashing Princess Margaret. The Idiot (Bautman) Omur Celmanbet I second The Idiot – I am currently
  reading it. Hilarious and refreshing. Stoner
  (Williams) Herzog (Bellow) Lucky Jim (Amis) Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance (Pirzig) Aparajito (Bandopadhyay) Kim (Kipling) The Code of Woosters (Wodehouse) The World as It Is (Rhodes) Being Mortal (Gawande) Songlines (Chatwin) Tracks (Davidson) The Ricketty Cossak (Tattersall) The Man Who Knew Infinity (Kanigel) White Trash: The 400-Year Untold History of Class
  in America (Isenberg) Nari Subramanian So many great suggestions. Here are a few more: Stoner by John Williams (In case you’re wondering, it’s about a man named
  William Stoner, who chooses and finds solace in a life of the mind. It has nothing to do with pot J) Herzog by Saul Bellow Lucky Jim by Kingsley Amis Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance by Robert Pirzig Aparajito by Bibhutibhushan Bandopadhyay (see translation by Gopa
  Majumdar) Kim by Rudyard Kipling The Code of the Woosters, Leave it to Smith, or pretty much anything else
  by P.G. Wodehouse Non-fiction The World as it is – by Ben Rhodes Being Mortal by Atul Gawande Songlines by Bruce Chatwin Tracks by Robyn Davidson The Ricketty Cossack by Ian Tattersall The Man Who Knew Infinity by Robert Kanigel (please do not watch the
  movie) I am currently reading White Trash – A history of class in America – it is
  eye-opening.

page_20.body_text: Use the Enterprise Wiki to create a single, go-to place for knowledge sharing and project management across the enterprise. Enterprise Wikis are simple to use, flexible, and lightweight in features. They are quick and easy to create, and you can easily add links to other information systems, corporate directories, or applications. By using an Enterprise Wiki, you can avoid email overload, provide structure to new and existing information, and encourage collaboration. This helps build consensus among team members. Working with content - text, graphics or video - is as easy as working in any word processing application, such as Microsoft Word. Use the Rich Text Editor to enhance the formatting of content, apply styles to text, reorganize or spell check your content, insert and format tables, and embed graphics or video. You can do all these things without leaving the wiki page. Other things you can do when working with Enterprise Wikis: Collaborate on wiki pages with other users Comment on a wiki page to enable discussion about the contents of the page Rate a wiki page to share your opinion about its content Categorize wiki pages to enable users to quickly find information and share it with others

page_28.body_text: Use the Enterprise Wiki to create a single, go-to place for knowledge sharing and project management across the enterprise. Enterprise Wikis are simple to use, flexible, and lightweight in features. They are quick and easy to create, and you can easily add links to other information systems, corporate directories, or applications. By using an Enterprise Wiki, you can avoid email overload, provide structure to new and existing information, and encourage collaboration. This helps build consensus among team members. Working with content - text, graphics or video - is as easy as working in any word processing application, such as Microsoft Word. Use the Rich Text Editor to enhance the formatting of content, apply styles to text, reorganize or spell check your content, insert and format tables, and embed graphics or video. You can do all these things without leaving the wiki page. Other things you can do when working with Enterprise Wikis: Collaborate on wiki pages with other users Comment on a wiki page to enable discussion about the contents of the page Rate a wiki page to share your opinion about its content Categorize wiki pages to enable users to quickly find information and share it with others

page_30.body_text: ABSNET Source ABSNET/Structured Finance Portal How to Cite the Source ABSNet, LoanPerformance, Lewtan now called Structured Finance Portal (12/2020); Moody's Description The ABSNET Loan database provides loan-level origination (such as Original FICO score, LTV, CLTV, documentation type, lien position, etc.) and performance (cumulative loss, delinquency, foreclosure, loan modifications, etc.) metrics on all US non-agency securitizations. Currently the database covers 6,683 deals (5420 of them active) comprising of 20,966,521 loans (6,045,989 of them active). The database has 83 origination variables and 38 performance variables which can be seen in the Loan Extract Layout file attached under the Loan (Setup) and Loan Period (Monthly Snapshot) tabs. The attached deal universe extract file also contains information useful in understanding the coverage of the database. Time Period Covered Access One person per case at a time.  Contact Laura Londa for information. Contact: Megha Agrawal - our primary rep, Director Megha.Agrawal@moodys.com Sam Suayan--Cornerstone's Rep Brian Caddigan --Product Manager Jacob Krayn --Head of RMBS Group Cost Between between $150K and $300K, depending on the modules needed. Important Notes For a case, we were particularly interested in this database so we can perform loan-level analysis comparing Countrywide loans to those of other mortgage originators and the industry as a whole. We analyzed the average FICO, CLTV, and documentation type across different mortgage products for Countrywide and the industry. We also examined the performance of Countrywide loans against that of its competitors. The data is not perfect, but the customer support group is very friendly and helpful in answering any questions. They are also happy to incorporate into their database customer requests, though it usually takes a couple of months. We have an archive of questions and answers from ABSNet Support. Finding Insured RMBS Deals It’s possible, though not simple, to do this in Bloomberg.  From the 
Helpdesk: “BLOOMBERG HELP DESK : There is not going to be a direct way to do this. If 
you want to do this, you can use MCAL <GO> to search for a list of deal 
names. You can then take those deal names and insert them into a template, XLTP 
XMBD <GO> to see the list of bonds. Once you get the list of bonds, you 
can use the field "INSURANCE_WRAP" in a =bdp formula to see if it is insured.” ABSNet.net has a tool called the Bond Screener.  You can use this to filter 
on credit support and insurance. MBIA (and possibly other insurers) has a list of 
deals they have insured on their website here: http://www.mbia.com/investor/structfin.html ​

page_43.body_text: Internet Archive (Archive.org) Source Internet Archive How to Cite the Source Internet Archive Description The Internet Archive, a 501(c)(3) non-profit, is building a digital library of Internet sites and other cultural artifacts in digital form. Internet Archive began in 1996 by archiving the Internet itself, a medium that was just beginning to grow in use. Like newspapers, the content published on the web was ephemeral - but unlike newspapers, no one was saving it. Today the archive has 29+ years of web history accessible through the Wayback Machine . It also works with 1,250+ library and other partners through our Archive-It program to identify important web pages. As the web archive grew, so did the organization's commitment to providing digital versions of other published works. Today our archive contains: 916 billion web pages 49 million books and texts 13 million audio recordings (including 268,000 live concerts) 10 million videos (including 3 million Television News programs) 5 million images 1 million software programs Because it is a library, the Internet Archive pays special attention to books. Books published in or prior to 1929 are available for download, and hundreds of thousands of modern books can be borrowed through its Open Library site. Like the Internet, television is also an ephemeral medium. The organization began archiving television programs in late 2000, and its first public TV project was an archive of TV news surrounding the events of September 11, 2001 . In 2009 the Internet Archive began to make selected U.S. television news broadcasts searchable by captions in its TV News Archive . This service allows researchers and the public to use television as a citable and sharable reference. Time Period Covered Internet: back to 1996 Books: varies Television news: back to late 2000 Access archive.org Contact: For assistance using the Internet Archive, email #Information Resources Cost Free (scanned texts require registration) Important Notes Some of the content available through the Archive may be governed by local, national, and/or international laws and regulations, and your use of such content is solely at your own risk. Users agree to abide by all applicable laws and regulations, including intellectual property laws, in connection with their use of the Archive. In particular, users certify that their use of any part of the Archive's Collections will be limited to non-infringing or fair use under copyright law. AI Restrictions AI use of any content found through the Internet Archive would be subject to the specific content's original terms of use AI Definitions/Capabilities ​ Updated 9/17/25_hg

ALM is mostly using Generative AI only in testing at this point. They have incorporated automated solutions into different products to help improve workflows. How does ALM plan to use generative AI and advanced AI in the future? ALM plans to continue to use AI to enhance their work and process more data. What are some benefits that ALM sees in their use of AI? ALM's archive of data is trained with AI which allows them to generate better search results, identify key trends, and provide other insights. What are some negative consequences or concerns regarding the use of AI as it impacts ALM? Data privacy considerations Do you see AI impacting jobs at ALM and if so, how? "AI will certainly impact how everyone works. ALM will try to use it to help staff increase productivity. We want to be able to deliver more content and increase our breadth of coverage." How do you currently allow others to use your data with external AI? Do you see that as an issue – if so, what are your future plans to combat that? "We do not allow outside parties to use our data, and our IT team puts safeguards around the scraping of our content." Additional Information? ALM has internal guidelines for the use of AI to make internal staff aware of the benefits and pitfalls of tools available. Updated 10/05/2025_tr

page_48.body_text: Australia Commonwealth of Courts Source Australia Commonwealth Courts How to Cite the Source Cite by court. Description The Commonwealth Courts Portal is an initiative of the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia and Federal Court of Australia. It provides web-based services for clients to access case file information. E.g., documents filed and upcoming court events, as well as outcomes of court events and any orders made. Federal Law Search is available via the Commonwealth Courts Portal. It provides selected case file information to the public. Federal Law Search does not require registration and is free to use. Only orders and judgements are part of the public case file. All other documents are displayed in the case file but must be requested directly from the court. Public case file search link: Federal Law Search Case files may contain the following: Orders and judgements List of documents filed Name of parties and legal counsel Time Period Covered January 1984 to present Access Everyone at Cornerstone can access. See this step-by-step guide for How to Make an Access Request to Inspect Court Documents . Contact: Email #Information Resources with requests. Cost Case files are free along with orders and judgements. Cost varies for document orders. See current fees here . Important Notes Restricted Documents: Obtaining certain documents may be limited if they are considered 'restricted.' 'Restricted' documents in a proceeding are those documents that fall outside the categories set out in subrule 2.32(2) of the Federal Court Rules. Examples of restricted documents include an affidavit (other than an affidavit accompanying an application or amended application in a native title proceeding); an exhibit; an expert report ; evidence taken on deposition; and written submissions. To inspect restricted documents, non-party requires the leave of the Court, under sub-rule 2.32(4) of the Federal Court Rules. Public Interest Case Files: There are some cases considered to be of significance to the public and documents will be made available in an Online File.  These Public Interest case files may contain what are usually considered restricted documents such as affidavits and exhibits. See here for a list of current Public Interest case files. AI Restrictions AI Definitions/Capabilities Updated 6/22/2026_AA

If you pulled your data via Request Builder, you can use it for your case and turn it over.  If you did not, please contact Gena Rosati to discuss whether you can use it or not. Description Please note there are some limitations to using the Bloomberg terminal. Bloomberg provides extensive, up-to-the-minute information on stocks, bonds, indices, mortgage-backed securities and commodities. Includes detailed historical price data regarding: · US Treasury and non-US-government bonds · Corporate debt · Mortgage-backed securities · Money market · Municipal debt · Equity · Preferred shares · Commodity markets · Indices · Currency Includes fixed income data regarding: · Price/Yields · Current Credit Ratings · Historical Credit Ratings · Credit Spreads · New Issuances · ABX Data Time Period Covered Data from the Federal Reserve is typically available going back at least 10 years, and often much longer. Intra-day data : Bloomberg keeps only 240 day of data for the lesser used indices.  You can send an inquiry to our rep. about prior data. Access Contact the #Bloomberg Request Team regarding data inquiries and retrievals. Accessible in some offices via a dedicated Bloomberg terminal. If there is not a terminal in your office, you can contact #BOS Bloomberg Request Team for assistance from consultants in the Boston office, who are the most knowledgeable about what is available. The first time you log in to the terminal you will need to create a profile. Either check on the back of terminal for the serial number or try putting these seri al numbers into the terminal: SN 493071 SN 174877 Contact customer service and they can walk you through setting up an account. Bloomberg Customer Service: 212-318-2000. Bloomberg data is available via SFTP using dlsftp.bloomberg.com. See additional info . Much of the historical data is available through the Data License Request Builder. Please follow the instructions here. You will also need to save this file to the desktop of the terminal before trying to log in (if it is not already there). For the Data License Requ est Builder Software, please refer to the CRIKIT page and the Data License Software Manual. For the BVAL product please refer to the BVAL User Guide. Cost $150 per login.  Cases will only be charged up to $1,500 per month for login charges. I f you expect that your Bloomberg data charge
will be $1,000 or more, please email Gena Rosati, Matt Armstrong, Ryan Clydesdale, and Royce Kennedy with your
account user number, the case name, and expected data charge. Data download pricing as of 6/23/26: Per Security Fee Appendix 2026.pdf The headings of each table correspond (roughly) to the Download Categories in the request bulider and to column AD on the Request Builder fields spreadsheet. Contact #Information Resources with any questions Contact (within CR or Vendor) Internally you may contact #Bloomberg Request Team with questions regarding the software and how to use it. The list of members by office is located here . There is also a 24/7 Bloomberg Data License help desk available on the web. You can login from your desktop to ask your questions. You will also be able to see all questions that have been asked by Cornerstone people to see if your question has already been asked and answered. Create your own UserID , and the Password will be emailed to you.  If the form asks: Acct:783004 and Cust:30243067. Once in, click on Post Query at the top to post a question.  Click View Query to see all questions asked with answers. This group cannot answer pricing questions, but our reps listed below can. Our Customer Support reps are: NY/Boston Annie Gjineci: agjineci1@bloomberg.net LA Alexis Longo: alongo12@bloomberg.net Our Data License rep in NY/Boston is: Glen Fuchs: gfuchs@bloomberg.net Cornerstone Comments Always check the Bloomberg settings page (dividend adjustment, stock split adjsutment etc..) to ensure that you are getting the appropriate data.  Do this by entering "PDFE <GO>". Trade Volume Data: North American-listed securities (NYSE, Nasdaq, and Toronto) should be downloaded from Eikon if you do not need to include foreign exchange listed trading volume in your analysis. Pricing data is downloaded from the same source as the trading volume data. Eikon requires careful attention to be sure the correct RICs (the unique security identifier in Eikon) are being used.  In particular, confirm whether the selected RIC represents a consolidated RIC or an individual security. Global Trading Volume Data should be downloaded from Bloomberg for global trading volume downloads for securities with listings on foreign ex changes (non-North American) that need to be accounted for in an analysis. If addressing a dual-listed security, North American data should also be downloaded from Bloomberg as well.  The practice of downloading pricing data from the same source as the trading volume data should continue. Alternate Data Sources -- The Information Resources group has put together spreadsheets covering the various types of data normally pulled from Bloomberg.  Each sheet has a list of alternate sources for a certain type of data with notes, contact and pricing information where available.  If you are interested in any of these sources, please contact the IR group to assist with contacting the vendors. page_58.body_text: ​ Blo omberg Data License Request Builder Bloomberg has changed the authentication process for request builder; before being able to use the program, you will need to perform a simple setting change. Please use the attached instructions to update the configuration to your profile; you will only need to do this once. The key and the information needed can be found on the Bloomberg terminal in the following location: C:\Windows\Request Builder\private-key.ppk Directions Please feel free to contact #IT Help Desk if you have questions or require assistance with the process. As of March 8, 2010, Bloomberg's Request Builder software has replaced the Bloomberg API Excel tool (Historical Data Wizard and other functions).  Please use the links below as an introductory guide to the Data License Request Builder software. Request Builder Software User Manual (2014) 1. Per Security Product Manual 2. How to Configure the Software 3. How to Download Historical Data Using the Gethistory Function 4. How to Download Dividend History for an Index Using the Gethistory Function 5. How to Download Dividend History Using the Getdata Function 6. How to Specify a Pricing Source 7. Cost of Data 8. Frequently Asked Questions 9. More Questions? Per Security Product Manual A copy is saved here . See bookmarks for Gethistory fields. This manual contains syntax for more advanced functions (bulk downloads, etc) and error codes. How to Configure the Software Log onto the Bloomberg terminal. Save this file on your desktop Follow these software download instructions For parsing data, download the latest version of The+BB+Parser.xls . You must save this file and open it from your hard drive or the LAN. Do not choose Open File. How to Download Historical Data Using the Gethistory Function Click on the Request Builder icon on your desktop. Follow these step-by-step instructions . Save your request using the naming convention ticker_12345_01.req . In your Output Format options, specify " horizontal ." N.B.  Data License historical stock/volume data defaults to Adjusting for Splits Not adjusting for dividends You can change these defaults by linking to your Bloomberg Personal Defaults - Equity (PDFE).  See FAQ . A list of available fields for GetHistory can be found here . How to Download Dividend History for an Index Using the Gethistory Function Follow a similar process to that for a Historical Data Download. In your fields list, add INDX_NET_DAILY_DIV . In your securities list, ensure that you have a Yellow Key Index. In your Output Format options, specify " horizontal ." How to Download Dividend History Using the Getdata Function Follow a similar process to that for a Historical Data Download. Use Program Name: " getdata "; Program Flag: " oneshot " In your fields list, add DVD_HIST_ALL In your securities list, use the following syntax to get dividend history between two dates: Security||2|DVD_START_DT|DVD_END_DT|YYYYMMDD(of Start Date)|YYYYMMDD(of End Date)| This syntax is called an override.  You can read more about overrides in the Product Manual . In your Output Format options, specify " bulklists ." The output columns are returned in the following order: Declared Date, EX-Date, Record Date, Pay Date, Net Amount, Frequency, Dividend Type For many purposes Cornerstone will use the Ex-Date, but you should check with your manager. How to Specify a Pricing Source In some cases, you may want to specify a pricing source other than the default (for instance, TRACE). You can do so by specifying the PRICING_SOURCE in the header of your request file.  If you only want this pricing source, add EXCLUSIVE_PRICING_SRC=yes. See attachment Sample for an example request file which requests TRACE data exclusively.  You would save this file on your local drive, upload it to the FTP site, then re-dowload the request to your local drive. Cost of Data See cost section of the main Bloomberg CRIKIT Page .  When you use GetHistory to download historical end of day data, the cost is $3/security regardless of which dates, fields, or securities you download.  Contact #Information Resources with any questions about pricing. Frequently Asked Questions See FAQ page. More Questions? Contact: #Bloomberg Software Help for internal support from Cornerstone power users There is also a 24/7 Bloomberg Data License help desk available on the web. You can login from your desktop to ask your questions. You will also be able to see all questions that have been asked by Cornerstone people to see if your question has already been asked and answered. Create your own UserID , and the Password will be emailed to you.  If the form asks: Acct:783004 and Cust:30243067. Once in, click on Post Query at the top to post a question.  Click View Query to see all questions asked with answers.
