page_59.body_text: ​FAQ FAQ for Bloomberg Data License 1. Pricing/Logistics 1.1. Is there a document with pricing for different data categories? 1.2. When is Cornerstone charged for the data we retrieve? 1.3. If I request a data field that isn’t available for a particular security, am I still charged for the data if it is all “NA”? 1.4. Is it necessary to “save” your data request before submitting? Or will the request still work if you go straight to “submit”? 1.5. Will I be charged for downloading an Excel file directly from the Bloomberg terminal that is not available through the data license? 1.6. If a security has more than 1 CUSIP associated with it; will we be charged for each CUSIP (sometimes 10-15) or by security? 1.7. Will I be charged for downloading an Excel file directly from the Bloomberg terminal that is not available through the data license? There are approximately 5100 securities that trade on the NYSE and first tier NasdaQ: If you need just pricing for one particular day in time that could be obtained through our single point history feature at a cost of $0.20 a security. Since market cap was also mentioned, the only method of pulling that data point historically is through our gethistory program at a cost of $3.00 a security. Since the gethistory program does not distinguish between 1 day of history or 10 years, additional history could be pulled on that security list and still remain within the $3.00 charge. Is downloading news articles from Bloomberg free? There is no additional cost beyond the $150 login. We need to download daily returns data from Bloomberg for around 15 funds over 2 years. We would like an estimate of what this will cost. The cost will be $3 per fund assuming they are funds whose info is basic and publically available. How much is it to download auction rate security data? Pricing for these securities would depend on the type of security that they are pulling. This information would cost the following on a per security basis: Corporates, Money Markets, Governments: $1.50 Municipals: $1.00 Agency Pools: $0.15 CMO, CMBS, Whole Loans and ABS: $2.00 How much would it cost to download corporate bond pricing data from Bloomberg? It depends on the bond.  If they are just basic bonds that are generally available (i.e. not illiquid) and you are just getting pricing then it is either $3 per bond if you are getting the history (gethistory function), or $.60 per bond if you are just getting a few days.  That is per bond, not per day. I am trying to get a price estimate for retrieving the ratings for 350 bonds over 5 years? Unfortunately, ratings are not available to be downloaded historically. Does downloading a CACS (looking it up on a terminal and outputting to Excel) cost money, beyond the Bloomberg logon fee? the charge is $1.50 per security for Corporate and Government securities. This is the charge incurred when using the data license software.  If you are able to export a screen directly from the Bloomberg terminal, there is no additional charge for that.  Basically, if you want just a few companies, you'd probably want to use the export function from the terminal.  If you wanted the CACS for a few hundred companies, the data license is more cost efficient in terms of time. What is the cost for downloading industry/sector related descriptive fields for a number of different securities? For example, 127 securities for variables (INDUSTRY_SECTOR or INDUSTRY_GROUP) The cost would be $1.50 per security regardless of whether you requested one or both of those fields. Specifying Downloads/Fields How do you enter date ranges when using the download tool? You can just use date range in some programs as gethistory, getticks, getquotes, getallticks, getallquotes, getactions and getfundamental. If you are using request builder you can use the calendar on the bottom, if you are writing your request you just need to include DATERANGE= on your header (see page 18 of the Per Security manual for more details) Is there a comprehensive list of Getdata fields (there appears to be one for Gethistory in the Data License Per Security Product Manual). Which fields can be downloaded for Getdata but not Gethistory? There is a file that is updated daily on our server called “fields.csv.”  This lists all of the fields with their field types. Gethistory is mainly for historical prices. Is there any way the data tool can download descriptive information such as DES screens or News summaries, or does this information need to come from the Bloomberg terminal? Info that appears on DES screens may be accessed through Per Security requests, however, there is not a request type per say that will fully encompass all data that appears on a DES screen without individually selecting each data point in the file. News may not be accessed through Data License Per Security, however, there is a news feed product we offer as a separate license. Personal Defaults According to the Data License Per Security Product Manual, it is possible to link the data license account with individual Bloomberg logins, to take advantage of personal defaults.  Will individual Cornerstone users be able to access their personal defaults when using the data download tool? The Cornerstone Bloomberg terminals are shared terminals, however, they may be linked to Request Builder software in order to set overrides (i.e. specific pricing sources, distributions, fundamental analysis, etc). Split-adjusted and not split-adjusted share price defaults may be set on the Terminal through the PDFE<GO> function.  Choose 6<GO> and at the bottom of the page you’ll see an area to set Capital Changes Defaults. In order to link to a terminal, you will type “IAM” and press enter on the terminal.  This will give you a User # and S/N.  This info may be entered in the “Optional Parameter” area under the Settings tab on the Request Builder Login screen. N.B. that this will change the defaults for all users of your data license terminal, so use this option carefully (i.e. switch back to standard defaults before logging off). According to the Data License Per Security Product Manual, the Gethistory program defaults to adjusting volume/price for splits and not dividends. Do personal defaults override the Gethistory defaults?  Is there a way to change these defaults, besides by linking through personal defaults?  Do these defaults apply to the Getdata program, or is price/volume only from Gethistory? The only way to have your personal default attached to DL is by linking your request to a Terminal. You can run getdata also linked, all your set ups will be applied in this case (pricing source, PDFE, PDFN, etc). · Data License defaults . · Adjustments that can/cannot be made by linking to PDF are here (see columns F-J). Data questions What is the Difference between Bloomberg and Markit Short Sales Data? There are three main reasons for the differences, all of which relate to how Bloomberg gets its data vs. Markit.  Bloomberg gets its data from the exchange and the reporting entities are U.S. broker dealers.  Markit gets its data from its global clients (custodians, prime brokers, hedge funds), which give Markit data on their securities lending activity (custodian), securities borrowing activity (prime brokers), and cost of borrowing (hedge funds).  Markit uses its proprietary data on securities lending to proxy for short interest whereas Bloomberg gives the reported numbers.  The reasons for the data differences are: Bloomberg’s data includes naked shorts, which option market makers are allowed to do.  Since shares are not borrowed in this scenario, Markit data would not reflect it. When an investor (e.g., a hedge fund) wants to short, it will go to its prime broker to borrow shares.  Depending on the situation, the prime broker may lend out shares from its own inventory (e.g., from their proprietary trading desk) rather than go out and borrow shares from a custodian.  This usually makes the cost of borrowing lower, but tends to happen only for blue chip stocks where shares are plentiful.  This type of shorting would be reported in Bloomberg’s data, but not in Markit’s (presumably because the prime broker didn’t actually borrow shares). Markit’s clients are global and includes firms that do not report to the exchange.  For example, if a foreign firm wants to short a U.S. stock, that would not be reported in Bloomberg, but would potentially be captured by Markit. More questions? Email your Bloomberg contacts .

page_60.body_text: ​Bloomberg limitations In general, only data retrieved using the Request Builder can be used for case work. Excel Add-in We do not, and cannot, have access to Bloomberg’s Excel Plug-In. Even if you were able to download it, you would not be able to use it as it has been disabled on their end. The reason so many people are confused, is because the Bloomberg help desk does not have access to any information regarding our contract. Thus when we contact them, the first thing they tell us to do is to download the plug-in. And even if the person at Cornerstone knows enough to say we are not allowed to have access to it, the BB help-desk doesn’t understand that. We are not the typical BB client, and it is rare for BB to restrict access to their plug-in, so the help desk is always sure we are wrong. Excel Icon For some data, the terminal has an icon for exporting to Excel (without the Add-in). This data is unique to Bloomberg and is the exception.  This data can be downloaded and used in casework. Screen shots Using screen shots from the Bloomberg terminal violates our contract.  Additionally, we cannot manually enter the screen shot data into a spreadsheet. Adding new data No one in Cornerstone has the authority to enter into a contract to add or increase any amount of data from an existing or new data source. The Bloomberg help desk wants to meet your needs and may offer to add a contract for data that is not usually available.  These contract additions are not free.  Ex: No one can approve adding access to historical Markit ABS index data. Programs and robots No one can, under any circumstances, write and install a program that will automate going into Bloomberg and downloading articles, data, screenshots, etc. This violates our license and Bloomberg will shut us down (and possibly sue us) if they suspect we are doing this. Bloomberg monitor the activity on their terminals very closely. Log-in Every person must create their own login and password.  Shared passwords make it difficult to track billing. Billing Pop-up Be sure to type in the correct case name each time you log on.

page_62.body_text: ​Bloomberg Law Source Bloomberg Law How to Cite the Source Citation style can depend on the information accessed through Bloomberg Law.  News articles retrieved from Bloomberg Law (e.g. Bloomberg News or Bloomberg First Word) would follow a standard citation format.  Books and treatises would cite the content and include " available at Bloomberg Law." Description Bloomberg Law is a legal research database comprised of News & Analysis, Court Dockets, Practice Centers, Laws & Regulations, and Secondary Sources. Information Resources uses Bloomberg Law primarily to search Bloomberg News articles and court dockets from federal and state courts. There are also various tools for company research and legal analytics. Time Period Covered Varies. Bloomberg News goes back to 6/17/1991. Access Only IR has access. Contact: Email #Information Resources with requests. Cost News searches and headlines are free. News articles:  $3.50 each. Courier document retrievals:  $100 per order, plus $2 per page. Docket tracks and updates:  $.10 per page to a maximum of $3 for any single document. Important Notes Bloomberg does not have comprehensive coverage of news sources, so it is not an appropriate source for a news content analysis.  However, it is our main source for Bloomberg News articles that can be used in production. Additional comments: We can create custom, targeted news searches limited by both keywords and fielded criteria like the Company or Ticker, names of People, Topics, Regions, and Industries. Unlike Factiva, we cannot search for certain keywords in headlines and other keywords anywhere in the article. We can only search for all keywords in headlines or in the first # words of an article. Up to 1,000 headlines can be downloaded at once. Large news retrievals will be comprised of several excel files. AI Restrictions Bloomberg's Terms of Service: Any use of Bloomberg's data for use outside of the firm needs prior approval from Bloomberg. Please contact IR if you plan to use AI on any Bloomberg products. AI Definitions/Capabilities Bloomberg's Use of AI: leverage externally hosted commercial & open source LLMs Accuracy of LLMs: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): "limits the use of LLMs to Bloomberg Industry Group content, fine-tuning, and guardrails to increase accuracy and help ensure outputs are based on real data." Claim to regularly test their products using LLMs for accuracy Privacy and AI: Bloomberg does not use consumer data to train LLM models They retain customer search queries for quality assurance and to enhance search functionality Organizational Policy on AI: outlines guidelines for data handling, security best practices, and responsible AI development Security Controls: encryption, access controls, intrusion detection systems, prompt injection controls, anonymization, and guardrails AI/LLM Use-Case Review Committee: This committee of professionals evaluates potential security risks, data privacy concerns, and ethical implications, helping to ensure responsible use of technology Generative AI Products (as of Feb 2025) AI-Driven Legal Research and Tools (as of June 2025) Bloomberg Law AI Assistant, a chat-based tool that allows you to summarize and ask questions about documents you're viewing, including Court Opinions, Court Rules, U.S. Code and CFR sections, State Statutes, Regulations, Session Laws, and Constitutions, as well as select secondary sources.  Deep thinking mode allows for more complete, complex and nuanced research. Bloomberg Law AI Assistant Flyer_May 2026.pdf Bloomberg Law Answers , which provides a quick answer to your search question using relevant legal documents, including Federal and State Court Opinions, U.S. Code, CFR, State Statutes and Regulations, Practical Guidance, Bloomberg Law News, and secondary sources like books and manuals. AI Summary for Complaints , a feature that draws out the main points in an initial public complaint. Updated 05/19/2026_SAT

page_65.body_text: ​Bureau of Labor Statistics Source Bureau of Labor Statistics How to Cite the Source Bureau of Labor Statistics Description The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) is the principal fact-finding agency for the Federal Government in the broad field of labor economics and statistics. The BLS is an independent national statistical agency that collects, processes, analyzes, and disseminates essential statistical data to the American public, the U.S. Congress, other Federal agencies, State and local governments, business, and labor. The BLS also serves as a statistical resource to the Department of Labor. The BLS publishes a wide variety of labor-related statistics, including: Inflation and prices (including consumer price index for urban wage earners and clerical workers; all urban consumers; average price data; department store inventory price index; producer price index for industry data; commodity data; and international price index); Employment (employment, hours, and earnings, national and state; labor force statistics; job openings and labor turnover survey; state and county employment and wages; business employment dynamics; wages from occupational employment statistics survey; American time use survey; union affiliation data; employment projections); Unemployment (labor force statistics including the national unemployment rate; local area unemployment statistics; layoffs); Pay and benefits (national compensation survey; employment cost index; employer cost for employee compensation; employee benefits survey; work stoppages; work stoppages data; weekly & hourly earnings; national, state and county earnings/wages); Spending and time use (consumer expenditure survey; American time use survey); Productivity (major sector productivity and costs index; major sector multifactor productivity index; industry productivity and costs; foreign labor statistics); Workplace injuries (census of fatal occupational injuries; nonfatal cases involving days away from work; occupational injuries and illnesses; occupational injuries and illnesses and fatal injuries profiles); International (foreign labor statistics; prices; import/export price indexes); Employment projections (education level; occupational; occupation across industries; industry employment). Time Period Covered Most data series are available over many years, with many available over decades.  However, some data sets are more limited in availability. Access BLS website Contact: (202) 691-5200 or use the email form online: http://data.bls.gov/cgi-bin/forms/opb?/home.htm Cost Free Important Notes AI Restrictions ​ AI Definitions/Capabilities ​ Updated 9/25/2025_aig

page_82.body_text: CLS Source CLS Group Holdings AG How to Cite the Source CLS Group Holdings AG Description CLS plays a fundamental role in the foreign exchange (FX) market – it operates the largest multicurrency cash settlement system to mitigate settlement risk for the FX transactions of its Members and their customers. Settlement of FX transactions requires the exchange of principal in two currencies. Settlement risk is the risk that one party pays the currency it sold but does not receive the currency it bought, resulting in a loss of principal. Background The impetus behind the creation of CLS came from regulatory concerns regarding the potential for FX settlement risk to be a major source of systemic risk, following the collapse of Bankhaus Herstatt. Launched in 2002 and owned by the world's leading FX banks, CLS settles payment instructions relating to underlying FX transactions in 18 currencies and certain other transactions that result in one-way payments in a subset of those currencies. How CLS Works CLS mitigates settlement risk through the provision of its unique payment versus payment settlement service which has direct links to the real time gross settlement (RTGS) systems of the currencies it settles. In addition to mitigating settlement risk, CLS also streamlines and standardizes FX operations, reducing costs. FX settlement includes potentially large cash funding values.  These values are materially reduced in CLS through the multilateral netting of the obligations between Member banks to deliver best in class liquidity management.  As regulatory requirements for larger liquidity buffers increase, the benefits from multilateral netting at an industry level are increasingly important. Time Period Covered ​ Access Contact CLS directly. Contact: London: +44 (0)207 971 5700 New York: +1 212 943 2290 Tokyo: +81 3 3517 2791 Hong Kong: +852 3520 6000 Cost Important Notes They do not currently offer a commercial product. They have a very high level monthly report on their website.  They mentioned that they are considering launching a commercial product but have no launch date or specifications available at this time.  They said that they can respond to requests for supplemental data from central banks working with them. They have no coverage of non-deliverable forwards.  They have coverage of a large range of OTC deliverable FX products. In the 18 currencies where they offer settlement ( https://www.cls-group.com/products/settlement/clssettlement/currencies/ ), they estimate that they have greater than 90% market share of the OTC FX market. AI Restrictions ​ AI Definitions/Capabilities ​ Updated 9/25/2025_aig

page_87.body_text: Competition Policy International (includes former GCP Magazine) Source Competition Policy International How to Cite the Source Competition Policy International Description Competition Policy International (CPI) is an independent knowledge-sharing organization focused on the diffusion of the most relevant antitrust information and content worldwide. CPI recognizes the importance of intellectually sound and balanced debates and aim to promote them across the world in the most innovative ways available. Created and managed by leaders in the competition policy community, CPI delivers timely commentary and analysis on antitrust and global competition policy matters through a variety of media and applications. CPI PUBLICATIONS CPI releases daily, weekly, and monthly antitrust-focused publications that reach several thousands of readers including enforcers, judges, lawyers, economists and academics in over 150 countries. CPI Columns are released regularly to provide up-to-date analysis on the most current antitrust issues. CPI also publishes books in hard-cover, paperback, and electronic formats. CPI Antitrust Chronicle (formerly known as GCP Magazine: The Online Magazine) The Antitrust Chronicle, our signature publication, is released bimonthly and consists of articles written by leading experts in competition law and economics. Articles focus on a specific topic at the forefront of competition law and policy debates.  CPI Antitrust Chronicle was formerly known as GCP Magazine: The Online Magazine and is dedicated to the intellectual integrity of all of the articles that it publishes. Articles and commentary published in the CPI journal and in CPI Antitrust Chronicle are selected and reviewed by editorial teams comprised of competition policy experts drawn from academia, authorities, courts, and law firms around the world. CPI Antitrust Chronicle has been published since November 2006. CPI Antitrust Chronicle does not solicit or accept payment for contributions, nor does it provide preference to any individual or entity that has purchased subscriptions to its publications. GCP does not accept funding from any entity, directly or indirectly, in exchange for publishing articles related to any case or ongoing controversy. CPI Journal CPI Journal was a peer-reviewed, academic journal that covers competition law, economics, and policy. Issues were published twice a year in the Spring and Autumn and in both print and online forms. The journal was published from 2005 to 2015. Issues were arranged thematically and included both new articles and 1 or 2 classic antitrust articles to refresh readers' memories of seminal discussions on important topics. Time Period Covered ​ Access Competition Policy International If you can't access something, try logging into this site: https://www.pymnts.com/cpi/account-management/ Another alternative:  If you see a blue box with a message on the web page that says "THIS ARTICLE IS NOT AVAILABLE FOR IP ADDRESS 4.30.144.108. Please verify email or join us to access premium content!" you can follow these steps: Click on "verify e-mail" Enter your e-mail address, you will then receive an e-mail with a link. Please save this e-mail with the link. Click on the link in the e-mail. Once this process has been finalized, you should now be able to access the Chronicles included in your CPI plan. If you use different browsers, you will need to verify each browser using the same link you received in your e-mail. This process only needs to be completed once. This link can also be used to verify a second device. Contact: #Information Resources Cost Free (Cornerstone has a subscription) Important Notes AI Restrictions Customer will not copy, reprint or distribute content except for in ways in accordance with this Agreement and as set forth in the Order. page_100.body_text: ​ CRSP FAQ ​The CRSP Support Team handles large and/or custom data requests that would be impossible or inconvenient to retrieve from the portal.  Additionally, the CRSP Support Team has access to variables not available through the portal.  The CRSP Support Team can be reached by email at #CRSP SUPPORT . 1. What does it mean when there is a - or negative value? 2. How am I charged for a custom data request fulfilled by the CRSP Support Team? 3. How should I format a request to the CRSP team? 4. Where can I get the PERMNOs for the data points in my custom request? 5. What data fields are included in a custom request and how are they organized? 6. How current is the data from custom requests? 7. I would like data for CRSP NYSE/AMEX/Nasdaq Value-Weighted Index but the portal only shows the CRSP NYSE/Amex/Nasdaq/Arca Value-Weighted Index.  Is the index without ARCA available? What does it mean when there is a - or negative value? A: If you look on page 69 of this PDF (72 of 130 of the total pdf).  Look at PRICE ADJUSTED, END OF PERIOD. PRICE ADJUSTED, END OF PERIOD Category: Prices Data Type: Floating Point Description: Daily — Daily close, adjusted for distributions. Replaced with bid/ask average if price not available. Bid/ask average identified by a leading dash -. How am I charged for a custom data request fulfilled by the CRSP Support Team? A: For custom data requests completed by the CRSP team, you will be charged the standard $0.15 per security per day (regardless of number of data points) that is applied when downloading data via the Portal-based interface (see CRSP for further information).  As well, the team member who is in charge of handling the request will bill his/her time to the case.  Since we pull our data directly from the database, it does not take very long to complete a request and the time billed is generally minimal (i.e. 15 minutes).  Please see the CRSP page for more pricing information.  Please contact Laura Londa with any other pricing questions. How should I format a request to the CRSP team? A: Your data request should generally come as a list of PERMNOs with the applicable start and end dates for each security (please format as YYYYMMDD).  We can also pull data by exchange (e.g. all NYSE securities) and we can work with you to pull data by other variables like SIC codes, share type (e.g. common equity, ADR, ETFs), etc. Where can I get the PERMNOs for the data points in my custom request? A: A list of all securities available from CRSP, their identifying information, and the available date range can be found in the header file at \\CRSPVM\crsp\Public Shares\Useful Files\headfile.xlsx . (open as Read-Only) What data fields are included in a custom request and how are they organized? A: Unless otherwise instructed, custom data requests will include all of the same fields and in the same order as when the data is pulled from the portal.  However, CRSP has a large number of fields in addition to those available from the portal.  Please consult the data documentation here . How current is the data from custom requests? A: Just as in the portal, data from custom requests has about a one month lag. I would like data for CRSP NYSE/AMEX/Nasdaq Value-Weighted Index but the portal only shows the CRSP NYSE/Amex/Nasdaq/Arca Value-Weighted Index.  Is the index without ARCA available? A: CRSP changed their U.S. Stock Database product in 2009 so that we no longer receive the NYSE/Amex/Nasdaq index.  Instead, we get the NYSE/Amex/Nasdaq/Arca index.  The old index may still exist in their other products, but we don't get it anymore.  If you really want it, I'm sure you can buy it from them separately. We still have old data for the NYSE/Amex/Nasdaq index , but we only have data through January 2009: Useful Links A guide of all CRSP data descriptions, including all available variables can be found at \\Sqlcogen1\crsp\Public Shares\CRSP Documentation\data_descriptions_guide.pdf For standard CRSP requests, you can access CRSP directly through the portal

page_112.body_text: Courtroom View Network (CVN) Source Courtroom View Network (CVN) How to Cite the Source Courtroom View Network Description Courtroom View Network (CVN) delivers live and on-demand video and editorial coverage of high-stakes civil litigation. Since 2004, the CVN video library has grown to include over 1,000 trials with tens of thousands of hours of fully indexed, searchable video. Unless otherwise stated, all trials are fully indexed with evidence slides so that you see exactly what was presented at trial. Users can search by trial name, attorney, judge, expert witness, and more. Premium CVN docket, gavel-to-gavel CVN Video, and CVN Training services are provided as subscriptions, which provide access to trials, hearings, oral arguments, and other courtroom video that may be streamed over the Internet. Users may watch proceedings Live, or On Demand, on their personal computer, depending on the subscription. Video may also be viewed on DVD-ROM (Computer Only, playable in the CVN Player with synched digital exhibits) or DVD. When ordering DVDs, subscribers select proceedings at on CVN.com and receive them on DVD by U.S. mail or Fedex. CVN Video proceedings are designated into two categories: CVN Live Current Cases and CVN On Demand Archive Cases. CVN Live Current Cases are proceedings that are upcoming, in progress, or concluded within the last 30 days. These proceedings are available in one or all of the following formats: Live, On Demand, on DVD. A CVN Live subscription provides video access to all Current Cases, with premium events available only under a CVN Live Premium subscription. CVN On Demand Archive Cases are proceedings that concluded more than 30 days ago, and where the video has undergone a quality assessment, quality improvement where possible, and video chapters are logged for better browsing and navigation. These proceedings are available in these formats: DVD, On Demand. These proceedings are sold in a discount subscription and available through an annual CVN On Demand subscription. CVN's Editorial team finds trials using a variety of sources, including dockets and news articles. They also receive many tips and they poll subscribers to find out what they want to see. List of cases covered Time Period Covered 2004 - present Access Must purchase subscription Contact: #Information Resources Cost Video Library access online: https://cvn.com/pricing ($99 per month for 1 person, $399 per month for up to 6). This only includes online viewing of completed trials. Premium Live Access or Digital Downloads: Pricing for live and on-demand access to a single case is below. Each account or user would be able to log in from one device at a time. 1-3 accounts - $600 per day 4-6 accounts - $800 per day 7-9 accounts - $1000 per day Firm Wide - $1200 per day Downloadable files in addition to any option above would be $400 per day. Downloadable files would be delivered within 36 hours of each day ending. Live and on-demand access for the firm to all trials we cover would be $3,000 per month on an annual contract. Important Notes CVN focuses on civil litigation. Memberships automatically renew unless cancelled, which can be done on the Account page. Video Library memberships do not include access to live trials. CVN will periodically offer certain live trials to our members depending on interest. We would need to negotiate a license with CVN if we were to get a full subscription. AI Restrictions Parent company Remote Counsel (RC) grants users a limited license to access and make personal use of CVN and not to download (other than page caching) or modify it, or any portion of it, except with express written consent of RC. This license does not include any resale or commercial use of CVN.com or its contents; any collection and use of any product listings, descriptions, or prices; any derivative use of CVN.com or its contents; any downloading or copying of account information for the benefit of another merchant; or any use of data mining, robots, or similar data gathering and extraction tools. CVN.com and any portion of it content may not be reproduced, duplicated, copied, sold, resold, visited, or otherwise exploited for any commercial purpose without express written consent of RC. page_120.body_text: Datastream Source Datastream How to Cite the Source LSEG Workspace Description DataStream is the world's largest, most respected financial statistical database with access to more than 2 million instruments (securities and indicators for over 175 countries in 60 markets) which include worldwide equity coverage, comprehensive market indices, economics data direct from national government sources as well as the OECD and IMF, fixed income securities and associated indices, commodities and derivatives data. Also available is earnings forecast data from I/B/E/S . For more information, please see Analyst Estimates information sheet. A quick overview of Datastream content. Time Period Covered up to 50 years of history Access There is a Datastream add-on within the LSEG Workspace add-on and you can ask for access if you don't have it already For other questions, you can email #Information Resources with requests. Cost $250 per login to LSEG Workspace. Contact (within CR or Vendor) Datastream Customer Support 1-888-888-1082, option 2 Datastream Online Support: http://extranet.datastream.com/logon.aspx Cornerstone Comments I/B/E/S on Datastream user guide Answers to some questions that have come up regarding IBES data: 1.  What is the source of the Actual (Annual and Interim) EPS values? (DS: I0EPS and F0EPS) Datastream updates the actuals from many sources like press release, broker reports, PR Newswire, Company websites, market watch etc. The estimates are provided by the various contributors (brokers) spread all over the world. The brokers could be sell side and buy side. These include GOLDMAN SACHS, MORGAN STANLEY, JPMORGAN, Deutsche Bank, UBS, and Credit Suisse etc. We calculate neither estimates nor the Actuals. The actuals are updated based on the majority of the contributors using in their forecasts. The actuals which are updated on our product might be different from the press release because of the majority of the contributors might use different numbers in their forecasts 2.  Are the EPS estimates GAAP EPS or Pro Forma EPS? The EPS estimate might be EPS GAAP as well as Proforma. This is purely based on the majority of the contributing analyst. If the majority of the broker provide estimates on GAAP basis the we update EPS on GAAP (reported), but if the majority of the broker are providing their estimates based on Proforma then we update the EPS estimate based on Proforma basis. 3.  Gross Margin estimates (Annual and Interim) for this company do not start until almost two years after the DS base date.  Is this common?  Is there a reason to not expect estimates data until then?  Or is this just a gap in the data. It is common for estimates of a certain type or all types to be unavailable for periods of time.  None of the analysts covering the stocks were providing Gross Margin Estimates during the periods. The gross margin is a new measure which we have started collecting off late. 4.  Are P/S ratio (Price to Sales ratio) estimates available through IBES? There is no P/S ratio estimate available through IBES. 5.  Update frequency I/B/E/S monthly values are updated at the latest by close of business (EST) on  the  Tuesday following the third Friday of the month. The monthly update overwrites all previous monthly values and adds the latest month’s values. The monthly update is a snapshot taken on the Thursday preceding the third Friday of every month at close of business in New York Sample or additional information (including cross references) Type: Data and Statistics Type: Data and Statistics: Equity Market Data Type: Data and Statistics: Exchange Rates Type: Data and Statistics: Financial Data Type: Data and Statistics: Fixed Income Data Type: Data and Statistics: Forecast Data Practice Area: Antitrust Practice Area: Financial Institutions Practice Area: Health Care Practice Area: Securities Subject: Fixed Income Resources Subject: International Information

The most commonly requested datatypes are: EPS Sales / Revenue Long Term Growth (LTG) Recommendations (buy/hold/sell) Price Targets EBITDA EBIT Cash Flow IBES contains over 3,000 datatypes.  A summary of IBES forecast categories is available for consensus data . This document contains the list of available measures for detailed data .  See page 10. Basic or Diluted EPS? Thomson Financial determines whether a company is followed on basic versus diluted shares based on the majority rule. If a contributor is on the minority basis, the estimate is filtered and excluded from the mean calculation. Explanation of the methodology that Thomson uses to define Earnings Per Share (EPS) Majority Policy Most institutional clients prefer to view estimates on an “operating” basis, reflecting the majority of the analysts covering a security. Consequently, Thomson Reuters follows a ‘majority’ policy, where the accounting basis of each company estimate is determined by the basis used by the majority of contributing analysts. Once the majority basis has been established, contributing analysts in the minority may keep their original estimates, or are also given the opportunity to adjust to the majority basis. On rare occasions, the majority basis may be revised as additional analysts are heard from or as some change their opinion. In all cases, appropriate footnotes are added to the Thomson Reuters database stating the appropriate basis of each estimate, and if the item has been included or excluded from the mean estimate. Please note that as each quarter is treated independently of each year, any exclusion from a given quarter would result in an exclusion from the annual estimate Example: Q1 Included Q2 Excluded, minority basis Q3 Included Q4 Included FY Excluded, due to Q2 exclusion When submitting estimates, contributors are encouraged to include or exclude any non-extraordinary items they deem non-recurring and/or non-operating. Once a non-extraordinary or non-operating item is recognized, a Thomson Reuters Market Specialist will poll all contributors’ estimates covering a particular company, to establish if the majority of them are including or excluding the event. If there is no clear majority, then the charge or gain is included in the mean. If at any point the majority basis cannot be determined, the Thomson Reuters Market Specialist will further research the affected estimates, including potentially contacting the contributing analysts, to determine the majority basis. Footnotes are attached to estimates to alert clients as well as Thomson Reuters Market Specialists of special actions or situations affecting estimates. Update frequency I/B/E/S monthly values are updated at the latest by close of business (EST) on  the  Tuesday following the third Friday of the month. The monthly update overwrites all previous monthly values and adds the latest month’s values. On rare occasions, the majority basis may be revised as additional analysts are heard from or as some change their opinion. In all cases, appropriate footnotes are added to the Thomson Reuters database stating the appropriate basis of each estimate, and if the item has been included or excluded from the mean estimate.
Please note that as each quarter is treated independently of each year, any exclusion from a given quarter would result in an exclusion from the annual estimate
FY Excluded, due to Q2 exclusion

When submitting estimates, contributors are encouraged to include or exclude any non-extraordinary items they deem non-recurring and/or non-operating. Once a non-extraordinary or non-operating item is recognized, a Thomson Reuters Market Specialist will poll all contributors’ estimates covering a particular company, to establish if the majority of them are including or excluding the event. If there is no clear majority, then the charge or gain is included in the mean. If at any point the majority basis cannot be determined, the Thomson Reuters Market Specialist will further research the affected estimates, including potentially contacting the contributing analysts, to determine the majority basis.
Footnotes are attached to estimates to alert clients as well as Thomson Reuters Market Specialists of special actions or situations affecting estimates.

I/B/E/S monthly values are updated at the latest by close of business (EST) on  the  Tuesdayfollowing the third Friday of the month. The monthly update overwrites all previous monthly valuesand adds the latest month’s values. The monthly update is a snapshot taken on the Thursdaypreceding the third Friday of every month at close of business in New York

page_124.body_text: Daubert Tracker Source Daubert Tracker https://dauberttracker.com/index.cfm How to Cite the Source Daubert Tracker Description Daubert Tracker provides access to information associated with reported and unreported "evidentiary gatekeeping" cases. The database tracks cases from both federal and state jurisdictions going back to 1993 and is updated daily. In addition to monitoring the Daubert Trilogy, the product also tracks cases which reference state and federal rules of evidence pertaining to "gatekeeping" and cases considered to be the seminal "gatekeeping" cases from each state jurisdiction. Daubert Hearing History The U.S. Supreme Court decisions in Daubert v. Merrell Dow Pharmaceuticals 509 U.S. 579 (1993) and its progeny, Kumho Tire v. Carmichael 526 U.S. 137 (1999) and General Electric v. Joiner 522 U.S. 136 (1997) , govern the admissibility of expert testimony in the federal courts, so the federal courts use these cases (known as the "Daubert Trilogy") to assess (a) whether an expert is qualified, and (b) whether the techniques the expert utilizes are sound. List of Gatekeeping Authorities The Daubert Tracker monitors, analyzes and catalogs all reported and numerous unreported "Gatekeeping" decisions from both federal and state jurisdictions. A "Gatekeeping" decision is defined as any decision when a) one of the cases and/or rules of evidence on the list has been cited or mentioned and b) a testifying expert's methodology or qualifications has been challenged. and trade publications indexed and abstracted, 2,900 of them provide full 
text. On the EBSCOHost main page, there are three searching interfaces to choose from: EBSCOHost This is the standard interface for EBSCO. Information Resources usually starts with the next option. The Business Searching Interface is a completely separate user experience from the typical EBSCOhost experience. This is IR's preferred interface Tutorial for Business Searching Interface Business Book Summaries Business Book Summaries® (BBS) provides comprehensive, yet concise summaries of the best business books available. This database also contains many non-English full-text journals in economics and finance. Volume and issue browsing is available for all full-text journals. EconLit adheres to the high quality standards long recognized by subscribers to the Journal of Economic Literature (JEL) and is a reliable source of citations and abstracts to economic research dating back to 1886. It provides links to full-text articles in all fields of economics, including capital markets, country studies, econometrics, economic forecasting, environmental economics, government regulations, labor economics, monetary theory, urban economics, and much more. EconLit uses the JEL classification system and controlled vocabulary of keywords to index six types of records: journal articles, books, collective volume articles, dissertations, working papers, and full-text book reviews from the Journal of Economic Literature. End users can immediately access the full text of the web content, by following the link in the record. The index to the full text content in EBSCO Newswires is held for a rolling 30-day archive by EBSCO, so users can enjoy the previous 30 days of news relating to their search interests. Web News EBSCO's Web News provides near real-time access to thousands of top news feeds from around the globe. This collection includes over 14,000 feeds covering a range of business and general news topics. End users can immediately access the full text of the web content, by following the link in the record. page_137.body_text: EconLit Source EconLit How to Cite the Source American Economic Association Description EconLit EconLit is an authoritative index from the American Economic Association that serves as a reliable source for economic research citations and abstracts. Adhering to the high-quality standards long recognized by subscribers to the Journal of Economic Literature (JEL), this index covers more than 1.5 million records, including abstracts and citations dating back to 1886, and content drawn from dozens of countries. Indexed content includes peer-reviewed journal articles, working papers, books, conference proceedings, and other materials, covering a wide range of economic subjects including capital markets, econometrics, economic forecasting, labor economics, and many others. EconLit with Full Text EconLit with Full Text is the most reliable full-text database for economic research, and an authoritative resource for economic literature. It offers hundreds of full-text journals, including the American Economic Association journals with no embargo. It also contains all of the indexing in EconLit, which adheres to the high-quality JEL classification system for economics literature. In addition to this indexing, EconLit with Full Text also includes full-text articles from nearly 400 peer-reviewed journals and over a dozen full-text books. This content covers a wide range of topics in economics, including econometrics, monetary theory, labor economics, urban economics, environmental economics, and many other areas. Since many of the full-text journals are unique to the database, EconLit with Full Text is an excellent complement to Business Source Ultimate. It also contains many non-English full-text journals. Volume and issue browsing is available for all full-text journals. Time Period Covered With a rich collection of over 1.5 million records dating back to 1886, it encompasses a diverse array of economic subjects, including capital markets, labor economics, and econometrics. Access EconLit, the economics research database produced by the American Economic Association (AEA), is available on three platforms—EBSCO, ProQuest, and Ovid—each containing the same data but with slightly different user interfaces. All EconLit providers offer the capability of linking records to full text, dependent on the library's holdings. In addition, there is a version of EconLit bundled with full-text subscriptions, EconLit with Full Text, which is available only through EBSCO. Contact: https://www.aeaweb.org/econlit/access Cost All pricing is supplied directly from the platform providers Important Notes AI Restrictions AI Definitions/Capabilities Updated 09/24/2025_rk ​

page_138.body_text: EDGAR Source EDGAR (Electronic Data Gathering, Analysis, and Retrieval system) How to Cite the Source SEC.gov Description EDGAR, the Electronic Data Gathering, Analysis, and Retrieval system, is the primary system for companies and others submitting documents under the Securities Act of 1933, the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, the Trust Indenture Act of 1939, and the Investment Company Act of 1940. EDGAR provides free public access to corporate information, allowing one to research a public company's financial information and operations by reviewing the filings the company makes with the SEC. One can also research information provided by mutual funds (including money market funds), exchange-traded funds (ETFs), and variable annuities. Links to helpful pages: https://www.sec.gov/search-filings https://www.sec.gov/search-filings/edgar-search-assistance/accessing-edgar-data https://www.sec.gov/submit-filings/about-edgar https://www.sec.gov/search-filings/edgar-search-assistance/using-edgar-research-investments Time Period Covered EDGAR started in 1994/1995. Paper copies of filing documents prior to 1994 may be available by filing a Freedom of Information Act request. Or Information Resources might be able to get/request them from other databases. Access Freely available at https://www.sec.gov/edgar/search/ Contact: n/a Cost Free Important Notes Timestamps are EST and indicate the time at which the submission was accepted by EDGAR. There is no timestamp to indicate when filing content is first available on sec.gov. SEC reserves the right to block IP addresses that submit excessive requests. Current guidelines limit users to a total of no more than 10 requests per second, regardless of the number of machines used to submit requests. Any request that has been identified as part of a botnet or an automated tool outside of the acceptable policy will be managed to ensure fair access for all users. Information presented on sec.gov is considered public information and may be copied or further distributed by users of the web site without the SEC's permission. Please consider appropriate citation to the SEC as the source. Videos, social media posts, and other educational materials on sec.gov are printed, published, or produced and disseminated at U.S. taxpayer expense. Please do not use the SEC seal or any of the other logos or artwork from this site. SIC (Standard Industrial Classification) codes are not necessarily assigned by SEC. Generally, organizations choose their own based on their primary business line. https://www.naics.com/ufaq/who-assigns-sic-codes-to-businesses-and-how/ https://www.sec.gov/search-filings/standard-industrial-classification-sic-code-list AI Restrictions ​ AI Definitions/Capabilities ​ Updated 11/4/25_hg

page_140.body_text: eMaxx Source eMAXX How to Cite the Source eMAXX Description eMAXX covers over $7 trillion of total fixed income holdings, over 500,000 individual fixed income securities, holdings of over 7,000 buy-side firms including nearly 19,000 mutual funds, insurance companies, and top pensions funds globally across 33 countries. In line with the Lipper® global research and analyst teams, the data reported to eMAXX has three sources: Pension funds Mutual funds Insurance companies (only US insurance companies report trade data) The firms and professional information contained within the profiles content dataset includes, without limitation, from the sources within the public domain, including, without limitation, websites, publications, etc., a data subject, individuals, or companies within the financial and investment services industry and/or employers who wish to have the business/professional information (including business related personal information) of their personnel listed within or on the profiles content dataset. Some eMAXX data is available in Workspace, including terms and conditions and price histories of inactive bonds and most recent ownership data of active bonds. The eMAXX app (EMAXXOWN) provides access to bondholding information, institutional investor profiles, and contacts. This includes details of managing firm and fund ownership, portfolio composition, and institutional investor contact information. The information is updated based on sources collected from regulatory websites, fund management company (FMC) websites, and direct submissions from FMCs. Historical bond holdings data is available through the eMAXX FTP feed, which is different from the eMAXX Bond holders (EMAXXBH) app in Workspace and requires a separate subscription. Bond holdings has information on the companies that hold: A bond issue for government and corporate bonds Mortgage-backed securities Securitized debt US municipal bonds Included in bond holdings data: Report Date - date on which information was acquired Managing firm - this is the firm managing part of the bond or holder of the bond Par held (in 1000 USD) - the amount of the bonds (in USD) managed by the holder %par outstanding - the percentage of the total amount outstanding that the holder manages Bond holdings data is only available if the managing firms provide Refinitiv the rights to publish the data. Time Period Covered ~1989 to present. Historical data is available via a feed, which is delivered via FTP. Access Some data is available using premium login for Workspace; most historical data requires a separate subscription Contact: #Information Resources Cost Through Workspace, cost is $100 per login (capped at $1,000 per month); IR would need to get a cost estimate for access to the historical data feed Important Notes AI Restrictions ​ AI Definitions/Capabilities ​ Updated 3/25/26_hg

page_155.body_text: Tick History (DataScope) Source ​Tick History (Datascope) How to Cite the Source ​Refinitiv Description Tick History is an archive of historical tick data drawn from our real time content. It’s built on a platform that provides on-demand delivery of our universe of 70m active and retired securities. It comes with a web based user interface, and a REST API providing efficient programmatic access to the full content and capabilities of the product. Tick History covers OTC and exchange-traded instruments, from more than 500 trading venues and third-party contributors. It gives users access to historical tick-level global data across all asset classes, letting them build and back-test trading strategies, as well as perform quantitative research and analysis, transaction cost analysis, and market surveillance. Data coverage goes back as far as 1996, with a standardized naming convention based on RIC (Reuters Instrument Code) symbology that helps lower your data management cost. The perpetual model is essentially a onetime purchase. Client provides list of instruments, start and end date, fields, frequency and for a one-time fee, we provide a file for you to purchase with a perpetual right to use that data. The subscription model allows a client to subscribe to the service for a minimum of 1 year. You would have access to the front end gui and API with all history for XAU= going back to 1996. You would also be able to access all fields and all frequencies (full tick, minute, 5 minute, etc.). Include Gena Rosati or Laura Londa in any communications and purchases Sample or additional information (including cross references) ​ ​

page_159.body_text: Execucomp (Now Part Of S&P ) Source ExecuComp How to Cite the Source S&P ExecuComp Description S&P's executive compensation database can be used to identify company trends and industry peers. ExecuComp provides details on executive stock and option awards as well as pension plans to give you the full compensation picture. Selected company financials helps you compare executive pay to company performance. The ExecuComp database includes detailed breakouts of compensation data under the pre-2006 reporting rules so that you can research historical compensation trends. The ExecuComp database is released 6 times per year: January, March, April, May, June, and October. ExecuComp data is also available using the S&P Market Intelligence Professionals data set, which profiles professionals with current and prior board/company affiliations. Execucomp's data is a subset of the data available via the Professionals data feed.  The two databases have different naming conventions and organization, so mapping data variables between this is incredibly difficult. If you are replicating ExecuComp data, use the ExecuComp database, not Professionals.  Data includes biographies, standardized job functions, titles, education, compensation, options holdings, and full committee memberships. The People Basic SME data offering provides Professional data for private companies that do not file financials. The People Basic SME data is typically collected directly from the private company or through local company registries. The data points for People Basic SME include private company professionals metadata, inclusive of first and last name, gender year born, titles, unique person identifiers, job functions as reported, and flags indicating current or past board affiliations. Features: Covers more than 4.5 million professionals Compensation history going back to 1992 Over 40 different compensation types Gain insight on an individual's career history and professional relationships with current and prior information integrated into profiles of public and private company executives, board members, and investment professionals, globally Research individuals based on biography, contact data, education, compensation, affiliations, and corporate board membership information Make associations with a person's professional past, aligning a person's experience and relationships with your specific needs Focus on key decision makers, and not rank-and-file employees View committee membership details for board members and executives Evaluate the compensation of the chief executive officer (CEO) There is data on US and International companies (if the company files a proxy statement, there will be data.) Execucomp Professionals Database User Guide.pdf Execucomp Professionals Data Guide.xlsx exec_defs.doc Time Period Covered Compensation history back to 1992 Access Case teams must subscribe for access. Contact #Information Resources for more information Contact: Please contact #Information Resources for all inquiries Cost In 2024, the cost was $20,000 for 1 year of access for 3 users (we will need to get updated cost estimates for all new requests) Important Notes Delivery methods: XpressFeed (FTP File Transfer): This is our traditional data delivery method where your data team will install our proprietary software to receive the full dataset in a file via FTP (~30GB). This is the most common option used by our clients that are not using or interested in using Snowflake (cloud delivery). Whenever there are updates to the dataset (up to once per day), S&P will send you a "change file" with only the changes to the dataset where you will use that to update your dataset. Snowflake (Cloud Delivery): This option utilizes our partnership with Snowflake to deliver and store S&P data to you via cloud. With this option, you would incur the storage and compute costs necessary to power your queries, but clients usually find the pros of this delivery method outweigh the con of additional cost. For 30GB of data and relatively infrequent queries, I'd be surprised if you even paid $100 per year in snowflake fees. As I mentioned on our call, even if you don't have a current relationship with Snowflake, we can still leverage this delivery method through S&P paperwork through our partnership. With this option, you would access the data through a Snowflake portal (via web browser) and would require no "change files" to be managed by your team (we would handle that through Snowflake). You can read more about snowflake here: https://www.snowflake.com/en/why-snowflake/ We have access to some Execucomp data in Capital IQ. However, you need to pull the data by individual company.  It you want to pull large data pulls of executive data, you would need to subscribe to the product. AI Restrictions ​ AI Definitions/Capabilities ​ Updated 8/10/2026_hg

page_165.body_text: ​Factiva Source Factiva How to Cite the Source Cite the publication of the article, e.g., Reuters News or the Washington Post Description Factiva provides full-text access to more than 18,000 licensed sources, including the Wall Street Journal, Dow Jones Newswire, Reuters, company press releases, hundreds of national and regional publications, and general business, trade and industry publications. While Factiva does not include all news sources (no database does), it is Cornerstone's best database for news content analysis because it has so many sources, the cost is low, and we can output headlines and articles in useful formats. We have two access points: Factiva.com and FDK (Factiva Developers Kit), Cornerstone's bespoke Excel formats for headlines and text/Word formats can only be accessed using FDK. In Factiva.com, we can see all source types but can only download a maximum of 100 items at once. Headlines can only be output to Word or PDF (Excel is not an option). For Web News, Blogs, and Pictures, Factiva provides only a link to the website where the content is because they do not license this content (so full text is not available through Factiva). We use FDK for downloading headlines and can download up to 10,000 headlines in Excel and about 260 full text articles (due to text box character size limitations). We have various pre-set groups of publications. For more information on these groups, please see our FAQs starting here . We don't include web, blog and other non-text sources in FDK searches because they are not actually available in full text and are only available for 90 days. Timestamps: Most of the wire services provide time stamps for articles. Headlines are timestamped in ET and full text articles are timestamped in GMT (please note that LexisNexis AI News Metabase API's timestamps are in UTC and we only download articles, not headlines). For more information about the inconsistencies and idiosyncrasies involved with timestamps, please read our 6-page document explaining all the variances and issues with timestamps in Factiva, Reuters and others: What you REALLY need to know about Time Stamps in Factiva.docx Foreign languages: Factiva includes publications in 27 non-English languages. If the language uses lettering that requires a special keyboard or font software (Japanese, Chinese, etc.), someone will need to type the search terms in the foreign language and e-mail them to IR. Then the search terms can be cut and pasted into the Factiva search text box. The results will have to be downloaded in PDF rather than TXT or DOC format. Time Period Covered Varies significantly by source. Some publications go back to 1977. page_167.body_text: ​Timestamp Issues Known issues with timestamps in Factiva Some case team members discovered a few unusual inconsistencies with the timestamps of some articles downloaded from Factiva. While researching these few articles, more and more inconsistencies surfaced. These issues resulted in a month-long investigation by IR into how timestamps are assigned, where they come from and different publishers’ methods for dealing with updates and corrections. We talked directly to Factiva developers, and Dow Jones’ and Reuters’ content managers to finally determine how timestamps worked. Click here for a 6-page document we created to explain all the variances and issues with timestamps in Factiva, Reuters and others. The first page is an executive summary of the main points, and the rest goes into much detail regarding these points and some others. If the cases that you work on rely on the timestamps pulled from Factiva, you should try to find some time to go through this document as you may have to make some changes to how you use timestamps and what you assume about them. (LLL 6-12-14)

page_172.body_text: ​Fed in Print Source Fed in Print How to Cite the Source Cite by publication Description Fed-in-Print is the central catalog of publications within the Federal Reserve System. It is managed and hosted by the Economic Research Division , Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis . This database provides access to research published by the Board of Governors and all 12 Federal Reserve Banks. Coverage includes the core economic reviews, as well as specialized regional and international publications, working papers, and annual report essays.  Also included are selected speeches, community development publications, and conference papers. Fed in Print has its roots in the 1960s, when the librarians at the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia began compiling and publishing an index to the Federal Reserve Bulletin and each Reserve Bank's economic review.  In 1996, the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco introduced Fed in Print as a web-based, searchable index.  The print version ceased publication in 2000.  It has been managed and hosted by the Economic Research Division of the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis since 2013. Librarians throughout the Federal Reserve System contribute to the content.  As older publications are made available in full-text, they are added to the index.  Our aim is to make the database a vital tool for researchers, students, and all those interested in economics, finance, banking, and community development. Time Period Covered 1960s -- present Access https://www.fedinprint.org/ Contact: Cost free Important Notes AI Restrictions ​ AI Definitions/Capabilities ​ Updated 10/9/2025_aig

page_176.body_text: ​FedFis Source FedFis How to Cite the Source FedFis© or www.FedFis.com Description FedFis is the most comprehensive source for U.S. Financial Institution data. 10 years of quarterly historical time periods and over 5,000 precision data items for all U.S Financial Institutions. Precision Data Many State and Federal Regulators use FedFis. Our precision data matches up to the exact specifications used by the regulatory bodies for analysis of financial institutions. Non-Precision Data We also create specific metrics to meet our client's needs. Using algorithms, we can create high-level KPI metrics to better quantify your Ideal Customer Profile (ICP). Solving your problems is our main objective. All non-precision data is clearly marked so that the end user knows it is an analytical estimate. Real-Time Data FedFis data is captured in real-time across all verticals as each institution files. 40 quarters of full Financial Statements, Performance Ratios, and Bank Ratings. We ensure the highest level of speed and precision. Quarterly Data Capture Bank, Credit Union, and Holding Company data is captured within seconds of each institution filing their quarterly call reports. This collection process includes providing the newly calculated supplementary metrics such as performance ratios, peer rankings, and ratings. Historical Amendment Capture Periodically, institutions are required to file an amendment to a past call report. To guarantee data accuracy, FedFis captures all current and historical amendments on a daily basis. Daily Data Capture & News Several data segments offered through FedFis require updates on a daily basis: M&A Deals Capturing all M&A announcements is only half the battle. We complete the process by calculating all pricing metrics, specifying transaction details, and populating financials for each Financial Institution involved in the transaction. SEC Pricing For all publicly traded banking companies, we provide daily updates to stock price and the supplementary pricing and valuation ratios derived from the daily stock price. This is in addition to the quarterly filed SEC statement and pricing records. Branch Ownership Changes Bank and Credit Union branch deposit data is only filed annually. However, the ownership of a branch can change at any time, thus modifying the market share an institution has in a particular market. The end-user has the option to view "As Reported" or "As New Ownership" when selecting a market to analyze. Training Videos: Included is a quick guide to generate reports, along with short videos below on navigating the web portal: How to Generate Bank Profile Reports (2 min) How to Change Data Item Display (Columns) (4 min) How to Create Lists, Queries, & Peer Groups (9 min) Time Period Covered Goes back at least 10 years Access Please follow the instructions below to create your FedFis UI account: 1)      Go to https://fisweb.fedfis.com in your browser. 2)      Click the signup link to create your account.  Please make note of your password. 3)      Enter the company name: Cornerstone Research  *Must be exact 4)      FedFis will validate access within 1-2 minutes 5)      Save/bookmark https://fisweb.fedfis.com to access at anytime Contact: Training & Service Support Contact Dan Heilveil – VP, Relationship Management Phone: (512) 395-4502 Email: dheilveil@fedfis.com Technical Support Contact Krissa Coffin – Product Manager Phone: (682) 218-1006 Email: kcoffin@fedfis.com Cost No charge associated with the use of this database. Many State and Federal Regulators use FedFis. Our precision data matches up to the exact specifications used by the regulatory bodies for analysis of financial institutions.

We also create specific metrics to meet our client's needs. Using algorithms, we can create high-level KPI metrics to better quantify your Ideal Customer Profile (ICP). Solving your problems is our main objective. All non-precision data is clearly marked so that the end user knows it is an analytical estimate.

FedFis data is captured in real-time across all verticals as each institution files. 40 quarters of full Financial Statements, Performance Ratios, and Bank Ratings. We ensure the highest level of speed and precision.

Bank, Credit Union, and Holding Company data is captured within seconds of each institution filing their quarterly call reports. This collection process includes providing the newly calculated supplementary metrics such as performance ratios, peer rankings, and ratings.
Periodically, institutions are required to file an amendment to a past call report. To guarantee data accuracy, FedFis captures all current and historical amendments on a daily basis.
Several data segments offered through FedFis require updates on a daily basis:

Capturing all M&A announcements is only half the battle. We complete the process by calculating all pricing metrics, specifying transaction details, and populating financials for each Financial Institution involved in the transaction.

For all publicly traded banking companies, we provide daily updates to stock price and the supplementary pricing and valuation ratios derived from the daily stock price. This is in addition to the quarterly filed SEC statement and pricing records.

Bank and Credit Union branch deposit data is only filed annually. However, the ownership of a branch can change at any time, thus modifying the market share an institution has in a particular market. The end-user has the option to view "As Reported" or "As New Ownership" when selecting a market to analyze.

page_179.body_text: ​Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) Source Financial Accounting Standards Board How to Cite the Source Financial Accounting Standards Board Description Since 1973, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) has been the designated organization in the private sector for establishing standards of financial accounting. Those standards govern the preparation of financial statements. They are officially recognized as authoritative by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) (Financial Reporting Release No. 1, Section 101, and reaffirmed in its April 2003 Policy Statement) and the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (Rule 203, Rules of Professional Conduct, as amended May 1973 and May 1979). Such standards are important to the efficient functioning of the economy because investors, creditors, auditors, and others rely on credible, transparent, and comparable financial information. The SEC has statutory authority to establish financial accounting and reporting standards for publicly held companies under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. Throughout its history, however, the Commission’s policy has been to rely on the private sector for this function to the extent that the private sector demonstrates ability to fulfill the responsibility in the public interest. FINRA TRACE reports all transaction prices in TRACE-eligible bonds (investment grade, high yield and convertible corporate debt) - representing all over-the-counter market activity in these bonds. All prices in TRACE are transaction prices, not matrix prices. No data on Muni bonds is available. Enhanced Historic Time and Sales Trade Record File Layout . These charts and graphs and raw data may be shared with clients and other parties as required by the courts or regulatory agencies. 2. Cornerstone's use is considered commercial FINRA TRACE Fact Book Quarterly and annual aggregated OTC bond market trade statistics 3. Bloomberg Data License Request Builder Data Sources on Bloomberg (ALLQ) should be set to TRAC. A maximum of 240 trading days of tick data is available through Bloomberg. There is a limit of 20 million individual ticks. Cost $0 Contact (within CR or Vendor) For data we currently have, contact #Data Science Center and cc Phuong Dinh in DAPG ( pdinh@cornerstone.com ) FINRA: 1-888-507-3665 http://www.finra.org/AboutFINRA/ContactFINRA/index.htm TRACE: 1-866-776-0800 Trace Data Services < TraceDataServices@finra.org > Cornerstone Comments IMPORTANT: Please refer to this Guide to Trace Data , which was created by the F/FI Practice. TRACE started disseminating bond data in July 2002, but this was done in phases: During Phase I, effective on July 1, 2002, public transaction information was disseminated immediately upon receipt for the larger and generally higher-credit quality issues: (1) Investment Grade debt securities having an initial issue of $1 billion or greater; and (2) 50 Non-Investment Grade (High-Yield) securities disseminated under FIPS2 that were transferred to TRACE. Under these criteria, NASD disseminated information on approximately 520 securities by the end of 2002. Phase II, fully effective on April 14, 2003, expanded public dissemination to include transactions in smaller Investment Grade issues: (1) all Investment Grade TRACE-eligible securities of at least $100 million par value (original issue size) or greater rated A3/A- or higher; and (2) a group of 120 Investment Grade TRACE-eligible securities rated Baa/BBB and 50 Non-Investment Grade bonds. As Phase II was implemented, the number of disseminated bonds increased to approximately 4,650 bonds. In Phase III, fully effective on February 7, 2005, approximately 99% of all public transactions and 95% of par value in the TRACE-eligible securities market were disseminated immediately upon receipt. Most transactions were disseminated immediately upon their receipt by the TRACE System, although transactions over $1 million in certain infrequently traded Non-Investment Grade securities were subject to dissemination delays, as were certain transactions immediately following the offering of TRACE-eligible securities rated BBB or below. Since January 9, 2006, all transactions in public TRACE-eligible securities have been disseminated immediately upon receipt. NASD continues to monitor the effects of transparency on the part of the market made up of TRACE-eligible securities. How can I find the total par amount for all TRACE-eligible corporate bonds traded in a calendar year? The annual FINRA TRACE Fact Book contains "Transaction Information" data tables that will alow you to calculate this sum. To get the total par value traded (investment grade, high yield, convertible investment grade, and convertible high-yield combined), add the total par value amounts from tables 22, 23, 24, and 25. answer provided by Alie Diagne , - Trace Data Services How can I find the total par amount of all "Institutional" size trades and the par amount of all "retail" size trades in a calendar year? The annual FINRA TRACE Fact Book contains "Transaction Information" data tables that will alow you to calculate this sum.  For the retail size trades, add the par value amounts for trades <100 in table 22, 23, 24, and 25.  For institutional size trades, you will have to add the par value amounts for the remaining sizes (anything >100) in the same tables. answer provided by Alie Diagne - Trace Data Services

page_184.body_text: ​FOCUS Reports 1. What is a FOCUS report? 1.1. Schedule I 1.2. Part I 1.3. Part II 1.4. Part IIA 1.5. Part IIB 1.6. Part III 2. Are FOCUS reports publicly available? What is a FOCUS report? The Financial and Operational Combined Uniform Single (FOCUS) Report is a category of regulatory filings that registered broker-dealers are required to file with the SEC and with their designated examining authority (FINRA, NYSE, CBOE, etc).  There are several parts of the FOCUS report that are filed periodically.  All the FOCUS report forms begin with X-17A-5 , in reference to SEC rule 240.17a-5 Reports to be made by certain brokers and dealers . Schedule I Schedule I requires the reporting of general information designed to measure certain economic and financial characteristics of the registrant. Schedule I of Form X-17A-5 is a calendar year unconsolidated report to be filed by all registrants either as a supplement to the regular fourth quarter Part II of Form X-17A-5 within seventeen business days of the end of the third quarter. Part I Every broker or dealer who clears or carries customer accounts shall file Part I of Form X–17A–5 within 10 business days after the end of each month. Part II Every broker or dealer who clears transactions or carries customer accounts shall file Part II of Form X–17A–5 (§249.617 of this chapter) within 17 business days after the end of the calendar quarter and within 17 business days after the date selected for the annual audit of financial statements where said date is other than a calendar quarter. Certain of such brokers or dealers shall file Part IIA in lieu of Part II if the nature of their business is limited as described in the instructions to Part II of Form X–17A–5 (§249.617 of this chapter). Part IIA Every broker or dealer who does not carry nor clear transactions nor carry customer accounts shall file Part IIA of Form X–17A–5 (§249.617 of this chapter) within 17 business days after the end of each calendar quarter and within 17 business days after the date selected for the annual audit of financial statements where said date is other than the end of the calendar quarter. Part IIB Part IIB constitutes the basic financial and operational report required of OTC derivatives dealers. Much of the information required by the FOCUS report is the same or similar to the information required to be reported by broker-dealers required to file Form X-17A-5 Part II. Consequently, for those items that appear on both forms, the instructions for X-17A-5 Part II are to be followed when completing Form X-17A-5 Part IIB. The instructions apply to new information requests and to items appearing on both forms that have been altered to better reflect an OTC derivatives dealer’s unique business. Part III Part III is a cover-sheet like document used to identify annual audit reports. The form must be completed and attached to the front of each copy of the audited financial statements. The form contains space for a firm’s name and address, the name and address of the firm's accountant, the oath or affirmation, and a checklist of items included in the report. Are FOCUS reports publicly available? The reports are available from the SEC but as they are still submitted to the SEC in paper form, they are not available electronically.  These documents can be ordered through the SEC FOIA/Privacy Act Office .  2009 FOIA requests had a median processing time of 6 days.  Also, filers may request confidential treatment of annual audited financial statements in accordance with Rule 17a-5(e)3 so some information may be redacted or unavailable via FOIA.
