Fixed Income Resources 1.1. Fixed Income Databases 1.2. Fixed Income Government Sites 1.3. Fixed Income Internet Resources 1.4. Fixed Income Journals Fixed Income Databases : ABSNet Bloomberg (access through the Bloomberg terminals) Information on corporate and government bonds. The Corporate Bond Indexes are comprised of the "active" (most frequently traded) fixed coupon bonds represented by NASD TRACE, NASD's transaction reporting facility that disseminates all over-the-counter secondary market transactions in these public bonds. There are also Key Rates for Federal Reserve, Prime Rate, LIBOR, banking, and mortgages. http://www.finra.org/Industry/Regulation/Notices/2009/P118710 . If TRACE data is not available for a public bond on a given date, the bond did not trade. Bloomberg also calculates a BGN quote based on publicly available data and Bloomberg’s proprietary methodology. When downloading data in the Data License at the Bloomberg terminal, type in the source (BGN or TRAC) under the "Source" field. Normally, TRACE data is always preferred to BGN pricing. Transaction level details can possibly be used to serve as a gauge for volume reduction in a fixed income securities damages case. (Note: This data has not been used in a case as of July 2010.) Reporting Party Side (RPS) codes are the following: Bond pricing is FTI/Interactive Data data, which is a combination of actual pricing and modeled pricing (methodology is attached). For defaulted securities, the pricing seems unreliable after the default date. Note that FTI/Interactive Data pricing is available through S&P Capital IQ. : Bond pricing is FTI/Interactive Data data, which is a combination of actual pricing and modeled pricing (methodology is attached). For defaulted securities, the pricing seems unreliable after the default date. Public bond data is available through NASD TRACE, NASD’s transaction reporting facility that disseminates all over-the-counter secondary market transactions. TRACE is based on actual transaction data for TRACE eligible securities. Transaction level details are also available in Bloomberg’s Excel API. This is disabled, so if this information is required, please contact our Bloomberg representatives and Paul Schibell ((212) 617-2927. -B: A customer transaction where the dealer purchases securities from the customer. -S: A customer transaction where the dealer sells securities to the customer. -D: An inter-dealer transaction (always from the sell side). RPS codes and other tick level data are available for the prior 240 days. BondsOnline Bond pricing is FTI/Interactive Data data, which is a combination of actual pricing and modeled pricing (methodology is attached). For defaulted securities, the pricing seems unreliable after the default date. Note that FTI/Interactive Data pricing is available through Capital IQ. S&P Capital IQ Bond pricing is FTI/Interactive Data data, which is a combination of actual pricing and modeled pricing (methodology is attached). For defaulted securities, the pricing seems unreliable after the default date. Center for Research in Security Prices (CRSP) (access from the Portal page under Library Data Sources is for EQUITY only). CRSP Government Bond Indices: monthly and daily; CRSP Government Bond monthly Riskfree Rates; CRSP Fama-Bliss Discount Bond prices and yields. Also useful: Don Cram's Data Access and Analysis Page links to information about CRSP from various sources.(Cornerstone has access only to stocks and mutual fund data.) Datastream Contains historical, global coverage of equities, stock markets, commodities, futures, currencies, options, bond markets, company financials, and economic data. Datastream has Over 30,000 third-party bond indices, among them: JPMorgan, Citigroup, Lehman Brothers, Merrill Lynch, iBoxx and MSCI, with constituents lists available for all JPMorgan and iBoxx indices including historical lists for the JPMorgan Eurozone indices. Government Bond indices, calculated following industry standard methodology, for all major bond markets with extensive historical data and covering a wide range of calculations. In addition, Datastream has over 100,000 fixed-income instruments and over 200,000 warrants, certificates and convertibles covering 32 markets. For each bond, there are up to 200 terms and conditions items attached, as well as full historical price and volume details.  There is access to a unique database of over 800,000 redeemed fixed-income securities and warrants. Dealscan A comprehensive and reliable database for global loan, high-yield bond and private placement data terms and conditions on over 100,000 transactions dating back to 1986. Approximately 250 new transactions are added weekly to the database. eMAXX™ Reuters It combines essential fixed income ownership and institutional investor profile data. Factiva Quotes (this is no longer available to anyone outside IR staff) Prices for below investment grade bonds are available in Quotes under Historical Corporate Bonds U.S. market only).  Prices are provided by SunGard PowerData only. For Historical Corporate Bonds, Unit Trusts, and U.S. Government Debt, coverage is retained for only 6 years after the issue has expired or is retired. Pricing data is available for liquid bonds. If the bond does not have much pricing data in TRACE, pricing data will be limited/unavailable in Thomson databases. There is no liquidity "cut-off". Bond pricing is FTI/Interactive Data data, which is a combination of actual pricing and modeled pricing (methodology is attached). For defaulted securities, the pricing seems unreliable after the default date. Note that FTI/Interactive Data pricing is available through Capital IQ. Historical Corporate Bonds, covering data for the United States only, contains two types of bond pricing: 1) Exchange History Pricing - historical pricing based on the listed exchange for that bond. Pricing history includes: date, high, low and close values. 2) Dealer Priced Bonds - unlisted bonds that trade infrequently and do not have actual trade data but contain matrix history. These are "evaluated bids" or estimated values provided by SunGard PowerData (Tradeline) in order to provide a matrix value. The matrix value is not a trade; it is a formulated quote, based upon market conditions, price offered on similar bonds by market makers, and other bond pricing factors. The vendor applies these changing factors on a daily basis to each issue and re-estimates the matrix value accordingly. The evaluated bid price is stored in the low data field. History includes: date, close and low pricing. Municipal bonds are not available in the Quotes or Charting areas. Current and historical market data on the following instruments: Historical Corporate Bonds (U.S market only) Government Debt ** Treasury Notes Treasury Bonds Treasury Bills Federal Home Loan Bank Fannie Mae (Federal National Mortgage Association) Fannie Mae (Federal National Mortgage Association) Partnerships Freddie Mac (Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation) Ginnie Mae (Government National Mortgage Association) Inter-American Development Bank International Bank for Reconstruction and Development Series E or H U.S. Government Bond Other Type FactSet Fixed Income Comprehensive current and historical pricing, ratings and terms data for hundreds of thousands of public debt issues for public and private companies. You can also access information about thousands of indices and benchmarks. Data from providers like Mergent, ICMA, FT Interactive Data, and Merrill Lynch is organized to ensure proper linking to an issuer's bond terms, ratings, prospectuses, debt schedules, capital structures and more. Global Financial Data (GDF) A collection of 20,000 financial and economic time series. It includes data on bonds, commodities, interest rates, stock markets and indices, futures, exchange rates, GDP, prices, and unemployment. Also included are data on stock market capitalization, dividend yields, price/earnings ratios, and total return. It includes extremely long time series - e.g. U.K. Central Bank Interest Rates monthly from 1694 to date and daily from 1800 to date. Methodology and sources uses are well documented. Areas of data include Fixed Income Database , Equity Data , Total Return Data , and The Real Estate Database . Haver Data on: Dow Jones Corporate Bond Index Merrill Lynch Securities (Corporate and MBS) Bond Volume Treasury Bill and Note Total Returns Merrill Lynch Option and Swaption Volatility Expectations (MOVE and SMOVE) No data on individual bonds. MarketAxess provides a comprehensive suite of data and analytical tools through BondTicker™ . Mergent Fixed Income Securities Database (FISD) Mergent has a comprehensive database of publicly offered U.S. bonds. FISD provides details on debt issues and the issuers, as well as transactions by insurance companies. It is used to research market trends, deal structures, issuer capital structures and other areas of fixed income debt research. See FISD Data Dictionary for more information. Reuters DataScope Fixed Income Providesfixed-income pricing and reference data for both the buy and the sell-side; coverage of fixed-income instruments and terms and conditions around the world. Delivers composite and evaluated pricing from a comprehensive range of exchange and broker/dealer contributors. Learn more… SDC Platinum It has information on bond and equity new issues, M&A, syndicated loans, private equity and more. It does not have time series data. Standard & Poor's Ratings Direct RatingsDirect offers access to credit research on bond issues from around the world, including public finance and structured finance issues. Provides real-timeS&P credit ratings and detailed reports explaining these credit recommendations. Fixed Income Government Sites : Federal Reserve The Federal Research has select domestic and International research, and also has statistics on releases and historical data. There are weekly, monthly, and annual rates going back to 1977. Within the site there are also sections on Interest Rates - http://research.stlouisfed.org/fred2/categories/22 . An example of these: http://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h15/20040510/ . Federal Debt - http://research.stlouisfed.org/fred2/categories/5 . Office of the Comptroller of the Currency OCC has information and resources about the regulation and supervision of all national banks, as well as the federal branches and agencies of foreign banks. TreasuryDirect Offers product information and research across the entire line of Treasury Securities. It includes historical information on Treasury Securities auctions , TIPS/CPI data , Treasury buybacks , SLGS data , and Savings Bond data . Fixed Income Internet Resources Bonds Online This site provides overviews of bond issues and links to news about the bond market. BondsOnline Quotes and Data Instant access to and extensive coverage of over 3.5 million stocks and bonds as well as many other securities covering major and emerging markets and exchanges across the globe. Information includes Reuters Corporate Bond Spread Tables, daily spread data for five sectors back to January, 2000, global bond spread data for seven sectors and four currencies back to December 2003, and global government and sovereign bonds with daily yields for sixteen countries throughout Asia, Europe, and the Americas. Demonstration of Bonds Online . Brady Net, Inc. BradyNet is a comprehensive source of pricing and information on Emerging market debt, and also provides commentary on the financial markets from IDEAglobal, a leading Independent Financial Markets Research & Analysis provider. Emerging Markets Companion This site has asset pricing, research, news, and more for Brady bonds, euro and non-euro bonds and more, updated throughout the day. The Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) FINRA is the largest non-governmental regulator for all securities firms doing business in the United States.  All told, FINRA oversees nearly 5,000 brokerage firms, about 173,000 branch offices and approximately 677,000 registered securities representatives. Also includes market data on bonds .  Public bond data is available through NASD TRACE, NASD’s transaction reporting facility that disseminates all over-the-counter secondary market transactions. TRACE is based on actual transaction data for TRACE eligible securities ( http://www.finra.org/Industry/Regulation/Notices/2009/P118710 ). If TRACE data is not available for a public bond on a given date, the bond did not trade. Transaction level data is not available from TRACE, and whether the transaction was made on a principal or agency basis is not publicly available from any source. Investing in Bonds : Investing in Bonds was created by the Bond Market Association to educate investors about the benefits of bonds investing. The Investor's Guide to Bond Basics educates investors about the types of bonds available, criteria for evaluating a bond, a guide to buying bonds, bond investment strategies and a glossary of bond market terms. The Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association SIFMA : Statistical Data from the Securities Industry and Financial Markets Information. Provides access to historical and current data on issuance, rates, and average maturity for corporate and municipal bonds, and federally issued securities. Also, covers Moody’s Corporate Bond Yield Averages from 1996 to present. Yahoo Bonds Center : Yahoo Center has Bond Lookups with advanced search criteria, Composite Bond Rates, Bond Market Summary, Bond Screener, and a Bonds Education section. Fixed Income Journals The Bond Buyer : Corresponds to the printed publication, The Bond Buyer. Bond Buyer specializes in the fixed-income investment market and is considered the authoritative source of information for the municipal bond community in the U.S. Essential daily coverage of government and Treasury securities, financial futures, corporate bonds, and mortgage securities is provided. Extensive coverage of U.S. Congressional actions, worldwide monetary and fiscal policies, and regulatory changes relating to the bond industry is included. (Searchable through EBSCO Full text: 07/02/1997 to present; also available from Factiva, and from Bond Buyer Full Text, File 626 in Dialog ). (Searchable through EBSCO, Full text: 07/07/1997 to present). The Journal of Fixed Income : Offers a balance of economic theory, including direct applications for portfolio managers and virtually everyone involved in banking, securities trading, modeling and research in fixed income. (Searchable through EBSCO, Full Text: 03/01/2002 to present (with a 12 Month delay)). The Journal of Structured Finance : Offers insightful, comprehensive research & commentary on all aspects of structured finance for the practitioner, by the practitioner. (Searchable through EBSCO, 06/01/1997 to present (with a 12 Month delay). Journal of Structured & Project Finance : An ideal resource to zero in on the structuring, legal, regulatory, and capital aspects of project finance. (Searchable through EBSCO, Full Text: 06/01/1997 to present). Investment Dealers' Digest : Covers the debt & equity markets, issues in registration, investment banking, & corporate finance. (Searchable through EBSCO, Full Text: 07/06/1998 to present).

Bank and Financial Institution Regulators Banks and other financial institutions may be regulated by any of the four 
Federal regulators: Federal Deposit 
Insurance Corporation (FDIC) - Primary Federal regulator responsible 
for state-chartered banks not members of the Federal Reserve System and state 
chartered savings banks. Federal Reserve 
Board (FRB) - Primary Federal regulator responsible for state-chartered 
commercial bank members of the Federal Reserve System. Office of the 
Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) - Primary Federal regulator 
responsible for nationally chartered commercial banks. Office of Thrift 
Supervision (OTS) - Primary Federal regulator responsible for federally 
chartered savings and loan associations, federal savings banks and 
state-chartered savings and loan associations. To find the regulator for a bank/financial 
institution, search for the institution in the FDIC Institution Directory .  The profile page will list the 
"Primary Federal Regulator" What are Material Loss Reviews? In accordance with Section 38(k) of the Federal Deposit Insurance 
Act (FDI Act), when the Deposit Insurance Fund incurs a material loss 
with respect to an insured depository institution, the inspector general of the 
appropriate Federal banking agency (i.e. Bank Regulator) shall make a 
written report to that agency reviewing the agency's supervision of the 
institution (including the agency's implementation of prompt corrective action 
provisions of section 38), which shall ascertain why the institution's problems 
resulted in a material loss to the Deposit Insurance Fund; and make 
recommendations for preventing any such loss in the future. Under the FDI Act, a 
loss was material if it exceeded the greater of $25 million or 2 percent of an 
institution's total assets at the time the FDIC was appointed receiver. On July 21, 2010, the President signed into law the Dodd-Frank Wall 
Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (Financial Reform Act). The Financial 
Reform Act amends section 38(k) of the FDI Act by increasing the MLR threshold 
from $25 million to $200 million for losses that occur for the period January 1, 
2010 through December 31, 2011. Further, the Financial Reform Act calls for the 
OIG to perform in-depth reviews of failures when the associated losses are not 
material but they involve unusual circumstances. How 
do I find Material Loss Reviews? Unfortunately, there is no consolidated source of material loss reviews.  
Below is the summary of our investigation: FDIC The 
FDIC maintains a list of Material Loss Reviews back to February 2009. http://www.fdicoig.gov/MLR.shtml FRB The 
Federal Reserve Board Office of the Inspector General maintains Material Loss 
Reviews  on their website http://www.federalreserve.gov/oig/oig_rpt_2010.htm An advanced Google search will 
also retrieve available reports http://www.google.com/search?q=material+loss+reviews&as_sitesearch=federalreserve.gov OCC Material Loss Reviews must be requested via the Freedom of Information 
Act. The OCC has recently launched an online FOIA application to submit, track 
and retrieve FOIA requests. https://appsec.occ.gov/publicaccesslink/palMain.aspx A registration is required and nominal fees may be 
accessed. OTS OTS 
does not publish material loss reviews on their website. They do accept formal 
FOIA requests but the turnaround may be days to weeks. http://www.ots.treas.gov/?p=FreedomOfInformationAct SECONDARY SOURCES GAO The GAO has not compiled a list of 
material loss reviews. Lexis / 
Westlaw Neither Lexis nor Westlaw maintain 
collections of MLRs. Factiva Factiva public press searches may reveal when an MLR has been 
ordered or published but will not have the full text of the report.​

page_472.body_text: ​Credit Default Swaps and CDS Indices 1. Discussion of CDS Data Sources 2. CMA (Credit Market Analysis) 3. Markit 4. ICAP 5. Thomson Reuters EOD Pricing (Datascope) 6. GFI Group 7. Fenics (now part of GFI Group) 8. Bloomberg 8.1. Data via Bloomberg Terminal (view only, no download) 8.2. Data via Bloomberg Data License Request Builder (downloadable) Discussion of CDS Data Sources " Are all Credit Default Swap Databases Equal? " Sergio Mayordomo, Juan Ignacio Peña and Eduardo S. Schwartz, Working Paper Nov 2010 CMA (Credit Market Analysis) Credit Market Analysis (CMA) DataVision reports consensus data (bid, ask and mid) sourced from 30 buy-side firms, including major global Investment Banks, Hedge Funds, and Asset Managers. Among the papers that employ CMA data are Nashikkar and Subrahmanyam (2007) and Nashikkar, Subrahmanyam, and Mahanti (2009). Markit Markit provides composite prices. The Markit Group collects more than a million CDS quotes contributed by more than 30 major market participants on a daily basis. The quotes are subject to filtering that removes outliers and stale observations. Markit then computes a daily composite spread only if it has two or more contributors. Once Markit starts pricing a CDS contract, data will be available on a continuous basis, although there may be missing observations in the data. Markit is one of the most widely employed dataset. Papers that employ this dataset include: Acharya and Johnson (2007), Zhang, Zhou and Zhu (2009), Jorion and Zhang (2007), Jorian and Zhang (200), Zhu (2006), Micu et al. (2004), and Cao, Yu, and Zhong (2010). ICAP Icap will simply not sell to us for any litigation.  Laura Londa is working with them to try to get a master license in place that would allow them to sell to us, but it will take some time to do this.  Please contact Laura if you have questions regarding Icap purchases. (rev. 3/21/14) Thomson Reuters EOD Pricing (Datascope) Reuters EOD provides CDS composite prices. Reuters takes CDS quotes each day from over 30 contributors around the world and offers end of day data for single names CDSs. Before computing a daily composite spread, it applies a rigorous screening procedure to eliminate outliers or doubtful data. Mayordomo et al. (2009), among others, employ CDSs data from Reuters. GFI Group GFI, which provides traded CDS spreads, is a major inter-dealer broker (IDB) specializing in the trading of credit derivatives. GFI data contain single name CDS transaction prices for 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 years maturities. They are not consensus or indicative prices.4 Thus, these prices are an accurate indication of where the CDS markets traded and closed for a given day. GFI data have been used by Hull, Predescu, and White (2004), Predescu (2006), Saita (2006), Nashikkar and Subrahmanyam (2007), Fulop and Lescourret (2007), or Nashikkar, Subrahmanyam, and Mahanti (2009) among others. Fenics (now part of GFI Group) Fenics (elaborated by GFI) data are a mixture of traded, quoted and estimated CDS spreads. Fenics’ data are credit curves for the whole term structure of maturities, generated hourly (all trading days) for more than 1900 reference entities. Data points in a given name’s credit curve can be actual trades or mid prices calculated from the bid/offer quotes. If there are no market references, the Fenics CDS spread is computed using the Hull and White methodology to ensure that a credit curve always exists for each reference entity.5 Fenics data have been used in Mayordomo et al. (2009) among others. Bloomberg Data via Bloomberg Terminal (view only, no download) Via CDSD <GO>, the Bloomberg default pricing for CDS is the "Bloomberg CDS 5:15pm NY Fixing Price", abbreviated CBGN, which is arithmetic means of all included contributor spreads (including those we might not have access to individually) that were received during the previous rolling 24 hours. If there are five or more contributed spreads, the highest and lowest are excluded from the calculation[ 1 ]. On the terminal, you can set your CDS pricing contributor preferences (e.g. CMA) by typing 15 <Go> from the CDSD main screen or press Pricing Source Defaults. You can select price contributors for different combinations of industry and currency. The sources that are available to you, including live, tradable prices, appear in amber on the right side of the screen. Press <Page Fwd> to see all of them Data via Bloomberg Data License Request Builder (downloadable) Due to licensing restrictions between Bloomberg and 3rd party CDS data providers (CMA, Markit, etc), only the Bloomberg default pricing for CDS, "Bloomberg CDS 5:15pm NY Fixing Price" (CBGN), is available for download through the data license request builder .
paragraphs: Sergio Mayordomo, Juan Ignacio Peña and Eduardo S. Schwartz, Working Paper Nov 2010

Reuters EOD provides CDS composite prices. Reuters takes CDS quotes each day from over 30 contributors around the world and offers end of day data for single names CDSs. Before computing a daily composite spread, it applies a rigorous screening procedure to eliminate outliers or doubtful data. Mayordomo et al. (2009), among others, employ CDSs data from Reuters.

GFI, which provides traded CDS spreads, is a major inter-dealer broker (IDB) specializing in the trading of credit derivatives. GFI data contain single name CDS transaction prices for 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 years maturities. They are not consensus or indicative prices.4 Thus, these prices are an accurate indication of where the CDS markets traded and closed for a given day. GFI data have been used by Hull, Predescu, and White (2004), Predescu (2006), Saita (2006),Nashikkar and Subrahmanyam (2007), Fulop and Lescourret (2007), or Nashikkar, Subrahmanyam, and Mahanti (2009) among others.

Fenics (elaborated by GFI) data are a mixture of traded, quoted and estimated CDS spreads. Fenics’ data are credit curves for the whole term structure of maturities, generated hourly (all trading days) for more than 1900 reference entities. Data points in a given name’s credit curve can be actual trades or mid prices calculated from the bid/offer quotes. If there are no market references, the Fenics CDS spread is computed using the Hull and White methodology to ensure that a credit curve always exists for each reference entity.5 Fenics data have been used in Mayordomo et al. (2009) among others.

Via CDSD <GO>, the Bloomberg default pricing for CDS is the "Bloomberg CDS 5:15pm NY Fixing Price", abbreviated CBGN, which is arithmetic means of all included contributor spreads (including those we might not have access to individually) that were received during the previous rolling 24 hours. If there are five or more contributed spreads, the highest and lowest are excluded from the calculation[1].

On the terminal, you can set your CDS pricing contributor preferences (e.g. CMA) by typing 15 <Go> from the CDSD main screen or press Pricing Source Defaults. You can select price contributors for different combinations of industry and currency. The sources that are available to you, including live, tradable prices, appear in amber on the right side of the screen. Press <Page Fwd> to see all of them

Due to licensing restrictions between Bloomberg and 3rd party CDS data providers (CMA, Markit, etc), only the Bloomberg default pricing for CDS, "Bloomberg CDS 5:15pm NY Fixing Price" (CBGN), is available for download through thedata license request builder.

Call Reports data are a widely used source of timely and accurate financial data regarding a bank's financial condition and the results of its operations. Medicare – The Official U.S. Government Site Information on Medicare health insurance includes sections on drug plans, hospitals, nursing homes, and doctors, as well as resources for the various aspects of Medicare coverage, such as available services, forms, and Medicare-specific search tools. page_487.body_text: Associations ​ American Association of Insurance Services (AAIS) AAIS develops and maintains policy forms, manual rules, and loss cost rating information. It has decades of expertise in product development, actuarial analysis, and regulatory filings, AAIS is now a recognized leader in insurance product research and design. American Council of Life Insurers (ACLI) This is a life insurance association web site that includes a section for consumers. It provides detailed guides about the different types of life insurance. ACLI is useful for consumers as well as professionals. ACLI publications. American Insurance Association (AIA) AIA offers advocacy and educational material for learning about property and casualty insurance with links to policy reports and other key organizations. It provides detailed information on the key economic contributions of the P-C insurance industry in each state.   See State Insurance Profiles . American Risk and Insurance Association (ARIA) ARIA is an academic organization devoted to the study and promotion of knowledge about risk management and insurance. It publishes two peer-reviewed journals: The Journal of Risk and Insurance and Risk Management and Insurance Review . Highway Loss Data Institute (HLDI) HLDI, an affiliate of the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS), is a nonprofit research organization that publishes insurance loss statistics on most car, SUV, pickup truck, and motorcycle models on US roads. Sponsored by the automobile insurance industry, HLDI regularly publishes detailed analyses of losses under six insurance coverages — collision, property damage liability, personal injury protection, medical payment, bodily injury liability, and comprehensive (including theft). Independent Insurance Agents & Brokers of America (IIABA) This site has links to consumer information, state associations, and current issues in education and government affairs, and directory information Insurance Advisory Board c/o The Corporate Executive Board IAB is a membership organization that provides: Case-based best practices research, proprietary quantitative research, and an executive meeting series. Cross-functional perspectives on insurance, drawn from the Corporate Executive Board's unique access to the insights of Finance, IT, and other senior executives in the Financial Services industry. Practical tools and templates which provide accurate benchmarks, diagnose problems, and supply appropriate solutions. Insurance Information Institute (I.I.I.) I.I.I. is an excellent source of factual information and basic industry data about the industry. Covers I.I.I. is an excellent source of factual information and basic industry data about the industry. It covers auto, home, business, life, disabilities, disasters, statistics, industry financials, hot topics, media, and more. I.I.I. is useful for both consumers and professionals. Publications: I.I.I. Insurance Daily, 5/week Newsletter, which includes electronic news abstracts of insurance related articles, and the I.I.I. Insurance Fact Book. Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) / Highway Loss Data Institute (HLDI) The IIHS and HLDI are responsible for studying highway safety in the hope of reducing auto related accidents, fatalities, and damage to property. Their research often has important industry and public policy implications. The IIHS web site provides studies, news, and other highway safety information. This is a useful site for researchers, professionals, and consumers. Insurance Institute of America (IIA) Subjects covered on this site include ethics, general insurance management, risk management, general property and liability insurance, information resources, insurer operations, insurer finances, public policy, quality improvement, andregulation. Publications: the annual Course Guides and Succeed Booklet. These describe educational programs and materials provided by institutes. They include information on obtaining materials and registering for national exams. Insurance Library Association of Boston The Insurance Library Association of Boston is the leading resource for and provider of literature, information services, and quality professional education for the insurance industry and related interests.  We are members. Insurance Research Council (IRC) IRC is a non-profit division of the American Institute for Chartered Property Casualty Underwriters and the Insurance Institute of America . It is an industry sponsored organization that conducts research, publishes the findings, and makes them available to the public. International Insurance Society (IIS ) MULTINATIONAL. Description: Facilitates international understanding and the transfer of ideas and innovations among insurance markets through a joint effort of leading executives and academics on a worldwide basis Publications: The Geneva Papers on Risk and Insurance Issues and Practice - Special Issue, annual. International Risk Management Institute (IRMI) IRMI is one of the best-known publishers on risk and insurance. Click here to see the list of publications. Life Insurance Settlement Association (LISA) Click here to see a list of the state insurance codes. Life Insurance Marketing and Research Association (LIMRA) LIMRA is an international publisher of statistics and reports on the life insurance industry. It conducts research, produces a wide range of publications, and is a principal source of industry sales and marketing statistics. LOMA LOMA is an international association through which more than 1,200 insurance and financial services companies from over 80 countries engage in research and educational activities to improve company operations. LOMA members are involved in life and health insurance, managed care, annuities, pensions, banking, banc assurance, securities, and other financial services areas. Mortgage Insurance Companies of America (MICA) MICA is an organization of U.S. and Australian mortgage insurance companies united to provide a forum for discussion of industry wide standards, and for representation before Congress and federal and state regulatory. Publications: Fact Book and Directory, annual. • Also publishes press releases and consumer booklets. National Alliance for Insurance Education and Research This site offers free access to some of its publications and to the Resources Magazine. National Association for Fixed Annuities (NAFA) NAFA was created to provide training and education, and to foster better understanding of fixed annuities including declared-rate, index and payout. It is the only independent, non-profit organization dedicated exclusively to the education and promotion of these unique insurance products. National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) NAIC represents U.S. insurance regulators from the 50 states, the District of Columbia and the four U.S. territories. It provides a directory of state government insurance departments, as well as consumer and industry information , and is useful for both consumers and professionals. The NAIC's Securities Valuation Office (SVO) is responsible for the day-to-day credit quality assessment and valuation of securities owned by state regulated insurance companies. NAIC publications are available for purchase. The NAIC maintains one of the world's largest insurance regulatory databases. NAIC data is used to determine market share, conduct market research and monitor industry trends. The ten-year historical data available in PC and SAS format. This data may be purchased collectively or individually. NAIC accepts custom orders . Information on available products can be found in the catalog . To see more information in Crikit click here . National Conference of Insurance Legislators (NCOIL) NCOIL is the voice of state legislators in Washington to promote sound insurance public policy. They hold three meetings each year to educate lawmakers on both new and recurring insurance challenges, develop model laws and resolutions that states adopt as their own, and communicate with Congress and other leaders regarding the opinions of state legislators on critical insurance issues. Working with other state groups, they are committed to preserving state authority. Professional Risk Managers' International Association (PRMIA) PRIMA promotes risk management standards and practices globally. Property Casualty Insurers Association of America (PCI) Represents mostly medium to small insurance companies, Reinsurance Association of America (RAA) RAA is a national trade association that proactively influences and guides federal and state lawmakers, and international bodies, as they formulate and consider legislation that regulates the business environment in which the property and casualty reinsurance industry operates It provides free: market reports , Quarterly Reinsurance Underwriting Reports , Leverage & Liquidity Reports , Loss & Reserve Development Balance Sheet Analysis . Other products are available for purchase: Legal, Compliance and Regulatory Products Statistical Products Society of Insurance Research (SIR) SIR is an international, interdisciplinary organization of insurance research practitioners focused on identifying, understanding, and communicating industry trends, emerging issues, and innovations. Its researches may be conducted by the Society or by its individual or corporate Members. Other material linked here has been made available by partnering organizations. page_491.body_text: Judicial Opinions U.S. Supreme Court In accordance with 28 U.S.C. §411 , the opinions of the Supreme Court of the United States are published officially in a set of books called the United States Reports. Each US Supreme Court opinion is issued 4 times, first as a bench opinion, then as a slip opinion, then in a preliminary print, and finally in the bound volume.  At each stage, an opinion is subject to edits or revisions until it reaches the bound volume stage.  A more complete explanation is available on the Supreme Court website titled " Information about Opinions " PDF copies of the bound volumes of the " United States Reports " (the official published source of supreme court opinions) back to Oct 1991 are posted on the Supreme Court website. For decisions prior to Oct 1991 , PDF copies are available on HeinOnline

page_501.body_text: Product Launch Dates Consumer Electronics Association Digital America 2010 ($150) Digital America is CEA’s comprehensive source of statistical information on the CE industry including nine product categories ranging from audio to wireless, and the latest CEA market forecasts and trends. It also includes a detailed history section, chronology of product introductions and a list of industry sources. The historical data spreadsheet provides the year that products gained enough market traction to be included in the market tracking report. Digital America is useful if you are dealing with types of products rather than individual models within the same product type and if you could deal with product launch years instead of exact dates. Proquest Gale Group New Product Announcements/Plus (~$4.10 per release) NPA/PLUS contains the full text of press releases from all industries covering announcements related to products, with a focus on new products and services. In addition to product descriptions, press releases generally contain key details about new products and technologies, including technical specifications, availability, uses, licensing agreements, distribution channels, and prices. Company contacts and phone numbers are provided to allow follow-up by interested parties. The press releases contained in the database are obtained directly from the product manufacturer, distributor, or an authorized marketing representative. Factiva New Products / Services ($3.60 per release) This Factiva subject code (ns=C22) idenitifies the introduction, review, preview or announcement of a new product or service. It does not include products still in the early developmental stages or the opening of new facilities such as factories or retail stores.  Sources generally include newswires, major business publications, and trade publications.

Analyst Reports Overview The 
Information Resources staff has access to analyst reports through Eikon (formerly Thomson 
Research / Investext) and through Capital IQ .  Keep in mind that there is no source that has every 
report ever published.  Because Cornerstone is not an investment firm or 
investment advisor, we can only purchase reports that the banks make available 
on the open market. Analyst reports give in-depth detail of the 
opinions of financial experts on the health and future of a company at any one 
time. We use company analyst reports to review what the common conceptions of 
the company were during a specific time period. We also use industry analyst 
reports to assess the health of the industry to which the company belongs. Reports can be 
searched by the company (for reports on specific companies) or by industry (for 
reports on a certain industry). Free-text searching is also available, but 
limited. As well, searches can be limited to the brokerage house or analyst that 
wrote the report. This is valuable because there are some brokerage firm reports 
that we do not typically use in our analysis, and we want to avoid buying these 
reports. The best method for determining which reports to get, is to have the 
report citations printed first, so that the total cost and usefulness can be 
assessed before purchasing any unnecessary reports.  Many times, the requested 
reports are limited to those analysts listed in the Institutional Investor All-America Research Team . Costs vary 
by the size of the report and the time it takes to download the report. Reports 
are approximately $10 per page and are typically 2 to 8 pages in length but can 
be as large as 35 to 60 to 100 pages. Certain 
providers are available as entire reports only and can cost 
between $500 per report to $2000 per report. Market research reports are also available through 
Thomson Research. These can be very costly (averaging about $21 per 
page). Announcements Thomson Research has added over 200 new 
contributors from 55 countries in 2009 . Thomson Research has updated how they list Bank of 
America/Merrill Lynch reports. See here for their 
announcement. Thomson Research (formerly called Investext) has 
added 120 new contributors in 35 countries in 2008 . ​

page_506.body_text: Privitization (sale of state-owned assets) World Bank Privitization Database The database provides information on privatization transactions of at least US$1 million in developing countries from 2000 to 2008. The site was created in response to growing demand for updated and consolidated information on privatization transactions in developing countries. Prior to this effort the most comprehensive information could be found in the World Bank’s Privatization Transactions database, which covered the years 1990 through 1999 Thomson Reuters SDC M&A Privatization: indicates a government or government controlled entity sells shares or assets to a non-government entity. Privatizations include both direct and indirect sales of up to a 100% stake to an identifiable buyer and floatations of stock on a stock exchange. The former is considered an M&A transaction and will be included in the quarterly rankings; the latter will not. Thomson Reuters SDC Global New Issues Dealogic Capital IQ Transaction Screening Criteria: Merger and Acquisition Features > Privatization of Government Entity This feature is used to identify scenarios where National/ State Governments divest their majority or minority stake (leading to majority stake owned by private investors) in state-owned corporations to make them privately-owned corporations. The process of offloading the stake is most commonly carried out by undertaking a public offering for the state owned entity. Thus, the feature is assigned to transactions as a result of which, the majority ownership in the company is changing from state-control to private control. If the privatization involved a sale of stock to the public, it may be captured in the SDC global new issues database. ​

The documentation is also available here . What sources does Thomson One Banker - Ownership use to pull out data on North American as well as international/foreign owners and securities? · For North 
American ownership, see page 15 of this DOCUMENT . · Substantials - Ownership data on non-U.S.-traded 
obtained on through a number of sources including, but not limited to, the media 
and official company-issued statements. · Aggregates - Institutional position derived 
from cumulative mutual fund holdings. An Aggregate position may represent only a 
portion of total shares held. Are there any samples of data from the various resources? Yes, see 
sample here. Can I run a report listing all owners - including insiders? The All (Excluding Insiders) allows 
you to run all holders excluding insiders owning less than 1% of shares 
outstanding.  Keep in mind that this report is only updated with 
proxies. What date are the values updated by? Values are updated by the date of the 
filing. Is there a report that will detail the funds and their advisors? Yes, it is the Parent/Fund view which groups everything together 
under the parent. See here for sample report. Why don't the Mutual Fund positions add up to the Institutional position when viewing Parent and underlying Mutual Fund view for a particular stock? Mutual Funds do not always file on 
the same date as the institution - their holdings will then vary based on 
timing.  In addition, Institutions also file for private money and pension money 
that many not be invested in Mutual Funds. Are foreign company values in the domestic currency? No - all USD. How often is the data updated for stock splits? Daily. What is the date and source of Shares Outstanding? Shares outstanding reflects the 
latest filing and is adjusted daily by any corporate actions. What is the methodology surrounding M&A? The surviving issue is carried forward, history is not 
adjusted. See DOCUMENT for detailed information on M&A as 
it relates to the securities. How are mergers handled in the case of the institutional owners? In merger situations there is 
generally a survivor basis. In the majority of circumstances one of the 
institutions will be deemed as the acquirer and surviving entity and, at that 
point, the acquired firm will be made an inactive entity. Those inactive 
entities will still be viewable historically, but all activity going forward, 
including ownership, would remain with the surviving entity and 
GeoOwnerID. (Ownership is not combined historically). This means that on the subsequent 
filing post merger all filings would be reflected in the acquirer’s filing. When 
an institution is made inactive it drops off the CURRENT holders list completely 
and is only available historically. Thomson generally holds off completing the 
merger/acquisition process until the next 13-F filing deadline so that one can 
see the holdings reflected within the acquirers portfolio as well as making sure 
that they do not remove valid holdings from product 
prematurely. What is the GeoOwnerID? It is a unique identifier assigned to 
the institutions, they are generated by Thomson’s own internal 
database. Do Individual Investors have GeoOwnerIDs? No, they are only assigned to 
institutional entities. What type of owners does the Historical data cover, and how far back? The historical data within the 
product contains history back to 1997 and includes 13F filers and 
Aggregates. How is Market Cap calculated? Shares outstanding (as of the latest 
filing) multiplied by month end price. How is Free Float calculated? Shares outstanding less the sum of 
the positions held by the following investor types: · Strategic 
Entities—Corporation · Strategic Entities—Holding 
Company · Strategic 
Entities—Individuals · Government 
Agencies What are Strategic Entities? Corporations, Holding Companies and 
Individuals. What does Filing Status represent? The percent of investors whose most 
recent filing occurred in one of the following time periods: most recent, 
previous period, previous period -1. How are Thomson sectors defined? Based on S&P and Thomson 
proprietary methodology. How does Thomson define investment styles? In classifying the dominant style of 
an institutional investor, Thomson Financial employs quantitative techniques 
based on the key financial fundamentals of the individual stocks that constitute 
a given portfolio.  Each position is weighted by its percentage of the total 
assets under management for a given institution or mutual fund.  For each 
position in a portfolio, Thomson Financial compares the fundamentals of the 
individual stock to that of the S&P 500 Index to determine if: · The forward PE of the stock is higher 
or lower than the S&P 500 average. · The indicated dividend yield of the 
stock is higher or lower than the S&P 500 average. · The 3 to 5 year projected EPS growth 
rate in First Call is higher or lower than the S&P 500 average By aggregating each of the individual 
stock selections and looking at the percentage breakdown of total assets in the 
categories outlined above, Thomson Financial is able to assess the interplay of 
growth, value, and income that drives the stock selection process of each 
institution and mutual fund.  All three fundamentals are typically used in 
defining each style.  To be classified in a given style, an institution must 
generally meet all the criteria.  In some cases, however, the securities that an 
investor is currently buying and/or selling provide a better indication of the 
true investment style being employed.  In these cases, Thomson Financial applies 
its unique knowledge of the investor's behavior to accurately classify its 
dominant investment style.​
