page_664.body_text: ​Guidelines for preparing SPA Article Summaries on CRIKIT Redirected from Practice Areas and Working Groups/Securities Practice Area/Academic Articles/Guidelines for preparing SPA Article Summaries on CRIKIT Some things to keep in mind before you start: 1. The goal of this project is to organize and maintain the vast knowledge of academic literature within the Securities Practice group. 2. We often see email requests sent to the SPA group asking for pointers to a) the best papers on a topic b) or papers that might support a particular quote 3. We would like to create a resource that will make such searches easier by a) Creating summaries of key papers, including statements that they support, etc. b) Maintaining lists of important articles by topic. c) Organizing the information in a way that can be searched. Steps 1. Log in to CRIKIT (http://crikit.cornerstone.com/) 2. Collect the papers and abstracts you need. a) Click on “Securities Practice” in the tabbed list on the left side of the page. b) Click on “SPA Academic Articles” in the drop-down list that shows up. i) This is a listing of some of the key papers under key topics. ii) Papers or topics in green are already summarized. iii) The first 5-7 papers under each topic may be considered especially relevant. We should start by summarizing these first. iv) Choose a topic after discussing with the team and making sure that no one else has already chosen it. v) The title of the topic (e.g. “Market Efficiency-Stock Price Reaction to News-Speed of Reaction”) is necessary for tagging all the papers (discussed below), so make note of it. vi) Make note of the top papers under that topic, by copy-pasting them to a separate document or printing the list out. vii) Collect PDF versions of as many of these papers as you can from JSTOR or EBSCO (CR has subscriptions to these sources) or SSRN or author home pages.  Do not purchase articles just for the purpose of CRIKIT summaries without clearing it with the team.  If a free version is not available, collect the abstract and make a note that the free version is not available. viii) Make sure to collect the URL (web address) of the paper/abstract so that it can be included in the summary.  Wherever possible, this should be the URL of the JSTOR version of the paper. 3. Read the papers and make notes a) Read the paper carefully, especially the introduction and conclusion, since the main results of the paper will be summarized there, along with any caveats. b) Remember that we are not interested in reproducing the entire paper. We are interested in the main results, as they might apply to our work. We are also interested in data sources, critiques of other papers, useful quotes, etc. c) Make notes in a separate document rather than directly enter the notes into the CRIKIT summary. 4. Enter the summary onto CRIKIT a) Click on “Academic Literature” in the tabbed list on the left side of the main CRIKIT page (not the SPA Academic Articles page under Securities Practice). b) Click on “G – Financial Economics” in the drop-down list that shows up. This will show a listing of the papers already summarized. c) Click on the “New Academic Doc” button. (You need to be logged in for this to work.) This will pull up a template of the summary to be filled in. d) Enter the paper title as “Name, Journal, Year” (e.g. Aboody, Barth and Kasznik, Accounting Review, 2004) in the title field. This will be the name under which the paper will show up in searches. e) In the place where it says “INSERT CITE OF PAPER WITH LINK TO PAPER HERE,” enter the full citation to the paper (e.g. Aboody, David, Mary E. Barth, and Ron Kasznik. 2004. “SFAS No. 123 Stock-based Compensation Expense and Equity Market Values.” Accounting Review, 79(2), pp. 251-275.) and add a link to the JSTOR version of the paper (preferred option) or SSRN page or any other page that may contain a PDF version of the paper for which CR has access. If none is available, or if the available link is dubious as far as copyright goes, just add a link to the SSRN page that contains the abstract of the paper.  Do not add links to published papers posted on websites of uncertain background such as file-sharing websites. f) The Table of Contents is automatically generated, so do not fill that in. g) Fill in the remaining fields as appropriate – read the instructions in the template. h) Note that copy-pasting from Word into the template causes a few problems – these need to be sorted out on an individual basis.  In general, it will be best to copy-paste as plain text and then do all the formatting in the summary html page rather than directly try to copy the formats from the word page to the html page. This is especially true if you are creating a lot of nested lists. i) Do not forget to add your email address where it says “For questions about the overall content of this page, please email: [FILL IN EMAIL ADDRESS HERE]” so that people can ask you any questions they may have regarding the page. j) Save the summary. (It would be a good idea to save it periodically and use the “Edit Page” feature to add more content.) k) Review the saved version to make sure it looks ok. l)    BUGS: There are many, and the general principle is to be very very careful.  E.g. 1. A change in one part of the page may lead to unintended changes in other parts. 2. When you copy-paste some content, it goes directly to the title even though you pasted in the body of the summary. 5. Tag the article a) Tags are keywords attached to each article, so that it shows up in the relevant searches. b) They are a powerful way to categorize articles, since CRIKIT continuously updates the lists of articles under different tags. c) Each article needs to be tagged based on the topic under which it appears in the main list of articles. d) In the drop down list under “More” on top of the page (next to “Print Page”), click on “Tag.” e) In the box that pops up, enter the tags for the paper based on the topic under which it appears in the main list of articles. f) Enter each tag on a separate line. g) IMPORTANT: Make sure to enter all the levels of the tagging system. E.g. For an article under “Market Efficiency-Stock Price Reaction to News-Speed of Reaction,” make sure to add 3 different tags as follows: “Market Efficiency,” “Market Efficiency-Stock Price Reaction to News,” and “Market Efficiency-Stock Price Reaction to News-Speed of Reaction.” This will ensure that the article shows up both in highly specific searches (such as when someone clicks on the “Market Efficiency-Stock Price Reaction to News-Speed of Reaction” tag) as well as in higher level searches (such as someone clicks on the “Market Efficiency” tag.) h)   Add additional tags only if absolutely necessary, and if you do, add them judiciously, mainly for cross-linking papers across the topics in the master list. 6. Update list of summarized articles a) Go back to master list of SPA Academic Articles and link the citation of the paper to your newly added summary, so that anyone clicking on the citation will be taken to the summary. b) Keep the team informed of your progress. Contact Olivia Lian ( olian@cornerstone.com ), Frank Schneider ( fschneider@cornerstone.com ), or Nari Subramanian ( nsubramanian@cornerstone.com ) if you have any questions.

page_669.body_text: ​S&P Capital IQ – Getting to Insider Trades Data CLICK to download the Insider Trades Parser After logging into CapIQ, search for your company by name and click on the correct result. On the left-hand side, under “Investors”, click on “Public Ownership” Select the “Insider Trading” tab near the top of the screen. Make sure “All History” and “All Transactions” are selected from the drop down boxes at the top.  (Note: speak to your manager if you believe you have a reason to select something other than “All Transactions.” (We will filter out unneeded transactions later, in Excel.) Note: from this view, you can click on the link in the “Source” column (usually “Form 4” or “Form 5”) to see the filing supporting the given row of data.  You can check back to this filing if you ever have any questions about the transaction or any doubts about the data. At the bottom of the page, click “View 250 per page” (or whatever the maximum number available is). In the top left corner of the page, click the Excel icon to export the current page to Excel.  Note:  due to a recent change within CapIQ, the Excel download will be the full data set (while the view will continue to be limited to the number of observations you have selected - current max is 250). Download the Insider Trades parser . A copy of these instructions is also available in this Word doc . Insider Trading Transaction types Please note that CapIQ Insider Transaction data is adjusted for stock splits. The insider trade information is posted to the platform 4 times per day so it should reflect recent splits, reverse splits, etc as those happen.  We get a direct feed from the SEC for that data so the share counts reflect the information they collect. The parser does not currently exclude various transaction types - the parsed data will include a variety of insider trades.  In the past, our insider trading data was limited to Open Market Acquisition and Open Market Disposition . In the CapIQ data you may also find the following transaction types: Open Market Derivative Acquisition Open Market Derivative Disposition Private Acquisition Private Disposition Sale to Issuer (this is when an insider sells shares back to the company to meet some sort of obligation, e.g. taxes. As I understand it, these shares return to the company rather than to the publicly available float) Derivative Acquisition under Employee Benefit Plan Derivative Disposition under Employee Benefit Plan Derivative Exercise and Retained Other Derivative Acquisition Other Derivative Disposition You and your case manager may decide to exclude some or all of these transaction types from the float.  This should be done by referring to the original Form 4s which can be found on the SEC EDGAR website. A list of general recommendations for each insider transaction type can be found here. How we arrived here! Capital IQ is the new data source for insider trades data when calculating Float and Patriot. Capital IQ’s insider trades data offers a number of useful features: Insiders must submit filings to the SEC when they purchase or sell shares. When on Capital IQ, next to every row of data is a link to the filing supporting that row. Data can be immediately confirmed against the filings with a single click. Sometimes, insiders submit amended filings, for example if the initial filing was incorrect. Capital IQ updates its data so that it is correct according to all amendments, not just original filings. Capital IQ presents this data in such a way that it downloads to Excel in a convenient format for our use. Capital IQ also provides a few different ways to view its data.

page_684.body_text: Markit Short Sales Data Short Sales data is available for up to 5 different securities a year for $5,000 each. We can use it for litigation.  But we need to be able to tell them the type of case it is and who the client is.  If it is a standard 10b-5 securities case, it is generally not an issue, but if it is something else, they may refuse to give it to us.  If we are going to have to turn it over, it is better to make that arrangement when we purchase the data.  It is an extra $5k to be allowed to turn it over.  But it cannot be made public, nor can the opposing side use the data for their own work.  It will be turned over for the sole purpose of reviewing our work. Attached is a sample of the data and their data dictionary explaining the fields that are available. If you have any questions regarding this, please do not hesitate to contact Laura Londa. FYI: The information entitled Difference in Short Sales data between Markit and Bloomberg on our Data sources page was authored by Eric Tam.  In case anyone wants to know! page_689.body_text: ​(20130321) Some date issues in Factiva--Please take note From: Londa, Laura To: #Consulting Staff < ConsultingStaff@cornerstone.com > CC: #Library < Library@cornerstone.com > Hello all, I wanted to make everyone aware of an issue that has been found in Factiva.  I will also let you know when it is resolved.  Recently a case team discovered that several a rticles downloaded from Factiva seemed to have incorrect dates on them.  Some of them were very wrong (for example one article announce d an action taken by a company that actually didn ’t take place until two weeks later than the date on the article ). The good news is a fter working with Factiva and giving them several examples, it was discovered that all article s came from sources from just one publisher , Euromoney .  They are now working with that publisher to determine where the problem is and how to fix it. In the meantime, I wanted to provide everyone with a list of all the publications by this publisher in Factiva (see attachment ) , so that you know which ones may have issues and can verify the dates if needed.  IR can help with that verification if you need.  I will let everyone know when the issue has been resolved, or if I receive any significant news regarding the issue.   Don ’t hesitate to contact me with any questions regarding this .  I apologize for any inconvenience this might cause. --Laura Laura L. Londa Senior Director of Information Resources CORNERSTONE RESEARCH 1000 El Camino Real, Suite 250 Menlo Park, CA  94025-4327 650.470.7080 direct www.cornerstone.com "Patience is not the ability to wait, but the ability to keep a good attitude while waiting." --Joyce Meyer

CLE ON THE LAN 2.5. APPLICATION FEES 2.6. FEDEX 2.7. MAINTAINING APPLICATION RECORDS 3. POST-EVENT CLE PROCESSING 3.1. ATTENDANCE SHEETS 3.2. CERTIFICATES OF ATTENDANCE 3.2.1. New York 3.2.2. California 3.2.3. Illinois 3.2.4. Delaware 3.2.5. Virginia 3.2.6. Pennsylvania 3.2.7. New Hampshire 3.2.8. Email Template 3.2.9. Reporting Attendance Electronically 3.2.9.1. Texas State Bar MCLE Site for Providers 3.3. MAINTAINING ATTENDANCE RECORDS Introduction to MCLE The following U.S. states and territories require lawyers to take mandatory or minimum continuing legal education (MCLE) courses in order to practice law within that particular jurisdiction. Summary of MCLE Jurisdiction Requirements Credit Hours Defined As of January 2010, the following jurisdictions have a 60-minute credit hour: (States to which we commonly apply are in bold, blue font) AK, AL, AZ, AR, BC, CA , DE , GA, ID, IL , IN, IA, KY, LA, ME, MN, MS, MT, NH , NV, NC, ND, NM, OH, OR, PA , PR, QC, SC, TN, TX, UT, VA , VT, WA and WY. As of October 2007, the following jurisdictions have a 50-minute credit hour: CO, FL, GU, KS, MO, NY , OK, RI, VI, WV and WI. Preparing for a CLE event STANDARD COURSE APPLICATIONS The location of the event determines the states to which we will automatically apply for course approval California events require no applications as we are a preferred provider New York events require no applications as we are a preferred provider Washington, DC and Delaware both require applications to VA, DE,& PA PA applications are processed after the event due to advertising requirements. Chicago events require applications to IL Massachusetts events require an application to NH For guidance on creating new MCLE courses, see the rules and regulations for each state governing MCLE.  For the seven states listed above, a summary document was created for reference. RULE OF 5 If an event has 5 or more attorneys from a state to which we do not apply automatically (i.e. five attorneys from IL come to a NY event), we will apply for course approval in that state. ATTORNEY REQUEST If an attorney asks us to apply for course approval in his/her state, we will do so as a courtesy. page_693.body_text: ​(20131105) Excluded Analyst Report Contributors from Investext and Cap IQ From: Londa, Laura To: #Consulting Staff Hello, This email is a result of a question that came up in a particular case and the managers thought it should be circulated more widely as it would be of interest to many case teams. The Background Both Thomson and S&P (CapIQ) have two different distribution systems for analyst reports. The first is referred to as Real-Time Research.  As a subscriber to this service the users would have access to analyst reports as they are published.  The only companies that can receive Real-Time reports are investment banks, private equity firms, and to a much lesser extent corporations who are the subject of the reports.  For example, IBM can receive in real time any reports written about them, but no others. The second system is referred to as Embargoed Research or Aftermarket Research.  These reports come out after some lag-time decided by the contributor.  In some cases it may just be a day, and in others it could be a month or more.  Any company can purchase access to this research, and it is what we have access to through Thomson Research (formerly called Investext) and through S&P’s Capital IQ. The Important Differences First of all, not all companies that produce analyst reports are in either of these systems.  (Bernstein Research is an example of one that is neither in Thomson nor S&P).  Second, companies that are in the Real-Time services are not necessarily in the Embargoed services. (Goldman Sachs is probably the largest example of this which is why we cannot get their reports at all.)  And third, companies that are in the Embargoed service may not put their reports into the Real-Time service. (Caprock Investments is an example of this). The Possible Exception With all this said, there are ways to get the Real-Time contributors that are excluded from the Embargoed service.  One way is mentioned above with the IBM example.  The other way, for companies like us, is we can get permission from the contributor to access their reports.  Thus, we could ask Goldman Sachs to allow us access to their reports.  If they say yes, we would fill out a form that they would have to sign, and submit it to Thomson and/or S&P and they would turn on the Goldman reports for us.  (There are a few other background issues that would need to be taken care of as well, but there is no need to detail everything.  Feel free to ask if you want to discuss further.) The Data Attached below are the lists of contributors to Thomson’s and S&P’s Real-Time Service that are not included in the Embargoed Service that we have.  Please keep in mind that this list can change over time, and if you need something current, please let us know and we can contact the vendors.  FYI it can take several weeks to get the new lists. Excluded Providers - Thomson Restricted Providers - CapIQ This information has also been placed on CRIKIT here .  If you have any further questions, please let me know. --Laura Laura L. page_695.body_text: ​(20120118) Capital IQ Excel Plug-In Billing--How to enter the correct billing code From: Londa, Laura To: #Analysts < Analysts@cornerstone.com >; #Associates < Associates@cornerstone.com > Since we have added a lot of new users to Capital IQ, I thought it would be a good time to make sure everyone understands how to enter in a billing code when using the Excel add-in.  Please see below. --Laura ______________________________________________ From: Londa, Laura Sent: Thursday, May 07, 2009 3:27 PM To: #Analysts; #Associates Cc: #Information Resources; Patrick, Jonathan Subject: Capital IQ Excel Plug-In Billing Hello all, I wanted to make sure that everyone who is using Capital IQ's excel plug-in realized that you can set a project code in it or change a previously entered code.  This past month it looks like a lot of people either didn't enter anything (which takes an extroardinary amount of time to research and fix) or didn't realize they could change it and it got billed to the wrong case.  To change the account code please do the following: When you start your work in the Excel plug-in there is an entry box on the top middle of the Excel menu (see below).  Click on the Enable Expense Code button and then enter the code and press Enter.  The code will remain in the box while you work.  Once you use the code once it will get stored in the drop down for next time.  Please don't hesitate to contact me with and questions or concerns. --Laura Laura L. Our access is limited to a set group of 10 people, but that group can pull the data for any case team that needs to use it.  The data will be in excel format . Below is a brief description of the database If you happen to need something that is not available through the database, we can purchase the disc for your case at a steeply discounted price. page_700.body_text: ​(20110304) Planning to move to Bloomberg Law From: Londa, Laura To: #Officers < Officers@cornerstone.com >; #Principals < Principals@cornerstone.com > CC: Gharsallah, Neila < ngharsallah@cornerstone.com >; Amin, Tara < tamin@cornerstone.com >; Chen, Kevin < kchen@cornerstone.com >; #Information Resources < InformationResources@cornerstone.com > Hello there, I wanted to let you know of a planned change that may affect some of you.  We are hoping to move from Westlaw’s CourtExpress to Bloomberg ’s BLAW for docket tracking and searching.  After testing we have determined that the content is pretty much equal, but the cost is significantly lower for BLAW.  Instead of the current cost of $ 55 K for West + an additional $10K every time we need another set of tracks (we currently have over 400 and can only buy them in packs of 99 tracks for $10K per pack), BLAW will cost us $30K and provide unlimited tracks for the library ’s use. There are also other added features to BLAW that I won’t go into here. How this will most affect you is if you are currently receiving dockets when there are changes, you will no longer receive the entire docket, but rather just the list of changes to it.  It should significantly decrease the size of your incoming emails for tracks which will especially help those receiving many tracks.  And if you would ever like to see the entire docket, IR can always pull it for you.  Include d in the changes they list, you will be notified when attorneys are added to cases .  You will still find out as soon as defense counsel are added to a case. I wanted to bring this up before we move forward with it to make sure this will not cause too much of a burden for you all.  Please let me know if you have concerns with this or would like more information. Thanks, Laura Laura L. page_701.body_text: ​(20110408) New SEC filings search system from Morningstar coming this month From: Londa, Laura To: #Consulting Staff < ConsultingStaff@cornerstone.com >; #Project Administrators < ProjectAdministrators@cornerstone.com > CC: #Library < Library@cornerstone.com > Hello everyone, I want to let everyone know that we are going to be changing our SEC filings vendor.  Currently we use Westlaw Business (formerly LivEdgar) and will be moving to Morningstar Documents (former ly 10-K Wizard).  While WB has some great features and functions, they are not ones that we get much use out of and it is simply getting too expensive for our typical use.  After many weeks of testing and reviewing we realized that Morningstar will provide us with the same documents, the ability to download in bulk and search full text, but at a fraction of the cost.  We expect to save almost $100K annually with this transition! We will also have a much simpler billing system so that you will no longer need to wonder how much you are spending.  Where WB charged per minute, Morningstar will charge $50 per login with unlimited downloads . Y ou can stay in as long as you need , howeve r it will log you out if there is no activity for 10 minutes.   The switch will occur this month and those with WB IDs will automatically be assigned Morningstar IDs and I will be setting up a number of WebEx training sessions for you to choose from in the coming weeks. page_703.body_text: ​ABSNet Users (Active only) This is Active Cases only.  If either the case or the user on that case is not here, they do not have access.  (To add a row, place curser in 1st row after header, right click, Row, Insert Row Before.) Price is $6K per month starting in March 2012.   Matters are charged for 30 days from start, i.e. 25th to the 24th of the next month. Laura's Spreadsheet with more information can be found here: < \\CRWADMIN1\Library\ABSNet\ABSNet Usage Tracking.xlsx > Here are the procedures to follow: Remind the requestor that the cost is $6000/mo and verify that it is ok.  Matters of the same case can all have access, but each different case must pay.  (It is not based on client.) Ask for a list of who they want to have access to ABSNet.  I usually explain the web access this way: “Do you also want web access?  If so, only one team member can have that, so you will need to let me know who it will be.  For those that didn’t see the emails that went by earlier, the web access is the same as the ABSNet consensus feed, but a different way to access the data.  The only difference is the Web access has ratings. Send the list to Laura and ask her to let you know when they have access.  If Laura is out of the office, please send the request to Stefanie Jarrell, and let her know that Laura is out. Forward this email: Rules of the Road to everyone who is getting access.  Just remember to change the case name in the subject line and in number 5 on the list. Forward the Web Access email only to the person they designate as the web user. Each team may only have one person with web access, and they absolutely cannot share the login. Do not cc anyone except me (or others in the library), but no other team members.  Remember to change the case name in the email. Please let me know who all you signed up, case name and number, who got web access, and the date their access started. If they ask how far back the data goes, it goes back to the origination date for the loans. If anyone has questions about specific data or whether the database has certain types of information, I’d first refer them to ABSNetAccess (that is the distribution name in outlook; there is no # sign in front), which is made up of all the current users of the data. If they do not help, You can refer them to our rep, Jonathan Harbach, Jonathan.Harbach@lewtan.com .  He can usually answer anything. If you have just been asked to add a user to a team that already has access, you can just send me (or Stefanie if I am out) an email asking us to add him/her.  And send the person the two emails in line 4.  If they want to be given web access that can only be done if no one on the team already is a web user.  If they are asking to replace the current web user, let me know and I can take care of it. Note: DPW-Tommy has saved previously purchased ABSNet data here: \\crilsas1\Data68\DPW-Tommy\Analysis\Master\ABSNet Data . ONLY DPW-Tommy teams have access.

page_705.body_text: ​(20111209) Price Changes to several IR databases From: Londa, Laura Sent: Friday, 12/9/2011 To: #Cornerstone Research Subject: Price Changes to several IR databases Hello all, I have been tasked by the OPC Budget Committee with improving the cost recovery of our databases used for our casework. The changes listed below will go into effect on January 1, 2012. In the last few years, our current pricing schedule has not been able to fully recover the costs of our database contracts.  Over the past year, I have implemented various changes in order to better control our costs, including renegotiating contracts to better reflect our current usage, moving to less expensive alternatives (such as Morningstar Documents instead of LivEdgar), and analyzing the rates we currently charge our clients. In addition to changing some of the rates I have also restructured the charges for some of the databases in order to make the costs more predictable for our case teams.  Below is the list of new pricing for several of our databases. Data New Billing Rates Notes ABSNet $11,500/month/case The increase is due to functionality that we have added to our subscription.  Contact Laura Londa for more information. Bloomberg $150/login (1500 max/month) With this increase, we will no longer charge separately for data downloads using the data license. We find it much too difficult for everyone involved to determine the costs in advance, and feel this will simplify things. Exceptions would be for extremely large amounts of data (>$5K, which are extremely rare) .  Please contact Laura Londa if you think you may need an excessive amount of data. Capital IQ $350/matter/month Anyone on a matter can use CapIQ and we will only charge the matter $350 each month (be sure to enter the matter information accurately). This includes all the data available except Analyst reports . Those are still charged at the listed rates as we pay those rates on top of our regular costs. CRSP $0.15/day/security Even with this increase, we will not cover the cost of CRSP, but I don’t want to increase it astronomically all at once. DataStream $700/matter/month For this a matter can get forecasts or pricing for up to 50 companies/securities each month.  For more than that, please contact Laura Londa for pricing. Factiva $3.60/article Due to a change by the vendor to our license. These changes will improve our recovery, make our response to urgent bills faster and more exact, and allow the case teams to better predict the costs of their data requests.   Please do not hesitate to contact me with any questions you may have. --Laura Laura L. Londa Director of Information Resources CORNERSTONE RESEARCH 1000 El Camino Real, Suite 250 Menlo Park, CA  94025-4327 650.470.7080 direct 650.324.9204 fax www.cornerstone.com "It's only when the tide goes out that you learn who's been swimming naked." --Warren Buffet

For this a matter can get forecasts or pricing for up to 50 companies/securities each month.  For more than that, please contact Laura Londa for pricing.
Due to a change by the vendor to our license.

These changes will improve our recovery, make our response to urgent bills faster and more exact, and allow the case teams to better predict the costs of their data requests.   Please do not hesitate to contact me with any questions you may have.

page_706.page_title: (20111221) And the crowds go wild! Firm-wide access to the New York Times!
page_706.body_text: ​(20111221) And the crowds go wild! Firm-wide access to the New York Times! From: Londa, Laura To: #Cornerstone Research < CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > Yes, you read that correctly.  We are finally getting access to the New York Times for the firm ! It was just announced a couple of weeks ago that they would start allowing group subscriptions, and we will be one of the first companies to sign up.  As a result we will be helping to test their system and provide feedback for improvement and they are giving us an incredible deal for access. In the first week of January, you will all receive an email from them with a link to register.  The registration is really just to set up a username and password ( no lengthy forms to fill out ).  After that you will be able to access it from your computer or your smart phone.  Once you are set up, you should only have to log in once and then it should remember you.  Eventually they will be moving to IP authentication, and you will no longer need a userid and password to access it, but they are not ready for that yet. Not only will you be able to access the NYT every day, you will also have access to their archives.  We will be getting unlimited access to their archived articles from 1987 through the present, and each person can also access up to 100 articles every four weeks from their older archives dating from 1923 through 1986. If you have any questions about this, or need help with the set up when you receive the email, just let me know.  Also, if you have feedback on any part of their system, please pass it along to me so I can gather it for them.  They are still trying to figure out how these large subscriptions might work, and the more feedback we give, the closer it will resemble what we want. J Thanks, Laura Laura L. page_707.page_title: (20140612) What you REALLY need to know about Time Stamps in Factiva
page_707.body_text: (20140612) What you REALLY need to know about Time Stamps in Factiva Some case team members discovered a few unusual inconsistencies with the timestamps of some articles downloaded from Factiva. While researching these few articles, more and more inconsistencies surfaced. These issues resulted in a month-long investigation by IR into how timestamps are assigned, where they come from and different publishers’ methods for dealing with updates and corrections. We talked directly to Factiva developers, and Dow Jones’ and Reuters’ content managers to finally determine how timestamps worked. Click here for a 6-page document we created to explain all the variances and issues with timestamps in Factiva, Reuters and others. The first page is an executive summary of the main points, and the rest goes into much detail regarding these points and some others. If the cases that you work on rely on the timestamps pulled from Factiva, you should try to find some time to go through this document as you may have to make some changes to how you use timestamps and what you assume about them. (LLL 6-12-14)

page_708.body_text: (20100105) Changes to Institutional Ownership Data From: Londa, Laura To: #Cornerstone Research < #CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > Hello everyone, As many of you know we normally get our Insitutional Ownership data from Thomson's ShareWorld product.  Thomson is getting ready to sunset that software and switch over to their online OneBanker product for this data.  There are a few differences that I will go over in this email as well as point you to locations on Crikit for more information.  We have been working with the Securities Practice area to make the transition as smooth as possible.  All changes take effect immediately. Here are the details: We will be retrieving the data from Thomson One Banker [TOB].  This is the same provider we've used previously, but the platform and format will be different.  See file here: < http://crikit/@api/deki/files/2510/=SW-TOB_comparison.xls > for a comparison of the format changes.  With a few exceptions, most requests will be fulfilled using the Single Security Momentum report from TOB.  As well, the major changes between ShareWorld (our previous database) and TOB are detailed here: < http://crikit/Information_Resources/Data_Sources/Data_Sources_by_Subject/Equity_Information/Institutional_Ownership_Data > which includes an FAQ and Glossary. The major change in format will be the inclusion of additional data columns which will be incorporated into the new macro that is part of the float template as well as some additional owners rather than just 13-F filers. Please note that there will be instances in which the data will need to be downloaded from a different module on TOB -- these will come from the Historical Momentum module.  This format is exactly that which we've previously received from ShareWorld (note that the new macro will also parse these files). The Float Template has been updated with the macro that allows one to work with the new (as well as the old) format. PRICING - Cost will be $500 for most data downloads.  However, we are willing to make adjustments for extremes, i.e., if a case only purchased 1 or 2 quarters we would cut it in half, and if they purchased more than 20 we would double it.  There are few cases that fall into those categories so it wouldn't involve too many manual changes for us.  This price has been determined by looking at the average cost of downloads per case. Please feel free to contact #Information Resources if you need more information about Thomson One Banker.  For questions about the Float Template, you should contact #Patriot Pro Help or Larry Dworkin or Kersi Shroff, both in CRNY. Thanks, The Information Resources Department Laura L. page_709.body_text: ​(20100108) Big Changes to Bloomberg--Please Read! From: Londa, Laura To: #Cornerstone Research < #CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > Hello everyone, We have recently had to renegotiate our Bloomberg license for compliance reasons.  In order to download, save and share Bloomberg data with each other, we have entered into a Data License with Bloomberg.  For an additional cost, there will be a separate piece of software installed on each terminal that will allow you to more easily download data from Bloomberg.  You will still be able to use the regular Bloomberg interface, but will also have an alternative for downloading large quantities of data. What this means is that ALL data downloaded from Bloomberg (via the software OR the regular interface OR Excel) will be charged on a per security, and in some cases per day, basis.  We will pass these costs directly through to the client each month.  As a result, you will need to be very aware of what you are getting from Bloomberg and calculating how much it will cost before you go in to download.  In some cases the costs will be minimal, in others they can quickly reach five or six figures. I will be holding a 30 minute informational session to go over pricing and the upcoming migration each day next week.  After that I will be scheduling training for the software to occur in each office over the next 3 weeks.  We will arrange at least 2 trainings in each office.  While I recommend that anyone who uses or asks for Bloomberg data for their cases attend one of the informational sessions, these sessions and the later training sessions will be REQUIRED for all Analysts (as the primary users of Bloomberg). I will send out 5 invites for the information sessions.  Please just sign up for whichever one is most convenient.  If you cannot make the one you choose, you are welcome to attend one of the others.  They will all be conference calls.  The sessions are: Monday, 1/11 3pm PST (6pm EST); Tuesday, 1/12 10am PST (1pm EST); Wednesday, 1/13 12pm PST (3pm EST); Thursday, 1/14 10am PST (1pm EST); Friday, 1/15 1pm PST (4pm EST). page_713.body_text: ​(20100311) Compustat CapIQ and Analyst Reports--Together at Last! From: Londa, Laura To: #Consulting Staff < #ConsultingStaff@cornerstone.com > CC: #Information Resources < #InformationResources@cornerstone.com >; Hunter, Kevin < khunter@cornerstone.com >; Wilson, James < jwilson@cornerstone.com >; #AMC < #AMC@cornerstone.com > Hello everyone. Big changes happening here at the Stone.  I think everyone will be happy about most, but there will be a price increase for Compustat that you will want to know about, so read on! Compustat After a year of fumbling through the networked version of Compustat on the term server, we are finally getting easier access.  Compustat data, including the Classic "as-is" data, will now be accessible through Capital IQ and the excel add-in.  The term server version will go down as soon as Kevin Hunter sees this email. LOL (Thank you Kevin for keeping that software alive as long as you did!) You will need to use a different userid and password than your personal one to access the Compustat data.  This is because of the cost of the data. Compustat will now be charged at $2000 per download. There is no charge for searching.  The charge occurs only with downloading data.  I know this seems exceptionally high, but it is based on the cost of the data which has skyrocketed over the years. If you go into Compustat using one of these passwords, please remember to change your password back to your personal password when you go in to regular Capital IQ to avoid overbilling your client.  Each office has been assigned two UserID's (see the end of this email).  Please use one of the ID's associated with your office so as to avoid log-in issues. Analyst Reports We have opened up CapIQ's Investment Research section to the entire firm. If you have a CapIQ ID you can access this new section now.  If you do not, contact #Information Resources to get you one! When you search a company in CapIQ and you scroll down all the list of options on the left you will see a section entitled Research.  Click on Investment Research and you will see the latest analyst reports that CapIQ has.  You can change the date range and add other criteria if you expand the Search Criteria section.  The reports go back well into the 1990's These reports do have additional costs associated with them.  On the left you will see a pdf icon with a $.  Hover over it and it will tell you how much each report is.  Your case will be charged for any you view or download.  The costs vary from $10 to $5000+. While CapIQ and Investext do overlap, you will see many reports that are not found in the other, so it is good to check both if you are concerned with finding everything.  If you have any questions regarding this, do not hesitate to contact #Information Resources with questions. Over the next few months we will hold new Capital IQ training sessions to show you Compustat, Analyst Reports, and many of the other great features available in this database.  It is well worth checking out as there is a wealth of information and data available here. page_718.body_text: (20100802) What to do when asked to click "I agree" to a license agreement. From: #Risk Management Committee To: #Cornerstone Research <#CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com> Hello everyone, When searching on the Internet for specific data or information you may often find something that looks like it might be perfect, but in order to view the data, you must first click a button or option that says "I agree."  The problem with accepting these agreements is that they often say either the information is for "personal, non-commercial use only," or contain some other clause which prevents our use.  However, the Risk Management Committee (RMC) also understands that there is no way to find out if the data is useful without accepting. Here is what we ask you to do when faced with this situation:  Go ahead and click the I agree button so that you can determine the usefulness of the information.  Should you decide that you may want to use it in your case work or other work, please contact Laura Londa, or the Information Resources group so that they can assist you with gaining the permission to use the information you have found.  With this simple series of steps we can make sure you get to the information you need quickly and Cornerstone does not violate any copyright or intellectual property licenses. Thank you so much for you consideration and assistance with this. --The RMC

page_722.body_text: ​(20100924) New Resource Opened up to Firm: Science Direct From: #Information Resources To: #Cornerstone Research < CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > Hello there. I want to let everyone know that we have been able to open up access to the Science Direct database firm-wide.  The database is IP authenticated so you must be either in the office or on a term server to access.  This database contains the full text of more than 2,500 peer-reviewed journals (including the Journal of Financial Economics) and more than 11,000 books (that you can access by chapter or by book).  It includes historical access to the journals as well, with some going back as far as the early 1800's.  Below is a longer description of this database. When you find an article you wish to read, you will be required to enter your name, email and a cost code .  This code must contain alpha-numeric characters only (no periods or dashes or spaces).  The client will be charged $25 for each article downloaded or viewed.  Books vary in cost .  This database is not flat subscription.  It is pay-as-you-go so the charges are hard costs and Cornerstone will be paying for any articles not billed to a case.  Please keep this in mind as you select articles for downloading.  If you would like any more information or a quick tour of the database, please don't hesitate to ask. To get started, just go here: http://www.sciencedirect.com/ , and if you'd like to browse their list of publications, you can go here: http://www.info.sciverse.com/sciencedirect/content/journals/titles .  This information is also on the ScienceDirect Crikit page here: http://crikit/Information_Resources/Data_Sources/Data_Sources_Alphabetically/ScienceDirect Enjoy, Laura About ScienceDirect ScienceDirect is a leading full-text scientific database offering journal articles and book chapters from more than 2,500 peer-reviewed journals and more than 11,000 books. There are currently more than 9.5 million articles/chapters, a content base that is growing at a rate of almost 0.5 million additions per year. Elsevier has digitized as much of the pre 1995 journal owned-content as possible, bringing articles from as far back as 1823 (The Lancet) to the desktop. Never has in-depth literature searching been so comprehensive and easy to find. The platform offers sophisticated search and retrieval functionality that enables the user to maximize the effectiveness of their knowledge discovery process. New tools facilitate research work flow aids such as access to content at an early publication stage and efficient multiple document downloading of content that can be stored, printed and passed to colleagues. The web environment offers new ways to present information as well as enhancing it with other content sources based on semantic technologies, e.g., NextBio. In addition, since 2003, many authors have been submitting extra value-added content associated with the research, such as audio and video files, datasets and other supplementary content, effectively accelerating research beyond the print format. Laura L. page_728.body_text: ​(20090123) New Insurance Section of Law360 Newswire to Launch From: Londa, Laura To: #Cornerstone Research < CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > There is a new Law360 publication that started today on Insurance.  Information regarding it and links to it are below.  It sould be IP authenticated for you as long as you are on the Cornerstone Network. Enjoy, Laura -----Original Message----- Sent: Friday, January 23, 2009 7:23 AM Subject: Insurance Section of Law360 Newswire to Launch Dear Laura, We are pleased to inform you that the Insurance Section of Law360 Newswire will be launched on Tuesday, January 27th, 2009. The Law360 Insurance section covers breaking news in insurance law and regulation. The service tracks litigation against major insurance carriers, brokers and reinsurers and emerging legislation. What do we cover? * State and federal litigation involving major insurance carriers, especially multiparty litigation and high value claims. * Disputes over claims related to directors’ and officers’ and professional liability insurance, property damage, mass torts and toxic torts. * Domestic and Global insurance regulation, including U.K. and EU. What distinguishes us from our competitors like Advisen, Mealey's and Business Insurance? --Specificity Our coverage is oriented to practitioners of insurance law. Most of our competitors write for the broader insurance market. --All in one package Our product includes features, analysis, news, legal cases, legislative and regulatory coverage. --Features and Analysis Our reporting matches the high quality standards associated with the Law360 brand. Attorneys just don’t want the news, they want analysis that points out trends and helps them with forecasting their client's needs. Our court reporting presents the news with context and analysis with an eye towards the significance of the case and its impact on future cases --Legal industry stories To round out our coverage we not only provide the most comprehensive coverage of the practice of insurance law, we keep attorneys aware of issues affecting the business of law. The launch of this section brings the total number of practice areas covered by the Law360 newswire to 12. We will be launching the Real Estate section later this quarter and add Tax and Mergers & Acquisitions coverage by year end. Enterprise subscribers All Law360 Enterprise customers will immediately have access to this content and we will be contacting you early next week to collect your user list information. page_731.body_text: ​(20090204) Out with the old and in with the new.  Announcing the new IR Wiki/Portal Site From: Londa, Laura To: #Cornerstone Research < CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > Hello everyone, As a result of suggestions from you all and our own desire to more easily update our information for your use, we have merged our portal page with our new Crikit site ( http://crikit/Information_Resources ).  If you go to the Information Resources Community on the portal, you will now see our Crikit site embedded there.  With Crikit, we were able to create a site that was more dynamic and able to handle many more types and forms of information. However we did not want to entirely abandon the portal as we know many people turn to it first, and we found that certain portal-specific applications could not be brought over.  Thus to access CRSP or to add yourself to one of our TOC Routing lists, you will still need to go to the portal. However I think you will really like some of the new things we have added to our new site. A few of the more interesting things you will find are Updated pricing list for the data we download Complete copies of the Institutional Investor's All-American Research Team articles from 1990 to present and broken out by year and by industry! Detailed information on all of the outside data sources that Cornerstone uses (including costs and how to source them). (Please feel free to add your own comments on the source as well or add new sources to the list.) FAQ with answers to commonly asked IR questions like time stamps, NAICS and SIC codes, Factiva Sources, etc. Searching tips and tricks for the databases you have access to And much, much more! And if you think there is something missing, don't hesitate to let us know.  We can easily add and update everything.  With this new site, we will be continuing to add new information and resources for you.  At the top of the main page you will see the latest announcements regarding changes to the page or to our resources.  So come on in and look around and let us know what you think.  ( http://crikit/Information_Resources ). Long Live Crikit! --Information Resources Laura L. Londa Director of Information Resources Cornerstone Research 353 Sacramento Street, 23rd Floor San Francisco, CA  94111 Direct Dial:  415-229-8153 Fax:  415-229-8199 Email: llonda@cornerstone.com http://www.cornerstone.com

page_732.body_text: (20090505) Reminder: Capturing codes in CRSP From: Londa, Laura To: #Analysts < Analysts@cornerstone.com >; #Associates < Associates@cornerstone.com > CC: #Information Resources < InformationResources@cornerstone.com > Hello all, I'd like to remind everyone that if you are going into CRSP to download data, please be sure to pick the case name as opposed to "No Case Name."  The list is updated regularly and should have all current names.  Should you be downloading for a case that has not been given a name yet (or it has not yet been listed), please send me or #Information Resources an email telling us what the name should be or that it should be billable and to check back with you later.  It takes and extraordinary amount of time for us to look up each user to determine what the data should be billed to. For example, in April alone 55% of the downloads in CRSP were listed as No Case Name.  Of those listed, 62% of them actually had case names that were on the list to be chosen.  I will also work to see if we can add the practice areas to the list since about 20% belonged to a practice area.  It would be a huge help for us if you could take a quick second to find your case name in the list and choose it before entering CRSP or send us an email if you don't find it.  Thanks so much for your understanding and help with this. --A very grateful IR group.  :-) Laura L. page_735.body_text: ​(20090625) Some newish and old litigation reporters you might not know we have From: Londa, Laura To: #Officers < #Officers@cornerstone.com >; #Principals < #Principals@cornerstone.com >; #Managers < #Managers@cornerstone.com > CC: #Information Resources < #InformationResources@cornerstone.com > Hello there, I wanted to tell you about some reporters that we have.  Some are new and some we have had but no one is on the routing list, so I thought I'd mention them with a description.  If you would like to be added to the routing list, you can either go to the IR Portal page and click on Routing List in the bar, or just respond to this email and let me know which ones you want to be added to. --Laura Bankruptcy Litigation Reporter Description This reporter offers comprehensive coverage of significant disputes in ongoing bankruptcy proceedings. The editors track dockets, summarizing recent developments and their implications for the debtor, its creditors, officers and directors, employees, and other parties. This reporter covers a wide range of topics, regarding Chapter 11 proceedings and includes analysis of the most noteworthy case law. Important litigation documents are also included. Features Covers significant federal district and appellate court rulings in bankruptcy cases Offers valuable commentaries by practitioners in the field Reviews a wide range of bankruptcy topics in a timely, unbiased manner Covers trial court proceedings, appellate briefings, and U.S. Supreme Court petitions in significant cases Pharmaceutical Litigation Reporter Description This publication provides up-to-date information on developments in litigation, legislation and regulation involving the pharmaceutical industry, with reproductions of the leading court opinions, complaints, briefs and responses. The lawsuits covered range from product liability suits to patent infringement, and from wrongful death to FDA approval. This publication is critical to anyone who needs to keep up-to-date on: FDA regulation, negligence and standards of care, generic competition, Daubert issues, trade secrets, and wrongful death. Intellectual Property Counselor Description This newsletter covers trade secrets, confidential information, copyrights, trademarks, licensing, basic patent information, and Internet and technology issues, all with a focus on providing practical material for corporate counsel. Issues also feature recent developments and useful articles, forms, and checklists. Features Discussion on recent case law and statutory developments Provides timely articles, forms, and checklists covering intellectual property law useful in the day-to-day counseling of businesses Coverage includes trade secrets, confidential information, copyrights, trademarks, licensing, basic patent information, and Internet and technology issues Expert & Scientific Evidence Reporter Description This reporter offers coverage of significant litigation involving how courts interpret the Daubert and Frye standards regarding the admission of expert and scientific testimony. It covers all stages of litigation, from complaint to final appellate decision and each issue. It is a source for determining which evidence courts are likely to allow and which evidence courts tend to disallow, which is especially important in situations where there may be conflicting opinions within the scientific community about the same subject. It covers both federal and state cases on all major issues in this area. Features Includes important documents Covers cases involving products liability, personal injury, antitrust, medical malpractice, asbestos, business/commercial, environmental, family, and criminal law issues Health Affairs Description Health Affairs is the leading journal of health policy thought and research. The peer-reviewed journal was founded in 1981 under the aegis of Project HOPE, a nonprofit international health education organization. Health Affairs explores health policy issues of current concern in both domestic and international spheres. Inside the Journal: Health Affairs is divided into the following major sections: Feature articles: New proposals, original research, and analysis of timely health policy issues Report From The Field: High-level journalistic article that explores a timely health policy topic, published with support of the Kaiser Family Foundation and Kaiser Health Reporting Commentary: Opinions and proposals for change Interviews: Conversations with leaders in government and the private sector Narrative Matters: Personal stories about the health care system that highlight policy issues of concern, published with support of the W.K. Kellogg Foundation Health Tracking: New research on trends and health care markets DataWatch: Data-driven analysis and original research GrantWatch: A review of recently awarded foundation grants and grant outcomes, with regular essays or special reports about health philanthropy Book Reviews Letters to the Editor: Lively discussion of issues raised in Health Affairs papers Thematic Issues: Health Affairs publishes both thematic and “variety” issues every year. Thematic issues (up to five per year) are devoted to in-depth exploration of a key topic surrounding health and health care. Laura L. paragraphs: Hello there,I wanted to tell you about some reporters that we have.  Some are new and some we have had but no one is on the routing list, so I thought I'd mention them with a description.  If you would like to be added to the routing list, you can either go to the IR Portal page and click on Routing List in the bar, or just respond to this email and let me know which ones you want to be added to.

DescriptionThis reporter offers comprehensive coverage of significant disputes in ongoing bankruptcy proceedings. The editors track dockets, summarizing recent developments and their implications for the debtor, its creditors, officers and directors, employees, and other parties. This reporter covers a wide range of topics, regarding Chapter 11 proceedings and includes analysis of the most noteworthy case law. Important litigation documents are also included.

DescriptionThis publication provides up-to-date information on developments in litigation, legislation and regulation involving the pharmaceutical industry, with reproductions of the leading court opinions, complaints, briefs and responses. The lawsuits covered range from product liability suits to patent infringement, and from wrongful death to FDA approval. This publication is critical to anyone who needs to keep up-to-date on: FDA regulation, negligence and standards of care, generic competition, Daubert issues, trade secrets, and wrongful death.

DescriptionThis newsletter covers trade secrets, confidential information, copyrights, trademarks, licensing, basic patent information, and Internet and technology issues, all with a focus on providing practical material for corporate counsel. Issues also feature recent developments and useful articles, forms, and checklists.

DescriptionThis reporter offers coverage of significant litigation involving how courts interpret the Daubert and Frye standards regarding the admission of expert and scientific testimony. It covers all stages of litigation, from complaint to final appellate decision and each issue. It is a source for determining which evidence courts are likely to allow and which evidence courts tend to disallow, which is especially important in situations where there may be conflicting opinions within the scientific community about the same subject. It covers both federal and state cases on all major issues in this area.

DescriptionHealth Affairs is the leading journal of health policy thought and research. The peer-reviewed journal was founded in 1981 under the aegis of Project HOPE, a nonprofit international health education organization. Health Affairs explores health policy issues of current concern in both domestic and international spheres.

From: Londa, Laura To: #Cornerstone Research < #CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > Hello everyone, Wanted to let you know about three new databases that we have pay-as-you-go access to.  Below is a brief description and a link to more information and pricing on CRIKIT. Audit Analytics-- Audit Analytics is a public company intelligence service providing independent research to the investment, accounting, insurance, legal, regulatory and academic communities.  Audit Analytics provides detailed research on over 20,000 public companies and more than 1,500 accounting firms.  Not only can you find out which auditors companies are using, but it also tracks when those auditor changes and why.  You can find auditor fees, audit opinions, when companies have issued financial restatements in the past and why, auditor info on deals and issuances, and much much more.  See the page on Crikit for more information: http://crikit/Information_Resources/Data_Sources/Data_Sources_Alphabetically/Audit_Analytics SharkRepellent-- SharkRepellent from Factset gives in-depth research on US public companies' takeover defense strategies. They cover the companies charters, bylaw provisions, poison pill provisions and state takeover statutes.  You can search on over 200 takeover defense data points.  They also have research covering proxy proposals, proxy fights and activism as well as profiles on activist hedge funds.  Reports can be produced in PDF, Word and Excel and there are direct links to the SEC filings and to the specific part of the filing you are most interested in.  See the page on Crikit for more information including pricing and a samples of their reports. http://crikit/Information_Resources/Data_Sources/Data_Sources_Alphabetically/Shark_Repellent MergerMetrics-- MergerMetrics from Factset gives in-depth research on Mergers involving US Targets.  Their data includes fees, termination rights, force-the-vote provisions, go-shop provisions, special committees, controlling shareholders, indemnification provisions, and much much more.  You can not only search for deals that have certain conditions, but you can also search for deals that do not have certain conditions.  For example you can create a list of deals that do not have go-shop clause.  The limitations on this database is that it only includes deals where the merger agreement is made available.  As a result you can create a report that contains sections of the agreements or the agreements in their entirety.  You can also report on trends in mergers.  It is an excellent complement to our other merger databases such as SDC and Capital IQ.  See the page on Crikit for more information including pricing and sample reports. http://crikit/Information_Resources/Data_Sources/Data_Sources_Alphabetically/Merger_Metrics If you have any questions about these databases, please do not hesitate to contact me or anyone in Information Resources. --Laura Laura L. page_738.body_text: ​CPA Continuing Professional Education (CPE) Here’s what we know about offering CPE state-by-state: Texas So we have two options for giving CPE credit in Texas.  We can apply to be a "registered sponsor".  It requires a decent length application and a $400 application fee.  It also takes 4-6 weeks of processing. Alternately, we can supply the providers with a generic CPE certificate.  They would have to fill out Form L002 "Claiming Continuing Professional Education Credits From a Non-Registered Sponsor" http://www.tsbpa.state.tx.us/pdffiles/l0002.pdf and submit it with the certificate.  It would then be evaluated by the board on an individual basis. North Carolina For North Carolina, the Board does not approve individual CPE courses . It is the responsibility of the individual CPA to determine if the course they attended complies with the minimum CPE standards as set in 08G.0404 Requirements for CPE Credit and to maintain documentation proving that the course met these standards. The simple guidelines are: is in one of the seven fields of study recognized by the Board and set forth in Paragraph (b) of this Rule; (Accounting and Consulting Services are two so I think we’re good there) is developed by an individual who has education and work experience in the subject matter of the course; (Our faculty seem appropriate) uses instructional techniques and materials that are current and accurate. (I’d say we meet that too) District of Columbia For DC, the requirement is set by section 2531 Continuing Education: Acceptable Continuing Professional Programs which says that professional programs are okay as long as they meet the Statement on Standards of Continuing Professional Education (CPE) Programs developed by NASBA and AICPA, which in my non-professional opinion, they do. In summary, our accounting breakfasts should be acceptable for CPE credit in at least CA, NC, & DC and we can use our current certificate. While our courses probably also meet NY and TX standards, we are not registered sponsors in those states. For NY, only courses from providers approved and registered with NY state or NASBA are eligible for CPE credit. For TX, we also would have to apply to be a registered sponsor or simply request that the CPA submit their personal request for CPE credit using our Certificate of Attendance.

page_741.body_text: ​(20090723) Some Clarification RE: New Pricing for Bloomberg and Compustat effective August 1 From: Londa, Laura To: #Cornerstone Research < #CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > Hello all, I got several variations of one question several times and so I thought it would make sense to send out a clarification regarding it.  The question was basically what do I put in as a charge code if I do not want the login charged to the client because it is a redo of what I've already done, or there was a mistake in my original download, etc.? Obviously we want to avoid billing the client for our mistakes or excessively for these databases, which is why we put the cap in place on Bloomberg.  I found that the monthly max generally covered the additional logins that were do-overs or fixing mistakes.  However we still want to be sure.  Compustat does not have a cap as it is not used that much, but we will watch it closely and the same rules apply to it. Regardless of why you think the client should not be billed the best thing for you to do is to put in the client code for which you are doing the work.  If, at the end of your work, you still feel the client should not be billed please send an email to #Information Resources, and let us know which database you were on, the date on it and what the code was you put in.  We will take care of correcting the allocations at month end.  This way is MUCH MORE efficient than putting in a generic code which raises all sorts of red flags and causes us in IR to do a lot of additional work at month-end.  So please always remember to put in the code for whatever case, or non-billable project you are doing the work for. BTW this also applies to all other databases that request codes such as Westlaw Business, Capital IQ, CRSP, etc.  You can always tell us the client shouldn't be billed afterwards. page_759.body_text: ​(20080212) Changes regarding Law360 publications From: Plummer, Laura To: #Cornerstone Research < #CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > Starting Tuesday, February 19th, all users of any Law360 publication will need to register and get a username and password in order to access the articles.  The IP authentication will be turned off automatically and the generic userid and password will be deleted by the vendor.  They are trying to set it up for us so that if you are currently signed up to receive one or more of their publications, you will only need to register once and your userid and password will work for any of them. Below is the letter they sent out regarding this change.  The reason for it is that they are adding features that will be customizable at the user level and therefore require individual IDs.  They have set it up in such a way that once you login, you should be remembered and not have to put in your userid and password again. Please do not hesitate to contact me if you have any questions or concerns.  I apologize for any inconvenience this may cause. --Laura -----Original Message----- From: Christina Rosas [ mailto:crosas@portfoliomedia.com ] Sent: Monday, February 11, 2008 1:13 PM To: Plummer, Laura Subject: Important message about your Law360 subscription Dear subscriber, I'm writing to you today to notify you of an important change in the way Law360 readers access our articles. Starting on Tuesday, February 19, 2008, our readers must be individually registered. This requirement applies to all readers, even those whose IP address has been registered to bypass user names and passwords. The registration process is quick and easy. When readers click on a story in our newsletters, they are taken to an online form asking them to submit their office e-mail address.  After readers have submitted their e-mail address, we send them a confirmation e-mail with a link to a page where they can create their password. Once users have been registered, they'll be able to access articles from the registered computer. Readers have to register each computer they use to access our publications. While they may be registered on multiple computers, they will only be able to access our publications from one computer at any given time. E-mail addresses are collected solely to register each reader individually, and to provide a means by which to send our readers password reminders. As part of this registration process, organizational user names and passwords will be retired and rendered invalid. Only individual user names (i.e., e-mail addresses) and user-generated passwords will be valid. However, users with IP authentication will be able to log in with just their e-mail address, which can be stored as a cookie on their computer. This change will yield many benefits, both for the readers and for you as an account manager: Readers will be able to personalize content and alerts. * They will also be able to add comments to articles and contact other readers directly. These changes will be implemented in the next few months. * Account managers will be able to manage all their subscriptions online, view users and expiration dates and add more subscriptions. We have designed this process to minimize the impact on account managers. I am hopeful there will be few, if any, queries from your user base as a result of our registration process. Our system will automatically recognize your users by their e-mail address and group them together for you, so that you may easily see who has registered. We will send you a link next week to an online panel where you can manage your subscriptions with us. If you have any questions or concerns, please do not hesitate to contact us. Best regards, Christina Rosas & Customer Relations Team 212-537-6331
paragraphs: Starting Tuesday, February 19th, all users of any Law360 publicationwill need to register and get a username and password in order to access the articles.  The IP authentication will be turned off automatically and the generic userid and password will be deleted by the vendor.  They are trying to set it up for us so that if you are currently signed up to receive one or more of their publications, you will only need to register once and your userid and password will work for any of them.

Below is the letter they sent out regarding this change.  The reason for it is that they are adding features that will be customizable at the user level and therefore require individual IDs.  They have set it up in such a way that once you login, you should be remembered and not have to put in your userid and password again.
Please do not hesitate to contact me if you have any questions or concerns.  I apologize for any inconvenience this may cause.
-----Original Message-----From: Christina Rosas [mailto:crosas@portfoliomedia.com]Sent: Monday, February 11, 2008 1:13 PMTo: Plummer, LauraSubject: Important message about your Law360 subscription
I'm writing to you today to notify you of an important change in the way Law360 readers access our articles.

Starting on Tuesday, February 19, 2008, our readers must be individually registered. This requirement applies to all readers, even those whose IP address has been registered to bypass user names and passwords.

The registration process is quick and easy. When readers click on a story in our newsletters, they are taken to an online form asking them to submit their office e-mail address.  After readers have submitted their e-mail address, we send them a confirmation e-mail with a link to a page where they can create their password. Once users have been registered, they'll be able to access articles from the registered computer.

Readers have to register each computer they use to access our publications. While they may be registered on multiple computers, they will only be able to access our publications from one computer at any given time.
E-mail addresses are collected solely to register each reader individually, and to provide a means by which to send our readers password reminders.

As part of this registration process, organizational user names and passwords will be retired and rendered invalid. Only individual user names (i.e., e-mail addresses) and user-generated passwords will be valid. However, users with IP authentication will be able to log in with just their e-mail address, which can be stored as a cookie on their computer.
This change will yield many benefits, both for the readers and for you as an account manager:

Readers will be able to personalize content and alerts.* They will also be able to add comments to articles and contact other readers directly. These changes will be implemented in the next few months.
* Account managers will be able to manage all their subscriptions online, view users and expiration dates and add more subscriptions.

We have designed this process to minimize the impact on account managers. I am hopeful there will be few, if any, queries from your user base as a result of our registration process. Our system will automatically recognize your users by their e-mail address and group them together for you, so that you may easily see who has registered. We will send you a link next week to an online panel where you can manage your subscriptions with us.
If you have any questions or concerns, please do not hesitate to contact us.
Best regards,Christina Rosas & Customer Relations Team212-537-6331

page_763.body_text: (20080324) Migration to the new LivEdgar platform From: Londa, Laura To: #Cornerstone Research < #CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > Hello everyone, LivEdgar is sunsetting their product, so we are starting our migration over to the new product, called Westlaw Business.  If you have a LivEdgar username and password, you will be receiving a new one for Westlaw Business in the next day or so.  Your old ID will be closed. I will be setting up training sessions in each of the offices so that everyone can see all the advances and features with the new interface.  These sessions should happen in the next couple of weeks. --Laura Laura L. From: Londa, Laura To: #Cornerstone Research < #CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > Hello everyone, Believe it or not, the Number One requested subscription is finally here!  After years of only allowing access to academic institutions, JSTOR has now allowed subscriptions to corporations.  Although they have opened up only about half of their collection to corporations, I think you will find many of the titles you are looking for such as The Accounting Review, Econimetrica, Journal of Applied Econometrics and many more.  More titles are being added every week as they negotiate access with the publishers.  There is a lag for current issues, but all historical collections are there.  For a complete list of the titles included in our access along with their coverage dates, and lag-time, please go here: http://www.jstor.org/action/showJournals?browseType=collectionInfoPage&selectCollection=corp . If you click on Business Collection under one of the titles, you will probably see the titles you are most interested in. Like our other new subscriptions, this is IP authenticated and can be accessed from the Library portal page under Library Data Sources.  And, there is not charge to the client for use of this database.  Use it as much as you would like!  If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to email me. Enjoy! --Laura Laura L. page_772.body_text: ​(20080805) Follow-up: Announcing: Firm-wide access to Compustat! From: Londa, Laura To: #Cornerstone Research < #CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > For first time users, before following the directions below, first Execute the NewUser.reg program under Start | Programs | Research Insight.  Then follow the directions below and you should be able to get in without problems. --laura ______________________________________________ From: Londa, Laura Sent: Tuesday, April 08, 2008 10:30 AM To: #Cornerstone Research Subject: Announcing: Firm-wide access to Compustat! After may months of testing and many MANY hours on the part of Kevin Hunter in IT (Thank You Kevin!!!!!), I am finally able to announce the opening of networked access to Compustat-- please see below for access instructions .  Boston and Menlo Park will stop handling the day-to-day basic Compustat requests.  However, we will not be getting rid of the #Compustat User Group, but rather turning it into an advanced user group where you can send your really tough questions for help and explanations.  If you'd like to be a part of this user group please let Ellen Ryan know. I am setting up training sessions in each office.  Look for them in the near future! Currently we are not charging back for Compustat, but hope to in the future.  I will give everyone advance warning before we put a charge-back system in place. And finally you will need to know a few things before you try to search in Compustat: 1) It is located on CRSFTERM4 2) You must have a default printer selected before trying to search (you should only have to set this up once).  If you are not sure how to set a default printer, contact #IT Help Desk. 3) Lastly you need to tell Compustat where to find the files.  Again, you only need to do this the first time you log in.  If you do not do this, you will get an error message when you try to access the database.  Here is what you do (it only takes about 5 minutes): After logging into the term sever, go to Start and select Research Insight Database Manager Under Database Areas, click on Properties Under Area 1 put: \\ crsfir \ ridata \ na1 Under Area 2 put: \\ crsfir \ ridata \ na2 Click Apply and then okay and exit the Manager Then go to start and click on Research Insight It will ask you to copy 596 files to update, say okay and on the next screen click Copy It will start copying. This will take about 5 min.  When it is done you should be ready to go. Please do not hesitate to contact me with any questions you may have. --Laura Laura L. Londa Director of Information Resources Cornerstone Research 353 Sacramento Street, 23rd Floor San Francisco, CA  94111 Direct Dial:  415-229-8153 Fax:  415-229-8199 Email: llonda@cornerstone.com http://www.cornerstone.com
