______________________________________________From:Londa, LauraSent:Tuesday, April 08, 2008 10:30 AMTo:#Cornerstone ResearchSubject:Announcing: Firm-wide access to Compustat!

After may months of testing and many MANY hours on the part of Kevin Hunter in IT (Thank You Kevin!!!!!), I am finally able to announce the opening of networked access to Compustat--please see below for access instructions.  Boston and Menlo Park will stop handling the day-to-day basic Compustat requests.  However, we will not be getting rid of the #Compustat User Group, but rather turning it into an advanced user group where you can send your really tough questions for help and explanations.  If you'd like to be a part of this user group please let Ellen Ryan know.
I am setting up training sessions in each office.  Look for them in the near future!
Currently we are not charging back for Compustat, but hope to in the future.  I will give everyone advance warning before we put a charge-back system in place.

And finally you will need to know a few things before you try to search in Compustat:1) It is located on CRSFTERM42) You must have a default printer selected before trying to search (you should only have to set this up once).  If you are not sure how to set a default printer, contact #IT Help Desk.

3) Lastly you need to tell Compustat where to find the files.  Again, you only need to do this the first time you log in.  If you do not do this, you will get an error message when you try to access the database.  Here is what you do (it only takes about 5 minutes):

After logging into the term sever, go to Start and select Research Insight Database ManagerUnder Database Areas, click on PropertiesUnder Area 1 put:\\crsfir\ridata\na1Under Area 2 put:\\crsfir\ridata\na2Click Apply and then okay and exit the ManagerThen go to start and click on Research InsightIt will ask you to copy 596 files to update, say okay and on the next screen click CopyIt will start copying. This will take about 5 min.  When it is done you should be ready to go.
Please do not hesitate to contact me with any questions you may have.--Laura

The subscription includes >    the full text of the print edition PLUS quarterly updates with new biographies and articles* >    excellent search and browse, both full text and advanced >    hyperlinked cross-references within articles and links to related sites >    well written articles placing topics in full historical context >    1,700+ articles by 1,500+ scholars, experts, and Nobel Laureates >    New and expanded articles covering: Behavioral economics, game theory, technological change and growth, labor economics, and much more *The first update is scheduled for September 15, 2008 and includes 5 new commissioned articles and 19 new biographies. page_789.body_text: ​(20081223) Compustat is back From: Londa, Laura To: #Cornerstone Research < CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > CC: #Information Resources < InformationResources@cornerstone.com > Hello there everyone, It looks like Compustat is back up and running (many many many thanks to Kevin Hunter!!!!!), but it has a new home (one that will have no other software installed on it that might conflict with it).  As a result, even if you used it before, you will have to follow the first-time user's instructions below. Things to Note: 1)  I believe we are still having a few default printer issues, so right now you will have to set your default to an SF printer (this should be fixed soon). 2)  It is also recommended that you make “Classic” (as reported data) the default database – otherwise you could inadvertently use “Compustat” figures (adjusted for mergers and acquisitions).  You can always choose to use the Compustat database for your data but it will be Classic data that will be accessed as the default. Instructions This only has to be done the first time you log in to Compustat.  After that, it should remember you and work just fine. First you will log in to Compustat's new terminal server: CRSFIRAPPS 1)  When you first log in: Execute the NewUser.reg program under Start | Programs | Research Insight. 2)  You must have a default printer selected before trying to search (you should only have to set this up once). If you are not sure how to set a default printer, contact #IT Help Desk. 3)  Lastly you need to tell Compustat where to find the files. Again, you only need to do this the first time you log in. If you do not do this, you will get an error message when you try to access the database. Here is what you do (it only takes about 5 minutes): After logging into the term sever, go to Start and select Research Insight Database Manager Under Database Areas, click on Properties Under Area 1 put: \\crsfir\ridata\na1 Under Area 2 put: \\crsfir\ridata\na2 Click Apply and then okay and exit the Manager Then go to start and click on Research Insight It will ask you to copy 596 (or some other large number) files to update, say okay and on the next screen click Copy It will start copying. This will take about 5 min. When it is done you should be ready to go. Good Luck, and let me know if you have any problems.  I apologize for all the downtime for this. -Laura Laura L. Londa Director of Information Resources Cornerstone Research 353 Sacramento Street, 23rd Floor San Francisco, CA  94111 Direct Dial:  415-229-8153 Fax:  415-229-8199 Email: llonda@cornerstone.com http://www.cornerstone.com

page_790.body_text: ​(20070629) An ugly change in the pricing of some Analyst Reports From: Plummer, Laura To: #Cornerstone Research < #CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > Hello everyone, As many of you have probably noticed over the past years, many investment banks have disappeared from our analyst report searches.  This was done at the request of the investment banks themselves.  For a variety of reasons they have decided to no longer make their reports available through these public resources.  While some have pulled their reports completely, others have chosen to simply limit the scope and/or the length of time their reports can remain available, or they have chosen to offer their reports, but at a premium price.  This is why you receive different results and/or pricing when you have us do the same search 2 months later. Well, this trend has gotten worse.  Several large investment banks have decided their reports are worth a super-premium and have changed what they are charging for them.  Regardless of any contract we have or get with Investext, these are outside of it at the request of the investment banks, so there is not choice but to pay full retail price.  With that said, attached is more complete info including embargos placed by various IBs.  Feel free to contact me with any questions. Thanks, Laura Laura Plummer Director of Information Resources Cornerstone Research 1000 El Camino Real, Suite 250 Menlo Park, CA  94025 Direct Dial:  650.470.7168 Fax:  650-324.9204 Email: lplummer@cornerstone.com http://www.cornerstone.com

page_791.body_text: (20070706) Announcing New Firm-wide Resource: CapitalIQ ​ From: Plummer, Laura To: #Cornerstone Research < #CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > Hello all, We've recently subscribed to a new database from S&P called Capital IQ.  Below is a description of some of it's capabilities and data as well as the charges associated with pulling the data.  You will have to enter a project code every time you log in.  Briefly, it has great data involving M&A, New Issues, Private Equity, Venture Capital, and Private Companies.  You can often find out the related parties involved in transactions as well such as Law Firms and Accounting Firms.  You can find relationship paths between officers, board members, and others of different companies.  And then there is lots of financial data for the companies as well as ratings and some earnings estimates (not very historical).  You can produce reports in both word and excel and can produce tear sheets, charts, summaries and detailed data reports. page_792.body_text: (20070727) New Resource Opened up to Firm: HeinOnline ​ From: Plummer, Laura To: #Cornerstone Research < #CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > Hey there everyone, How would you like to have unlimited access to pretty much every law review ever published?  Maybe you'd like to see what the first issue of the Harvard Law Review from April 15, 1887 looked like, or you'd like to search the CFR back to 1938 or the Federal Register back to 1936 and get PDF images of the actual publications?  Or even the US Attorney General Opinions back to 1791 or the U.S. Supreme Court Reports back to 1754?  Well now you can, and with NO CHARGE to your client! The Library has recently subscribed the firm to a service called HeinOnline .  HeinOnline offers access to over 1200 law and law-related periodicals as well as a variety of federal legislative materials including a treaties library and more!  You can search on the full text as well as title, author, keyword, etc. throughout the collection.  The only limitation is that due to their agreements with these journals, they often do not have the most recent 3 months to 1 year of the various publications.  For that we would need to go to some of our other online resources. We have IP authenticated access so you do not need a username and password , and there is no need to logout when finished . You can just close your browser. You can access it from the Library page on the Portal under Library Data Sources.  Feel free to use it as much as you want.  If you have any questions on it, or would like a quick demo on searching it, please do not hesitate to email # Information Resources and someone will walk you through the database.  And feel free to contact me with any questions or concerns. Thank you, Laura Laura Plummer Director of Information Resources Cornerstone Research 353 Sacramento Street, 19th Floor San Francisco, CA  94111 Direct Dial:  415-229-8153 Fax:  415-229-8199 Email: lplummer@cornerstone.com http://www.cornerstone.com

page_793.page_title: (20070823) 10K Wizard and Global Access Replacement LivEdgar
page_793.body_text: ​(20070823) 10K Wizard and Global Access Replacement: LivEdgar Yahoo GSI Due Dilligence Report.pdf From: Plummer, Laura To: #Cornerstone Research < #CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > Hello everyone, Over the next month we will be phasing out 10K Wizard and Global Access as our SEC filings providers.  We are replacing them both with the Thomson/GSI product, LivEdgar.  We believe that LivEdgar has the best of both products and then some!  Because LivEdgar is owned by the same company as Global Access you get all the history of Global Access, and full text search engine that blows 10K Wizard out of the water. LivEdgar offers you the ability to not just search the full text of filings, but to limit and adjust your search to suit your needs.  If you just want to search only particular sections of proxies/10Ks/8Ks/etc, you can do that, or maybe you want to search for merger agreements where Skadden was the counsel for the target and Ernst was the accountant, or you want to find reverse triangular mergers…you name it and you can find it.  You can even find all the comment letters and no-action letters associated with the companies and filings, and search them separately if you want.  SEC, NASD and NYSE rules and polices are at your fingertips, as are Canadian SEDAR filings.  You can even create your own spreadsheets of data comparing companies, deals, etc.  And this is just the tip of what you can do. (Take a look at the Yahoo Due Diligence report I downloaded with a couple clicks to get an idea of the amount of information available.) Everyone that has a 10-K Wizard ID and has used it in the last 2 years will automatically be assigned a LivEdgar ID.  You should receive it in your email in the next few weeks.  If you are not assigned one and would like one, just let me know and I will get you one.  There is a billing code requirement to log in, and the service is charged very simply: $10 to log in and $2/min.  You may download as many filings as you want, and can download them in bulk if desired (though I recommend emailing as it is faster).  If you need to order older paper filings, you can do that too.  There is an additional charge, but you can request a full quote before receiving. Most of the time they can turn around requests same day or next day at the latest.  Most filings are $25 to order, but larger ones can be more expensive. In a month's time we will close out all access to 10-K Wizard and Global Access.  In the meantime we will be setting up in-house training sessions in each office as well as offering web based training for those who cannot attend.  It is not a very difficult database to figure out, but to see all that it can do, I would HIGHLY recommend attending a session.  Their help desk is wonderful as well.  Feel free to call them for help.  If you have any questions or concerns, please do not hesitate to call or email me at anytime.  Keep an eye out for upcoming training announcements! Thanks, Laura Laura Plummer Director of Information Resources Cornerstone Research 353 Sacramento Street, 19th Floor San Francisco, CA  94111 Direct Dial:  415-229-8153 Fax:  415-229-8199 Email: lplummer@cornerstone.com http://www.cornerstone.com

page_794.body_text: ​(20070913) New Resources Opened up to Firm: Technology Law360, Energy Law360 and Employment Law360 From: Plummer, Laura To: #Cornerstone Research < #CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > Hello everyone, I am pleased to announce they we have subscribed to 3 more of the Law360 electronic publications.  We have set both the new subscriptions as well as our original five to IP authenticate.  This means you should never have to enter a username and password when accessing them from our network.  Besides reading the articles online, you can subscribe to a daily newsletter for each which summarizes the events of the past 24 hours.  Below are brief descriptions of the 3 new subscriptions. For those of you who are unaware of this product, we also have subscriptions to Competition Law360, Financial Services Law360, Health Law360, Intellectual Property Law360 and Securities Law360. To access any of these publications, simply go to the Library Resources Portal page, and will see them all listed in the drop down menu under Library Data Sources. Please do not hesitate to call or email me with any questions or issues. --Laura Technology Law360 :  A daily news service covering breaking news in technology law and litigation. The service tracks litigation involving software makers, computer makers, equipment makers, semiconductor manufacturers, telecom companies, information technology services providers, networking and wireless communications companies, and electronics retailers, among others. In addition, Technology Law360 alerts readers to changes in federal communications regulation and emerging legislation. Energy Law360 :  The newswire for legal professionals in the energy industry, covers developing stories in litigation, law and regulation. We offer the most extensive coverage of energy law available anywhere. Topics covered include Key litigation, Regulatory developments, Legislative initiatives and Law firm news.  We cover stories from across the globe, in every jurisdiction, and in every sector of the energy industry. Employment Law360 :  The newswire for legal professionals in the employment industry, covers developing stories in litigation, law and regulation. We cover stories from every jurisdiction, and in every sector of the employment industry.  Topics covered include Key litigation, Regulatory developments, Legislative initiatives and Law firm news. Energy Law360:  The newswire for legal professionals in the energy industry, covers developing stories in litigation, law and regulation. Topics covered include Key litigation, Regulatory developments, Legislative initiatives and Law firm news.  We cover stories from across the globe, in every jurisdiction, and in every sector of the energy industry.

Employment Law360:  The newswire for legal professionals in the employment industry, covers developing stories in litigation, law and regulation. We cover stories from every jurisdiction, and in every sector of the employment industry.  Topics covered include Key litigation, Regulatory developments, Legislative initiatives and Law firm news.

We will be holding BBL's or WebEx demonstrations in each office over the next month or so to introduce everyone to these and the other academic article databases that you and the Library have access to.  Be on the lookout for the session near you. --Laura Ebsco Ebsco's Business Source Corporate (BSC) database has over 3500 journals, magazines and trade publications indexed and abstracted, and 2900 of them have the full text available.  1800 of them are peer-reviewed.  Many of these go back to the 1980's and 1990's, and some go back to the 1960's!  Also available in this database are over 10,500 industry, geographical, SWOT analysis, etc. reports from Datamonitor, EIU (Economist Intelligence Unit), Bernstein Global Wealth Management and others.  Attached is a complete title list for BSC (though they are constantly adding new resources).  The library has been using this database to fill your full text request for many years. We have downloaded almost 2000 articles this year alone for you! To access this database, we have set it up to IP authenticate.  This means that as long as you are on our network, you do not need a username or password to get in.  If you go to the Library portal page, you will see a link to it in the pull-down menu under Library Data Sources.  There is no bill-back system in place at the moment, so you do not need to enter in any sort of project code.  You are free to use this for anything you are working on or studying.  You can search within fields, full text, publication, etc.  Please try to attend the presentation in your office to see all the ways you can search this database.  If you need help before that, or just have further questions, please do not hesitate to contact us at #Information Resources for more information. Social Science Research Network (SSRN) Social Science Research Network (SSRN) is devoted to the rapid worldwide dissemination of social science research and is composed of a number of specialized research networks in each of the social sciences.  Each of SSRN's networks encourages the early distribution of research results by publishing Submitted abstracts and by soliciting abstracts of top quality research papers around the world. We now have hundreds of journals, publishers, and institutions in Partners in Publishing that provide working papers for distribution through SSRN's eLibrary and abstracts for publication in SSRN's electronic journals.  The SSRN eLibrary consists of two parts: an Abstract Database containing abstracts on over 164,400 scholarly working papers and forthcoming papers and an Electronic Paper Collection currently containing over 131,100 downloadable full text documents in Adobe Acrobat PDF format. The eLibrary also includes the research papers of a number of Fee Based Partner Publications. Many of you are already familiar with SSRN, and have discovered that many of the papers on their website are available at no cost already.  Some do require a nominal fee (usually $5), and the library is happy to help you retrieve those when you find them.  What our subscription entails is access to their elibrary for each of the networks to which we are subscribing (Accounting, Economics, Financial Economics, Legal Scholarship and Management Research Network).  Most of the publications in their elibrary are offered at no additional cost to subscribers, but there are a few publishers that will still require a fee.  You can completely search SSRN without ever subscribing to the networks.  The networks will allow you to receive their ejournals which are like announcements with abstracts and links when new research or papers are added to SSRN in a particular area or from a particular school or publisher. We will add a link to the Library Portal under Library Data Sources, but unfortunately we cannot IP authenticate this database, nor can we set up automatic subscriber lists.  You will need to subscribe to each network that you are interested in.  (If you prefer, you can send me an email listing the networks you want to be added to, and I can add you in, but you will have to go in later to choose which journals you wish to subscribe to.)  The attached PowerPoint will lead you step-by-step through the subscribing process and the signing up for the ejournals.  Below are also some samples of a few of the ejournals you can choose once you have subscribed.  Each Network has many ejournals from which to choose.  Again, I ask that you please try to attend the demonstration in your office to learn how the subscription process works.  If you cannot attend, or need access sooner, please do not hesitate to contact #Information Resources for assistance. page_797.body_text: ​(20071105) New TOC Routing System starting at the Stone and open to Everyone! From: Plummer, Laura To: #Cornerstone Research < #CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > Are you tired of having to look through a bunch of TOC just to get to the one reporter or journal you want to see? Do you want to see the TOC as soon as the journal arrives as opposed to waiting until the others like it show up? Would you rather just have someone send you the TOC of just the journals you want? Well , you are in luck as we have completely revamped our TOC system. You will no longer get an email with a link that has the TOC of all reporters or all academic journals in it.  Instead, you will go to the Library Portal Page, and click on Routing List in the menu bar.  This will take you to a page that lists all the journals we get here in SF (soon we will add any missing from Boston as well).  Check off the ones you want to receive and click Submit.  We will add you to that routing list, and you will receive an email containing just the title you checked off, and on the day of its arrival to our Library.  No more waiting; no more scanning through a bunch of other titles to get to your favorite! If you see an article you want, simply reply to the email and tell us what article you want and we will email it on out to you.  It's that simple.  Please do not hesitate to call or email me with any questions you may have. --Laura Laura Plummer Director of Information Resources Cornerstone Research 353 Sacramento Street, 19th Floor San Francisco, CA  94111 Direct Dial:  415-229-8153 Fax:  415-229-8199 Email: lplummer@cornerstone.com http://www.cornerstone.com

page_805.body_text: ​ Institutional Ownership data: CC in email: Chen, Rui; Kim, Brian; Armstrong, Matt Please note that this data was retrieved from Eikon.   It is basically the same data we were retrieving previously, but formatted differently and from a different platform.  To parse the data, utilize the ffitools web application provided by the Data Science Center, which can be found at: https://data-science.crpages.com/.   If you have any questions, please contact Rui or Brian (Cced) in the Data Science Center. Considerations when using Eikon: 1. Sometimes Eikon picks up a proxy filing instead of a 13-F filing. In these cases, our current program identifies these as insiders and excludes (consistent with the old VBA float program). The webapp outputs these investors that get excluded from the data. Analysts need to be aware of this output and review to make sure that there are not any institutional investors excluded that should not be. a. We have asked Refinitiv about a couple specific cases of them picking up the proxy instead of the 13-F and they respond saying that it was an error on their end. They refreshed the data and it is fixed. So, if an analyst runs into this, the Eikon help desk will be very useful. 2. Sometimes Eikon picks up a 13-G filing instead of a 13-F filing. A 13-G filing is an abbreviated filing of a 13-D and can be used to report holdings of a company greater than 5% and in which the investor is not seeking to influence company operations (i.e. passive investments). In these cases, the institutional investor will also disclose these holdings in a 13-F. Sometimes, Eikon picks up the 13-G as well. This is something else that the Data Science team is working on. a. We have asked Refinitiv about a couple specific cases of them picking up the 13-G instead of 13-F. They said it was a mistake on their part and have refreshed the data. Again, this is an issue that analysts should be aware of and discuss with the Eikon help desk as needed. b. Analysts should compare the 13-F only to the all filings results and investigate any large differences.

page_807.body_text: ​ Source Markit ABX.HE Indices How to Cite the Source Description Markit was founded in 2001 as the first independent source of credit derivative pricing.  The most frequently requested Markit data is their ABX.HE indices . Time Period Covered 2006-Present Access License required. Note: Markit will not sell data to us. Cost ABX Indices - $25,000 for each license.  Includes all historical data for all ABX.HE tranches plus one year of data updates.  License is only for one client matter. Other indices including PrimeX - As of 11/22/11 all index data requests, no matter how small, are a minimum of $12,500 Other types of data are available from Markit. The absolute minimum for any non-index data is $7,500. Short Sales data is available for up to 5 different securities a year for $5,000 each. We can use it for litigation.  But we need to be able to tell them the type of case it is and who the client is.  If it is a standard 10b-5 securities case, it is generally not an issue, but if it is something else, they may refuse to give it to us.  If we are going to have to turn it over, it is better to make that arrangement when we purchase the data.  It is an extra $5k to be allowed to turn it over.  But it cannot be made public, nor can the opposing side use the data for their own work.  It will be turned over for the sole purpose of reviewing our work. Attached is a sample of the data and their data dictionary explaining the fields that are available.  If you have any questions regarding this, please do not hesitate to contact Laura Londa. Contact (within CR or Vendor) For specific questions about data, contact Markit's Credit Data Team: Tel. 917.441.6654 (9am-5:30pm ET) Markit website David Del Zotto Assistant Vice President Equity Sales Markit 620 8th Avenue New York, NY, 10018 + 1 212 863 9400 Office + 1 917 940 5639 Mobile David.DelZotto@markit.com Cornerstone Comments Unfortunately, smaller custom requests are not available for the ABX.HE indices.  They only sell licenses for the entire run of indices data. Both the spread data and pricing are included for $25K FYI Costs can increase significantly if the data is being used for litigation as opposed to a non-litigation project.  Prices will also vary based on who will see the data and who will see the analysis that used the data.  Markit also requires that the client number and matter number be written in the contract to assure it will only be used for that matter.  They often also require the name of client. Attached is a sample of the data and their data dictionary explaining the fields that are available. Difference in Short Sales data between Markit and Bloomberg There are three main reasons, all of which relate to how Bloomberg gets its data vs. Markit.  Bloomberg gets its data from the exchange and the reporting entities are U.S. broker dealers.  Markit gets its data from its global clients (custodians, prime brokers, hedge funds), which give Markit data on their securities lending activity (custodian), securities borrowing activity (prime brokers), and cost of borrowing (hedge funds).  Markit uses its proprietary data on securities lending to proxy for short interest whereas Bloomberg gives the reported numbers.  The reasons for the data differences are: Bloomberg’s data includes naked shorts, which option market makers are allowed to do.  Since shares are not borrowed in this scenario, Markit data would not reflect it. When an investor (e.g., a hedge fund) wants to short, it will go to its prime broker to borrow shares.  Depending on the situation, the prime broker may lend out shares from its own inventory (e.g., from their proprietary trading desk) rather than go out and borrow shares from a custodian.  This usually makes the cost of borrowing lower, but tends to happen only for blue chip stocks where shares are plentiful.  This type of shorting would be reported in Bloomberg’s data, but not in Markit’s (presumably because the prime broker didn’t actually borrow shares). Markit’s clients are global and includes firms that do not report to the exchange.  For example, if a foreign firm wants to short a U.S. stock, that would not be reported in Bloomberg, but would potentially be captured by Markit. Sample or additional information (including cross references) Subject: Economics Type: Bond Indices ​

page_810.page_title: Copyright DOs and DON'Ts for IR
page_810.body_text: Copyright DOs and DON'Ts for IR Start an academic literature tracker or add to it whenever you look up a book or article for billable client matter.  If starting a tracker for a new matter, open template and save right away as new matter name.  This avoids adding your information to the template. Even if it's from EBSCO or another subscription, it's more efficient to do it now and have a record that it was already checked than to look again at everything when the case is filing You can even attribute the time spent doing this to the request! When working on DRU/DCL, check files to make sure they can be used. Examples of what cannot be used: Items from ResearchGate or Academia.edu, as these are for research use only. Items with timestamp older than a year. Items that were obviously licensed to someone else (e.g., HBR case studies that have note at bottom about being downloaded via a university for educational use only) Items that are not available using our subscription sources and for which we have no record of purchase. Books that we don't own or don't have a record of purchasing. Items that were obviously purchased for another client matter. If purchasing a case study from HBR, always purchase 1 pdf and 2 permissions. Keep in mind that many of our experts get access to items using their university accounts, which are only to be used for educational purposes and by university employees, students, etc. Fill out all fields in tracker. Include ISSN or ISBN (or CCC identifier) unless you are clear in the Notes column that the item is covered by one of our subscriptions (e.g., CCC, EBSCO, JSTOR, ProQuest, etc.) Authors (last name only) and Journal/Publication Titles can be helpful later. When someone is on deadline, they can filter the workbook/spreadsheet and sort by these columns to see if something on a DRU/DCL list has already been taken care of - SHOW EXAMPLE In first column, include only last names In publication title, don't include "The" at the beginning of a publication name If the publication is a book, use the book title rather than the chapter title (unless there's a compelling reason to use the latter) Always fill in your initials and the date you worked on it as this is extremely helpful for someone else when working on the same matter in the future. Check the list in NetDocs after saving to be sure that you saved the correct version.

Go to Remote Desktop Server: sqlsfgen1 Launch CRSPSift (there should be a shortcut on the desktop). The first time you use it after a monthly update, you need to add the latest Environment. Click on New. Go to Environment Scanner . You will need to Add the Location: C:\CRSP\Data Click on Start Scan. Any data that has not been added under your profile will show up. Add latest. Close. Then make that the default. Find latest (usually at the bottom of the list). Click Edit. Click Default Environment. Apply To run a query: Click latest, then Time Series Access, then OK. Open Query. Go to <C:\CRSP\CRSP Team Folder\CRSPSift Requests>. Choose <Default Daily Query.tsp.kls>. If more than 1 security: On your desktop, open \\Sqlsfgen1\crsp . Go to: \\Sqlsfgen1\crsp\CRSP Team Folder\CRSPSift Requests . Launch: <input.csv>, it will open in Excel. Columns are PERMNO, StartDate, EndDate. You can paste the list of PERMNOs and Start Dates and End Dates. Date format is YYYYMMDD. Save file as CSV.  Excel will ask if you want to keep it in this format; YES, YOU DO! Close file. You will get an error from CRSPSift if you have this file open. Continue with instructions listed under If only for 1 security -> Go to Data Items tab. Add new items if needed by Searching (you have to chose the tab) and then Add to Query.  They will be added to the bottom of the list. Go to Date tab. Make sure Start Date and End Date cover the range you are seeking. All other options usually do not change.  We usually want Daily data. Go to Layout Tab. Change the Field Delimeter from No Delimeter to Comma . No need to check the Direct Edit or Notes tabs. Verify [1]. Execute [2]. On the Server, go to <C:\CRSP\CRSP Team Folder>. You can email it or copy it from the Server folder on your desktop to the folder the requestor indicates or send a link to the file. You may need to open the .txt file to confirm that the delimeter was indeed changed to comma.  If not, try again. Close CRSPSift by doing File -> Exit.  Answer No to All about saving changes. Sign Out of the Server.  Do not just close the window. I've uploaded the two Bloomberg.com presentations 
that we talked about yesterday.

1. BloombergLaw.com for news, litigation and other 
legal materials

You can search for US districts and for state 
dockets. The search options (i.e. search for dockets in SDNY for copyright cases 
with motions to dismiss) and the output options are much more sophisticated than 
in Pacer.

You can also set up docket tracks and alerts or save 
searches.

Other cool features are:- BL gets the complaints hours or days before Pacer or Westlaw 
(for some districts).- Docket 
Analytics lets you run federal litigation profiles reports by Law Firms, 
Litigant, Case Types, etc. (think about Counsel Monitor)

- It searches the available documents in the 
dockets - not only the dockets' texts- You can search by source: statutes, legislative materials, rules, 
opinions, patents- You can do quick 
citations search even if you don't know the exact citation format (i.e. 552 us 
148)- It has some international 
legal materials

with timestamps (you can search the news by topics. e.g. "securities" will 
search the concept of securities not for the word.

All the above and more are included in a flat fee 
contract for unlimited subscribers.

2. BloombergLaw.com for a Corporate Transactional 
Practice

When you conduct a company search under  Company and 
Market  you'll get news, financials, filings, docket analytics, historical stock 
price, corporate actions, institutional holdings etc. on the same results page

letters)- Class action news- Law blogs

​Browser 
Errors in Thomson One Banker Hi Guys, Andrea and I have had a browser error lately where, 
after signing into One Banker, the company search box that usually appears in 
the upper left corner of the screen fails to materialize. The solution we've found is to clear your temporary 
internet files by clicking on Internet Options from the browser Tools menu.  
Once inside the "General" tab, click "Delete…", select Temporary Internet Files 
(you can keep everything else), and click "Delete.   Once your files are 
deleted,  close all browser windows and open your browser again.  TOB should 
work fine again.  I've noticed I've had to do this once a week or so lately, 
depending on usage. Hope this helps, Peter Gigante Information Specialist CORNERSTONE RESEARCH 353 Sacramento Street, 23rd Floor San Francisco, CA  94111-3685 415.229.8227 direct www.cornerstone.com

CourtLink​ Hi All, Just wanted to send out a quick summary of what I 
learned during my brief conversation with the Lexis rep yesterday: CourtLink started scanning and running OCR on 
complaints around March 2009.  They cover all US Federal Civil cases and some 
key state courts (I believe the number she gave was about 30 state courts)  This 
allows users to search the full-text of the docket and/or the full-text of the 
complaint.  Also, you can set up docket alerts based on words or phrases in the 
complaint. I've been asked about searching complaints by members 
of an IP development project and I'm betting others have had similar requests in 
the past.  If you have any examples you want to bring up during the 
presentation, Lexis Leslie said she'd be happy to run some live search 
examples. Also, CourtLink comes with the Lexis version of 
Monitor Suite (f.k.a. CounselMonitor).  She'll also give a quick overview of 
their expert witness document collection (depositions, testimony, CV's, 
etc)

etracking in the NY state system2​ From: Gigante, Peter 
(10/9/2009) To: #Library < Library@cornerstone.com > E-TRACK was the system I 
was talking about that allows you to track a docket with in the state courts.  
Since the NY state cases we want seem to be primarily in the state supreme court 
(which is not the highest court in the state http://www.courts.state.ny.us/courts/structure.shtml ), WebCivil Supreme is where you'll find the dockets of 
interest. http://iapps.courts.state.ny.us/webcivil/etrackFAQ An important thing to notice in NY state supreme 
court dockets: In many state and federal courts, a judge is assigned 
as soon as the case is filed.  New York takes a different approach.  Under the 
New York rules, a judge is not assigned to a case until one of the parties files 
a Request for Judicial Intervention (or "RJI") Form with the clerk.  Prior to 
the plaintiff filing an RJI, the court's only role is to issue an index number 
and be a repository for filed documents. This one page form triggers the court's 
actual entry into the case.  My guess would be that allowing cases to be filed 
without immediately involving the judges was to encourage out of court 
settlements, as there is a filing fee for the RJI. So what does this 
mean? WebCivil Supreme only displays cases for which a Request 
for Judicial Intervention (RJI) has been filed. You can manually add recently 
filed Supreme Court cases to your eTrack account and commence receiving 
notifications when an RJI is filed. Simply click on the "Add a Pre-RJI Case" 
link and enter the County, Index Number, Year of Filing and the Plaintiff and 
Defendant names.  You will not receive any email updates from eTrack unless and 
until an RJI is filed.  You can generally find the index number from the County 
Clerk's site: SCROLL http://iapps.courts.state.ny.us/iscroll/FNF913.htm I'll toss this on CRIKIT too.  It's free and public 
so why not. Peter Gigante Information Specialist CORNERSTONE RESEARCH 353 Sacramento Street, 23rd Floor San Francisco, CA  94111-3685 415.229.8227 direct 415.229.8199 fax www.cornerstone.com

RECAP: Free alternative to PACER​? From: Czegledi, Katalin 
(10/9/2009) To: Londa, Laura < llonda@cornerstone.com > CC: #Library 
< Library@cornerstone.com > All, RECAP https://www.recapthelaw.org/about/ is a project of the Center for Information Technology 
Policy at Princeton 
University. It is an “add on" for the Firefox web browser therefore it works 
only with Firefox. When a registered person with RECAP 
downloads a document from PACER the document will automatically be downloaded to 
RECAP too and will be available for other RECAP users. When a RECAP user searches PACER and 
the document is available for download, RECAP puts a small icon next to the 
official PACER link. That means users always have a choice between downloading 
the free RECAP version (if one is available) or paying for the PACER 
version. One of the downsides of it I read about 
is that it's possible for "hackers" to upload documents to the RECAP collection 
that are not really from Pacer. Also, Cornerstone does not recommend 
installing Firefox on Cornerstone computers. To make it short RECAP is simply data sharing among Pacer users and probably not for 
us. -Katalin . _____________________________________________ From: Londa, Laura Sent: Monday, September 
28, 2009 10:45 AM To: #Library Subject: FW: Free alternative to PACER? Anyone want to volunteer to take a look 
at RECAP and report back to the group? ______________________________________________ From: VanDeventer, Paul Sent: Monday, September 
28, 2009 10:40 AM To: Londa, Laura Subject: Free alternative to PACER? Hi Laura, You may have already heard of this or seen the 
article, but there was a neat article in the LA Times about cheaper or free 
governmental data, including court filings.  I thought you (and IR) might be 
interested, for example, in a free alternative to PACER.  Apologies if you have 
already heard of this or seen the article, or feel free to ignore if it's not 
useful: < http://www.latimes.com/business/la-fi-hiltzik28-2009sep28,0,6508895,full.column > Here's the most relevant part Among his tools -- and the 
neatest transparency application I've seen -- is an add-on for the Firefox Web 
browser called RECAP (yes, PACER spelled backward), developed at Princeton 
University. If you run a PACER search, RECAP will tell you via an 
on-screen icon whether a given document can be downloaded for free from its own 
database. If you download something not yet available, RECAP automatically adds 
it to the free database, in a sort of digital Kumbaya. This cuts into the 
courts' PACER revenue of $10 million a year, which may be why PACER has 
responded with a 
rather prickly warning about RECAP on its 
site. Paul Van

hearings: http://www.gpoaccess.gov/chearings/about.html Congressional 
Hearings: About A hearing is a meeting or session of a Senate, House, joint, or special 
committee of Congress, usually open to the public, to obtain information and 
opinions on proposed legislation, conduct an investigation, or evaluate/oversee 
the activities of a government department or the implementation of a Federal 
law. In addition, hearings may also be purely exploratory in nature, providing 
testimony and data about topics of current interest. Most 
congressional hearings are published two months to two years after they are 
held. NOTE: Not all congressional hearings are available on GPO Access . Whether or not a hearing is disseminated on GPO 
Access depends on the committee. GPO Access contains selected House and Senate hearings for the 105th 
Congress (1997-98) forward. The House and Senate appropriations hearings for 
fiscal year 1998 are included. Documents are available as ASCII text and Adobe Portable Document Format 
(PDF) files. Graphics, including scanned images of camera ready copy are omitted 
from the ASCII text version but are contained in the PDF files. Catalogs are available for the 105th Congress to the present. Links are 
included with each congressional hearing listed in the catalog, which retrieve 
the text of the corresponding document as an ASCII text or PDF file. GPO 
Access continues to add hearings irregularly as they become available 
during each session of Congress. If a congressional hearing is not listed in the

about this new service option. Kristina Eden Michigan Information Transfer Source (734) 763-5060 mits.mail@umich.edu

​FINRA: Trade Level Trace Data 20140820: In response to a request about FINRA data: As of August 20, 2014, we already have some FINRA data in-house that was 
purchased for another case, so the $2000 set-up fee is waived.  So the cost for 
your case (by the way, what case is this?) would be $2000 per calendar year for 
the entire dataset, but this does not allow for turning over the data if 
needed.  To turn over the data, it costs additionally $1 per security per year 
up to a $1000/year max.  They do not provide data for single securities. Be aware that it can take a week or more to receive the data once requested. We 
have to go over and sign the contract, then FINRA requires payment before they 
release the data. However they will not accept payment before the invoice has 
been issued. It can take 3 or more days to get the invoice. After that, we can 
wire the money, and they will pull the data after that and send it. It might 
take an additional day for them to pull the data together for us. If you'd 
like to pursue this option, we can arrange this for you. issues From: Marcus, David 
(9/8/2009) To: #Securities Practice < #SecuritiesPractice@cornerstone.com > CC: Goodman, Andrea < AGoodman@cornerstone.com >; Londa, 
Laura < llonda@cornerstone.com > Attachment Link Anyone relying on IBES data should be aware of the attached 
article.  It shows that historical IBES data changes depending upon the download 
date, in a non-random way.  For example: "We find that between 1.6% and 
21.7% of matched observations are different from one download to the next.  The 
changes, which include alterations of recommendation levels, additions and 
deletions of records, and removal of analyst names, are non-random in nature: 
They cluster by analyst reputation, brokerage firm size and status, and 
recommendation boldness. The changes have a large and significant impact on the 
classification of trading signals and back-tests of three stylized facts: The 
profitability of trading signals, the profitability of changes in consensus 
recommendations, and persistence in individual analyst stock-picking 
ability." The paper was published in the August 2009 JF.

alternative way did. kc A. An easy

the document in the new Outlook message, i.e. <link> For example 
< \\crwadmin1\consulting\somefilename.doc > Copy the link from your Outlook message into your page Alter the text of the link if you would 
like to display a simple text rather than the path to the folder or the document For example replace

click Insert Link (click the right mouse button ot the chain 
link icon on the editor's bar) You need the "Link to" part of the Search 
tab in Make link dialog. Next you have a 
choice. You can either 
(a) in the "Link To" portion of the Search Tab type your link in the format file://link/ For example, if

replace backslashes (\) with forward slashes (/) or (b) In the "Link 
To" portion of the Search tab type file:/// wait for a file icon to appear at the right of

document or folder next, in the "Link to" part of the Search

On the Varonis page, click on 'Membership Requests' on the left pane. 3- On

requesting membership for others, click 'Change Users/Groups', then search for 
and 'Add' members to the list in section #1 * 4 - In Section #2 on the Membership Requests form, click 'Browse' and 
search for the group name(s) that you are requesting access to 5 - Click 
'Add' so that the group(s) now appear in section # 3 “Operations”. IMPORTANT: 
Make sure that the Available Operation says "Grant Membership". If it says 
"Revoke Membership" then you are already a member and you should log off your 
computer and log back in to gain access to the folder 5- Type in a brief 
reason of why you are making the request in section #4 (i.e. "Just added to the case team") 6- Click 
'Finish' The system will then automatically send out requests to designated group 
members for approval. Please let us know if any of this is unclear, or does not 
work for you, and we'll be happy to assist. Thank you *a failed submission when adding multiple people means that one or more are 
already in the group you’re trying to add them to. If this happens, please 
submit requests one user at a time. Regards, Sonia Lara

5: California Law by Laura A. Cadra Chapter 
6: Bibliography of California Resources by Patrick Meyer Chapter

9: Assisting Self-Represented Litigants by Laura A. Cadra & June Kim Chapter 
10: Bibliography of Self-Help Resources by Lisa Schultz Chapter

Allen-Hart Chapter

following information is available through SDC? We want to know certain details 
for M&A transactions between 2005 and 2009 where the target was a tire 
manufacturing company. The specific metrics that we are interested in for the 
transaction are goodwill, net assets, net assets purchased, purchase price and 
transaction costs. If it is available, we would like a

Service Request: 1-4340364154 from Thomson Reuters Service Request: 
1-4340364154 Hi Katalin/ Stephen, Please find the resolution to 
your query below. Please note that Form 13F is a quarterly report of 
equity holdings filed with the SEC by institutional investment managers having 
equity assets under management of $100 million or more. Included in this 
category are certain banks, insurance companies, investment advisors, investment 
companies, foundations and pension funds. Non US institutional investment 
managers are required to file a Form 13F if they use any means or 
instrumentality of United States interstate commerce in the course of their 
business; and (2) exercise investment discretion over $100 million or more in 
Section 13(F) securities. Thus, if the filer is required to file form 13F 
(provided that equity assets invested in 13F securities is $100 million or 
more), holdings for Volkswagen ADR should be included in the report. With 
regards to the list that you’ve gotten from SEC, I am not sure why Volkswagen 
ADR is not included in the list.  I have run the current holders report (see 
attached file) of Volkswagen ADR and Parametric Portfolio Associates LLC 
reported its holdings of Volkswagen ADR in its Q4 ’09 13F report.  See below 
link for the 13F filing. Dated: 12.31.09 http://sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/932859/000119312510027043/d13fhr.txt Please

19, 2010 9:09 AM To: Czegledi, Katalin Subject: RE: RE: Service Request: 
1-4340364154 from Thomson Reuters Hi Katalin, Please find the 
resolution to your query below. Aggregated Mutual Funds - These are 
institutional positions derived from cumulative mutual fund holdings. These 
holdings are captured from individual mutual fund portfolios, and typically 
represent a proportion of the total shares held by an Investment 
Advisor. To answer your questions: A mutual fund pools the money 
of thousands of different shareholders to be used in collective investments such 
as equity stocks, bonds, cash, and short-term market instruments. A portfolio 
manager handles the trading of the fund's underlying investments and monitors 
the gains and losses of the mutual fund. Information is gathered from 
various Institutions and data sources. These are reported on a monthly, 
quarterly, semi-annual and/or annual basis. *   EDGAR filings *   
FTP *   SEDAR *   Institution Contacts (Phone calls, emails, faxes, 
published reports) *   Third Party Vendors *   Regulatory 
Agencies *   Institution websites *   Financial Publications and 
Newspapers *   Stock Exchanges It is not classified as a "regulatory 
filing per se" because not all mutual funds disclose their holdings in 
regulatory agencies.  US mutual funds disclose their holdings via N30D filing in 
SEC, Canadian Funds discloses in SEDAR, and other mutual funds discloses 
holdings from the above mentioned sources. Mutual fund holdings are only 
part of the total holdings since it represents only the institutional position.  
Declarable Stakes/Substantial positions are not included in the Mutual Fund 
holdings.  However, for Declarable Stakes position, they are not required by law 
to disclose their positions if they did not meet the required threshold (in a 
given country) for disclosure. Regarding 13F holdings, the 13F 
filer/firm will file the holdings mostly for US stocks that he is managing in 
his 13F reports.  If it is US stock, the 13F filer will also file for the 
holdings he discloses in the Mutual Fund portfolio in his 13F report.  This is 
why 13F positions supersede Aggregate MF position in the product. Please 
see attached file for example (Lufthansa's shareholder report). In the 
attached file (highlighted in yellow), BlackRock Investment Management, LLC is 
managing the funds highlighted in blue.  The 21311157 shares of BlackRock came 
from Declarable Stakes (DS) position.  The reason why BlackRock is reflecting 
the position coming from Declarable Stakes rather than MF is because it 
represents the complete holdings of BlackRock in Lufthansa, whereas the MF 
position represents only the institutional positions.  However, as previously 
mentioned, companies are not required to file if they did not meet the required 
threshold for disclosure.  Hence if there are no DS or 13F position, the 
cumulative holdings of the underlying funds will reflect as the holdings of 
BlackRock.  This doesn't mean though that these are the only positions held by 
BlackRock.  It's possible that BlackRock are still holding the DS shares but it 
was not captured by the content team since the company no longer discloses the 
holdings. Kindly note: Declarable Stake/Substantial - a position which 
meets or exceeds the minimum disclosure threshold in a given country. This 
information can be sourced from stock exchanges, regulatory sources, third party 
data vendors, newspaper publications, legally approved websites and direct 
company contact. Do revert to us if you require further clarifications. 
Thank you for your

​Ownership Data Questions (Thomson) 5/7/2009 From: sarah.inman@thomsonreuters.com To: Londa, 
Laura; Stasch, Melinda; Goodman, Andrea; Gigante, Peter; Czegledi, Katalin; 
Percy, Joanne; Chiappetta, Sarah Attachment Link Hi All, Thanks for your time 
today. Below is some written 
explanation that Adam had provided me, in addition – there is some additional 
data within the Ownership Glossary (screenshot of where this is in the Help Menu 
is attached).  Let me know if you have any follow up questions on the 
below: 1. The ThomsonONE data 
involves a lot more extensive value-add than the ShareWorld data.   Because of 
the value add there can be significantly more holders listed on the ThomsonONE 
side. Within ThomsonONE, 
whenever possible we attribute institutional ownership to that of investment 
discretion, meaning whoever calls the shots with the $ should have that $ tagged 
to the particular institution. In the case of the of a 
Fidelity 13F Filing for example, from our contact with the firm, and tracking 
their reports historically we know that there are in fact two separate pieces of 
this 13F which have their own investment discretion.  The bulk goes to FMR, a 
portion though is separated out and assigned to the firm Pyramis Global 
Advisors.  To top the situation off, there is a second set of value add done to 
the Fidelity filing, because we combine the holdings (excluding Pyramis), with a 
second 13F filed under the name FIL Ltd., and those combined constitute what we 
disclose as the Fidelity portfolio. 2. Some general 
background on why the issue with positions exceeding shares outstanding happens. 
 To say they ‘often’ exceed the shares outstanding in a particular quarter is a 
bit of a misconception.  This is wholely dependent on an individual security 
basis.  It may often be an issue for a particular security, but not for all 
securities.  Of the thousands upon thousands of securities we’re tracking 
ownership for I would say less than 1% have their shares held exceeding there 
Shares Out. The reasons for such a 
thing occurring can be any number of a few things, I’ll give you some examples, 
to help you get a better understanding. 1- The 
13F filings themselves -  
13Fs are reported on an individual basis by investment firms.  There is a 
possibility that certain positions could be reported more than once to the SEC. 
 We actively remove filers portfolios from the products if we know they are not 
managing any equity assets in house themselves despite the fact that they file. 
 As an example the California State Teachers Retirement System files as 13F for 
$15 Billion, yet they manage none of that $ themselves, as it outsourced to 
outside investment managers, who are undoubtedly reporting the positions as 
well.  In this case we can remove the assets because we know they aren’t 
managing any of those assets themselves, but oftentimes we are not able to 
identify firms that are doing this (or they are outsourcing a portion of their 
assets to other firms).  In the situation unfortunately there will always be 
unavoidable double counting of assets.  Positions for other pension fund filers, 
are ones that could typically be taken with a grain of salt because they may not 
have discretion over everything they file for. 2- Dates -  While 13Fs are 
pegged to a particular date, if aggregated institutional data is included, the 
aggregate can be made up of fund disclosures from anywhere up to the last 2 
years.  So aggregate ‘dates’ and totals are not really written in stone. 3- The 
Security itself -  we are reliant on 
the shares outstanding figures that the securities themselves are providing to 
the general public.  We have at times run into circumstances, where we have 
different numbers for shares outstanding between source types because the 
company may not have had a complete understanding in what they were going to 
provide. Regards, Sarah Sarah 
Inman Major

4262  Fax: (301) 545-4727 Mobile : (617) 901 
2768 sarah.in man@thomsonreuters.com thomsonreuters.com

Pharma Research - Patents on Biologics​ The pages from the 
Orange Book are on the LAN now. So after some more research, I 
think it’s going to be harder to come up with a definite answer than I 
originally thought. There has been a lot of discussion that: The new Biologics Act does not require any 
notice of relevant patents to the FDA, by the holders of patents on biological 
products licensed under the BCA, and it does not require that the FDA publish 
any listing of such patents. There is no Orange Book. Instead, the new Biologics 
Act creates a complex procedure for identification and litigation of potentially 
relevant patents, independent of any period of data exclusivity. The new 
Biologics Act allows the FDA to grant an application for approval of a 
biosimilar or interchangeable product without regard to the existence of any 
patent. So, we have to get 
creative. Here are some suggestions, in recommended order: 1) We could look into infringement 
litigation surrounding a particularly biologic and see what patents are 
asserted. 2) We could look at analogous patents in 
the EU. 3) We could search PTO’s records, though 
as I said before this might make some muddled waters. 4) We could try to pose the question to 
the companies directly (It’s a long shot but they may be able to give us a 
number without indicating the exact patents) Peter Gigante X8227 _____________________________________________ From: Liu, Heidi Sent: Wednesday, November 16, 2011 12:28

Regulation SHO and Threshold Lists​ From: Arya, Vishal 
(2/13/2009) To: Goodman, Andrea < AGoodman@cornerstone.com > The daily archives of the threshold 
lists are available from 1/7/05. ftp://ftp.nasdaqtrader.com/symboldirectory/regsho/ Starting on July 10, 2006, the SEC 
began reporting threshold lists where securities violated either Reg SHO OR Rule 
3210.  Definitions below. Subject to the 
requirements of SEC Rule 203 of Regulation SHO Where there is an aggregate fail to 
deliver position for five consecutive settlement days at a registered clearing 
agency totaling 10,000 shares or more and equal to at least 0.5% of the issuer’s 
total shares outstanding. When this occurs, the security becomes subject to 
mandatory close-out requirements outlined in the SEC's Regulation 
SHO. The allowed values 
are: Y = Yes, if the issue is subject to 
mandatory close-out requirements of Regulation SHO N = No, if the issue is NOT subject 
to mandatory close-out requirements of Regulation SHO Subject to the 
requirements of NASD Rule 3210 Where, for five consecutive 
settlement days, there are aggregate fails to deliver at a registered clearing 
agency of 10,000 shares or more and the reported last sale during normal market 
hours would value the aggregate fail to deliver position at $50,000 or more. 
When this occurs, the security becomes subject to mandatory close-out 
requirements outlined in NASD Rule 3210. The allowed values 
are: Y = Yes, if the issue is subject to 
mandatory close-out requirements of Rule 3210. N = No, if the issue is NOT subject 
to mandatory close-out requirements of Rule 3210. From: Goodman,

(6/4/2009) To: #Library < Library@cornerstone.com > Thought you all might be 
interested in this. A 
patent portal and list of 20 patent search tools I had not realized that so many search tools are

popular patent search systems. You can also share your knowledge and expertise

Search; MicroPatent; PatentWeb; PatAnalyst; PatBase; PatBase Express; Patent 
Analysis Search System; Patent Lens; QPAT; Qweb; SumoBrain; SureChem; Surf-IP; 
Thomson Innovation; TotalPatent; and WIPS Global (See my post of Jan. 3, 2009: 
law departments and patents for management systems and software.). Laura L. Londa Director of Information 
Resources CORNERSTONE RESEARCH 353 Sacramento Street, 23rd Floor San Francisco, CA  94111-3685 415.229.8153 direct 415.229.8199 fax www.cornerstone.com

SDC-Platinum request​ From: Donnelly, 
Rob To: #Information Resources InformationResources@cornerstone.com We would like a table of the follow: The top 250 acquirers ranked by the total dollar value of 
their mergers and acquisitions. In addition to the total deal value, we also 
would like to see the total numbers of deals by these acquirers. Acquisitions should be included if they meet the following 
criteria: -Acquirer is a US company (Target company could be from any 
country) -Announced between 1/1/1992 and 9/12/2008 -Merger or an acquisition of majority control (exclude 
LBOs) -Deal was completed -The acquirer should not be a private equity firm, 
management, or investors. If there is no such a filter, then we would like to 
include only deals where the acquirer is a public company. To do this: Once you have the cut of records, go to Analysis Tab, New Custom In this window, go to the Acquiror Tab, choose Acquiror Company, hit OK Next window on the Express Tab, choose how you want the data ranked, i.e. by 
number of transactions or deal value, etc.  Also choose # of deals you want 
shown (Show Top X) Go to Advanced Ta.  Choose which columns you want. DONE

(3/26/2010) To: Gigante, Peter < pgigante@cornerstone.com >; #Library < Library@cornerstone.com > Peter, I recently investigated intraday trades for pink 
sheets. There is no source. OTC sources 1. NYSE, but they only 
archive the EOD data. ArcaBook data is available on a historical/end-of-day 
basis in flat file format, enabling you to recreate the limit order book for any 
given time. 2. QuoteMedia. -  They only archive the most current week

trade data. 4. OTCBB – end of day trade data only 5.

about when the forecast gets changed from a Quarter 2 forecast to Quarter 1? So, 
for example, an analyst has an active forecast for Q4 2015, announced before the 
Q3 2015 results so it’s recorded as Quarter 2 in “forecast period indicator”. 
Then the Q3 2015 actual results come out, but the analyst does not update his 
forecast. Is this Quarter 2 forecast still counted as part of the consensus of 
forecasts for Q4 2015? Yes Let’s say then that he does release a new report, but the forecast remains 
unchanged. In this case, is there a new record with Quarter 1 in there, or does 
the old record with Quarter 2 again just get an updated review date? The old record with Quarter 2 again just gets an updated review date As some context for my other questions, we’re trying to calculate the 
consensus forecast not just for a particular period, but for a particular period 
as of a particular date, to see how that changes. So relating to that: ·         Regarding stop estimates. Say for example, we have a record that is 
a forecast for Q1 2012. And let’s say for example that the announce stop date is 
12/4/2011. ·         If we want to calculate the analyst 
forecast consensus as of 12/1/2011, should we include that record, since 
the stop date is after the date we want to calculate the consensus as of, or exclude that record, since the period being forecasted is after the 
announce stop date? Include the record ·         Similar question for excluded estimates – you mentioned in previous 
email that an excluded record should only be included if the exclude end date is 
before the period reports. What if the date we’re calculating the consensus as 
of is either: o   Before the exclude date, or ·         After the exclude end date, but before the 
period reports Include the forecast in both cases ·         Also a point of clarification for the exclusions. They seem to 
apply to specific forecasts. Since one broker often updates their forecast 
several times, during the exclusion period for their latest forecast, should 
their second latest forecast instead be counted in the consensus? Or should we 
completely exclude that broker from the consensus during the exclusion 
period? Do not include the broker’s forecast in the consensus.  As of a particular 
date, only the latest forecast from a broker is to be considered and if that 
forecast is excluded then the estimate should not be included in the consensus, 
even if the previous forecast was not excluded. ·         Additionally, why would there ever be two different forecasts, from 
the same broker, with the same activation, review, and announce date? We’ve seen 
some examples of this. In cases like that, which one do we count? We allow a broker to provide more than one forecast per day for the same 
ticker, measure, periodicity and fiscal period.  The timestamps in the original 
IBES files should be different for forecasts which have the same activation, 
review and announce dates.  As part of the end of day consensus, the forecast

the above scenario, normally more than one analyst will be listed in the report,

analyst, usually the one that is seen above the other analyst.  Consensus data 
is based on the latest estimate from the broker, no matter who the analyst 
is. When a report contains the same forecast as before, the review date gets 
updated; the estimate and the estimate activation date does not change.  
However, if a forecast is stopped due to discontinuation from the broker and 
then the coverage starts again with the same forecast, the forecast will be

page_923.body_text: ​From: Nora Sawyer To: #Library Date: 8/19/2022 ________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ I just ran across some interesting information that was news to me: Apparently, Factiva distinguishes how company tags are applied. By default, the code searches for "aboutness" (that is, articles about the company tagged). However, you can also run a search for "occurrence" using the company tag. So for example, you could find articles that mention Apple by searching for fds:occur=APPLC. They do filter out hits that don't meet their relevance criteria, so the search won't pick up all passing mentions of the company, but it will capture more than the normal  fds=APPLC search. Here's more information on how it works: https://customer.factiva.com/learning/db50769b-a61d-45c8-822f-57d3ebf857f7?pos=11&page=1 Nora Sawyer Information Specialist Extension 8282 My pronouns: She/Her/Hers This week's poem: Don't You Wonder, Sometimes? By Tracy K. Smith
paragraphs: I just ran across some interesting information that was news to me:

Apparently, Factiva distinguishes how company tags are applied. By default, the code searches for "aboutness" (that is, articles about the company tagged). However, you can also run a search for "occurrence" using the company tag. So for example, you could find articles that mention Apple by searching for fds:occur=APPLC. They do filter out hits that don't meet their relevance criteria, so the search won't pick up all passing mentions of the company, but it will capture more than the normal  fds=APPLC search.
Here's more information on how it works:https://customer.factiva.com/learning/db50769b-a61d-45c8-822f-57d3ebf857f7?pos=11&page=1

page_933.body_text: Use the Enterprise Wiki to create a single, go-to place for knowledge sharing and project management across the enterprise. Enterprise Wikis are simple to use, flexible, and lightweight in features. They are quick and easy to create, and you can easily add links to other information systems, corporate directories, or applications. By using an Enterprise Wiki, you can avoid email overload, provide structure to new and existing information, and encourage collaboration. This helps build consensus among team members. Working with content - text, graphics or video - is as easy as working in any word processing application, such as Microsoft Word. Use the Rich Text Editor to enhance the formatting of content, apply styles to text, reorganize or spell check your content, insert and format tables, and embed graphics or video. You can do all these things without leaving the wiki page. Other things you can do when working with Enterprise Wikis: Collaborate on wiki pages with other users Comment on a wiki page to enable discussion about the contents of the page Rate a wiki page to share your opinion about its content Categorize wiki pages to enable users to quickly find information and share it with others

page_945.body_text: ​ UK/EU Soures for Case, Regulatory Proceedings and Arbitration General Litigation Bloomberg Law News Bloomberg Law has an excellent staff of journalists in the UK and EU and they often report on cases or arbitrations as they get filed.  We do not know how they find out since the courts are not public in any way, but they do find out.  They will often list the law firms and sometimes the attorneys involved.  Also if you contact them, they are generally responsive and will send you what they can.  Sometimes that is the complaint, and sometimes it is just more detail than they published in the article. We have the ability to search for litigation cases in the  UK two ways using Bloomberg:  News Alerts and Case Alerts.  Once you’ve identified a case that you’d like to track, we can set up a track and request documents as they become available.   You can set up a track on EU cases but the information  comes from CURIA (see below) and there is little information available. Very few ocuments are available for EU cases. CURIA - The Court of Justice for the European Union You can searh by court, case number or parties and by date. There is case information and a separate tab for documents. https://curia.europa.eu/jcms/jcms/j_6/en/ Lawtel (not currently subscribed) Lawtel is an online tool providing up to date case law, legislation and journal coverage. It also provides extensive coverage of EU law – both the ECJ and EU Commission are subscribers. We provide legally guaranteed primary law to practitioners working under the jurisdiction of UK, EU and International law.  Lawtel’s brochure is here: \\CRNYFS2\Admin\London Working Group\IR Resources\Lawtel\Lawtel - Core Brochure.pdf The Pending Actions service from Lawtel enables users to search and track an action from when it has been acknowledged through to judgment, showing how proceedings develop leading up to hearing, meaning you will be the first to know about cases at the earliest possible stage. The service covers cases commenced in the Queen’s Bench Division (excluding the Administrative Court), the Commercial Court and Chancery Division (excluding the Bankruptcy Court) from January 2010. The database will inform users of the main issues pertaining to the case along with the case progress and final judgment. Once proceedings have been commenced and a Claim Form has been filed, we will add basic information relating to the case (Party names, Court, Case number, Date filed). For selected cases, once (and if) the Particulars of Claim is available, we will add additional information, such as subjects, keywords, a summary of the case and legal representation (if available). Example pending action \\CRNYFS2\Admin\London Working Group\IR Resources\Lawtel\Example Pending Action from Lawtel - Banking and Finance 6-2015.rtf IR Notes:  Generally a few weeks behind Bloomberg. Competition/Antitrust MLEX Mlex is an antitrust news and case and regulation tracking service called MLex, specifically the module MLex EU within this service.  MLex EU tracks antitrust litigation in the EU and UK and publishes articles and commentary on the litigation both as the case is developing and after it is over.  They also follow and publish articles about regulations and potential regulations pertaining to antitrust issues.  You can set up alerts for types of cases, courts, industries, etc. as well as save searches that you do. PaRR PaRR is a daily, global news service devoted to antitrust/competition law. Our global team of investigative journalists report on all aspects of antitrust/competition law including merger review, enforcement actions, intellectual property and litigations. PaRR's team of reporters, analysts and translators are based around the world in Asia, Europe and the Americas. In addition to our news offerings, subscribers also have access to our Global Case Database and M&A Timetable. The Global Case Database contains competition cases from 2010-present from Europe, the US, Brazil, India and China. The M&A Timetable contains merger review filing timetable information for deals between large, publicly traded companies over the past ten years. GCR GCR provides online competition news that can be delivered to you daily if you wish.  This includes: facts on significant deals and developments, promotions and departures, news and analysis on competition enforcement agencies, a searchable archive comprising thousands of stories published since December 1997. If you are interested in accessing this publication, simply go to: http://www.globalcompetitionreview.com and use our Username: corner and Password: stone to log in.  If you would like to start receiving the daily email you can go here: http://www.globalcompetitionreview.com/briefing/ and enter your email. European Commission Competition Cases Source of EC Competition Case Decisions - covers Antitrust, Cartel, Merger and State Aid Cases:- Link to Search page. Law360: International Trade (section) The international trade section covers litigation, regulation and legislation related to exports and imports. The section tracks trade and tariff disputes, customs controls and policy developments, with a focus on proceedings at the Court of International Trade, the International Trade Commission and the World Trade Organization.  To access: https://www.law360.com/internationaltrade . International Arbitration TDM OGEMID’s Transnational Dispute Management (TDM) journal.  “TDM is a peer-review online journal publishing about various aspects of international arbitration with a special focus on investment arbitration. Since the first issue was published in 2004 it has gained popularity among a large number of law firms, academics and other professionals in the field of arbitration.”  Included is automatic membership to OGEMIND.  You can find out more about the organization and TDM here: http://www.transnational-dispute-management.com/ogemid/ . You can view material ahead of its appearance in a regular structured issues of the Journal by going to the “Advance Publication” tab on the home page.  You can also sign up for alerts and monitor the RSS feed for advance publication http://www.transnational-dispute-management.com/rss/advance.xml . Here is a email alert of Advance Publications from TDM: \\CRNYFS2\Admin\London Working Group\IR Resources\TDM update alert.msg GAR GAR reports on arbitration cases, deals and community news in the United States, North America and globally. The benefits of a Premium GAR subscription are: Keep up to date Deal and case news : Legal and policy developments Community news : Departures, promotions and mergers Understand the market Surveys, league tables and country profiles High-profile interviews, commentary , and roundtable discussions Strategy and firm management In-depth reporting from GAR Live and other arbitration community events Identify your competitors GAR100 : A guide to the world's leading arbitration practices Know your arbitration centre The Guide to Regional Arbitration: ‘Whitelists’ and directories of arbitral providers nested in particular regions, explaining which are already worth using and which are ones to watch Strengthen your knowledge Special reports : Insight submitted by experts from leading firms worldwide, with a focus on the hot topics of the moment GAR Know-How : An interactive resource providing quick-and-easy comparisons of current arbitration process and procedure across multiple jurisdictions Get the background story Access to the archive covering over 8 years of historical news and analysis Law360: International Arbitration (search only) There is not a specific section on this, however it does exist as a practice area in the advanced search feature.  Thus we can create a search that provides the type of articles we want and then set it as an alert so that it will push out a “newsletter” to whoever wants to see it.

If you have trouble finding a corporate website for a company type Corporate or Corporate Website after the company name.
